मांश्चतु: मांश्चतु मांश्चतु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. (probably some colour), light yellow, dun-coloured (an epithet of Mitra or of a horse or horses; according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda VII. 44, 3, = मन्यमानान् स्तुवतो जनांश् चेतयते जानाति यद्वा अभिमन्यमानांश् चातयते नाशयति यः, one who is mindful of his adorers, or destroying those that despise him; ac-cording to Naigh. 1. 14, मांश्चत्वः = अश्वाः).
मांश्चत्व: मांश्चत्व, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. yellowish, (this word occurs with doubtful meaning in Ṛg-veda IX. 97, 4.)
मांस्: मांस् मांस्, n. = मांस, flesh, meat, &c. (see below; मांस् is defective in nom. and acc. sing. and du., the inst. is मांसा, acc. pl. मांसि, inst. dat. abl. du. मान्भ्याम्, &c.). —मांस्-पचन, अस्, ई, अम्, Ved. used for cooking meat (said of a caldron). —मांस्-पाक, अस्, m. = मांस-पाक, q. v. (Pāṇ. VI. 1, 144).
मांस: मांस, अम्, n. (said to be fr. rt. मन्; a fanciful derivation fr. मां स is given in Manu V. 55), flesh, meat, animal food, (according to some also अस्, m.); the flesh of fish; the fleshy part or pulp of fruit; (अस्), m., N. of a mixed caste (= मांस-विक्रेतृ, selling meat; cf. मांस-च्छेद); a worm; time; (ई), f. = जटा-मांसी, Nardostachys Jatamansi; a sort of drug; = मांस-च्छदा; [cf. Old Germ. môs, ‘food;’ Mod. Germ. Mus, Gemüse; Slav. manso; Lith. mēsa; Hib. maise, ‘food, victuals.’] —मांस-कच्छप, अस्, m. a fleshy abscess on the palate. —मांस-कन्दी, f. a fleshy protuberance or swelling of the flesh. —मांस-काम, अस्, आ, अम्, fond of meat or flesh. —मांस-कारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, flesh-making, flesh-preparing; (ई), n. blood. —मांस-खण्ड, अस्, अम्, m. n. a bit of flesh or meat. —मांस-ग्रन्थि, इस्, m. flesh-swelling, a gland. —मांस-च्छदा, f. a species of plant. —मांस-च्छेद, अस्, ई, m. f. or मांस-च्छेदिन्, ई, m. ‘flesh-cutter,’ N. of a mixed caste. —मांस-ज, अम्, n. ‘flesh-born,’ the marrow of the flesh, adeps, fat. —मांस-तान, अस्, m. a polypus in the throat. —मांस-तेजस्, अस्, n. ‘flesh-marrow,’ fat, adeps; [cf. मांस-ज।] —मांस-त्व, अम्, n. fleshiness, the being flesh; the derivation of the word मांस (Manu V. 55). —मांस-दग्ध, अम्, n. cauterizing of the flesh. —मांस-दलन, अस्, m. a plant, Amoora Rohitaka. —मांस-द्राविन्, ई, m. a species of sorrel, Rumex Vesicarius. —मांस-निर्यास, अस्, m. the hair of the body. —मांसन्-वत्, आन्, अती, अत् (fr. Ved. मांसन्), fleshy. —मांस-प, अस्, m. ‘flesh-sucker,’ epithet of a Piśāca; of a Dānava. —मांस-पचन, अस्, ई, अम्, meat-cook-ing; (अम्), n. a vessel for cooking meat. —मांस-परिवर्जन, अम्, n. avoiding meat, abstaining from animal food. —मांस-परिविक्रयिन्, ई, m. a flesh-monger, dealer in flesh. —मांस-पाक, अस्, m. a kind of disease (destroying the mem-brum virile). —मांस-पिटक, अस्, अम्, m. n. a basket of meat, a large quantity of flesh or meat. —मांस-पिण्ड-गृहीत-वदन, अस्, आ, अम्, car-rying a piece of flesh in the mouth. —मांस-पित्त, अम्, n. a bone. —मांस-पेशी, f. a piece of flesh; an epithet of the fetus from the eighth till the four-teenth day [cf. पेशी]; a muscle. —मांस-फला, f. the egg-plant, Solanum Melongena. —मांस-भक्ष, अस्, आ, अम्, or मांस-भक्षक, अस्, इका, अम्, flesh-eating, carnivorous, eating meat; (अस्), m., N. of a Dānava. —मांस-भक्षण, अम्, n. the act of eating meat, eating animal food. —मांस-भिक्षा, f., Ved. begging for meat as alms, soliciting flesh as alms. —मांस-भुज्, क्, क्, क्, flesh-eating, eating meat. —मांस-भूतोदन (°त-ओद्°), अम्, n. ‘boiled rice mixed with meat,’ rice and meat. —मांस-भेत्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ, flesh-cutting, inflict-ing a flesh-wound, piercing the flesh. —मांस-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, consisting of flesh; मांस-मयी पेशी, a piece of flesh. —मांस-मासा, f. a species of plant, = माष-पर्णी; (also read मांस-माषा।) —मांस-मुख, अस्, ई, अम्, having flesh in the mouth. —मांस-यूथ, अम्, n. a quantity of flesh. —मांस-योनि, इस्, इस्, इ, flesh-born; (इस्), m. a creature of flesh and blood. —मांस-रस, अस्, m. meat-broth, soup. —मांस-रुचि, इस्, इस्, इ, fond of flesh, having a relish for animal food. —मांस-रोहिणी or मांस-रोही, f. a species of fragrant plant. —मांस-लता, f. ‘flesh-tendril,’ a wrinkle. —मांस-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having or possessing flesh. —मांस-विक्रय, अस्, m. the sale of meat. —मांस-विक्र-यिन्, ई, इणी, इ, or मांस-विक्रेतृ, ता, त्री, तृ, selling meat, a meat-seller; (मांस-विक्रयिन् is used as a term of reproach for a low or vile person.) —मांस-वृद्धि, इस्, f. an increase or growth of flesh. —मांस-शील, अस्, आ, अम्, accustomed to eat meat; fleshy. —मांस-शोणित, अम्, n. flesh and blood. —मांस-शोणित-पङ्किन्, ई, इनी, इ, miry with flesh and blood. —मांस-सङ्घात, अस्, m. a swelling of the flesh. —मांस-सार, अस्, m. ‘flesh-essence, flesh-marrow,’ fat; (अस्, आ, अम्), having the flesh predo-minant among the seven constituent parts of the body. —मांस-स्नेह, अस्, m. ‘flesh-marrow,’ adeps, fat. —मांस-हासा, f. skin. —मांसाद् (°स-अद्), त्, त्, त्, or मांसाद (°स-अद or -आद), अस्, आ, अम्, or मांसादिन् (°स-आद्°), ई, इनी, इ, flesh-eating, car-nivorous. —मांसार्गल (°स-अर्°), अस्, अम्, m. n. a piece of flesh hanging from the mouth (of a lion &c.). —मांसार्बुद (°स-अर्°), अस्, m. a kind of disease of the membrum virile. —मांसाशन (°स-अश्°), अम्, n. flesh-meat; the act of eating flesh-meat. —मांसाशि-त्व, अम्, n. the state of one who eats flesh, the devouring of flesh. —मांसाशिन् (°स-आश्°), ई, इनी, इ, eating flesh, living upon meat. —मांसाष्टका (°स-अष्°), f., N. of the eighth day in the dark half of the month Māgha (on which meat is offered to the Manes). —मांसाहार (°स-आह्°), अस्, m. animal food. —मांसएष्टा (°स-इष्°), f. a kind of bird, the flesh of which is considered a delicacy (= वल्गुला). —मांसोन्नति (°स-उन्°), इस्, f. a swelling of the flesh. —मांसोपजीविन् (°स-उप्°), ई, m. living by flesh, a dealer in meat. —मां-सौदन (°स-ओद्°), अस्, m. meat and boiled rice. —मांसौदनिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. the preceding), see Pāṇ. IV. 4, 67.
मांसल: मांसल, अस्, आ, अम्, fleshy; lusty, brawny, mus-cular; powerful, strong (sometimes applied to sound); pulpy (as fruit). —मांसल-फला, f. Solanum Me-longena; [cf. मांस-फला।]
मांसिक: मांसिक, अस्, आ, अम्, = मांसाय प्रभवति, see Gaṇa Santāpādi to Pāṇ. V. 1, 101; (अस्), m. a butcher, a seller of meat.
मांसिका: मांसिका, f. (fr. मांसी), the plant Nardostachys Jatamansi.
मांसीय: मांसीय, Nom. P. मांसीयति, &c., Ved. to long for flesh.
मांस्पृष्ट: मांस्पृष्ट मां-स्पृष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved., ac-cording to a Schol. a comp. fr. माम् + स्पृष्ट।
माकन्द: माकन्द माकन्द, अस्, m. the mango tree; (ई), f. the Myrobalan tree, Myrobalan; N. of other plants (= Hindī माद्राणी, माकुनी); yellow sandal-wood, yellow sanders; N. of a city on the Ganges.
माकन्दक: माकन्दक, अस्, इका, अम्, belonging to the town Mākandī; (इका), f. = माकन्दी, the city.
माकन्दिक: माकन्दिक, अस्, m., N. of a man.
माकर: माकर माकर, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मकर), related or belonging to the sea-monster Makara; माकर आकर, ‘the mine of Makaras,’ the sea; माकरम् आसनम्, a particular posture in sitting; माकरो व्यूहः, a particular form of military array; माकरी सप्तमी = मकर-सप्तमी, the seventh day in the light half of the month Māgha.
माकरन्द: माकरन्द माकरन्द, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मक-रन्द), coming from or consisting of the juice of flowers.
माकलि: माकलि माकलि, इस्, m. the moon; N. of Indra's charioteer; [cf. मातलि।]
माकारध्यान: माकारध्यान माकार-ध्यान, अम्, n. (pro-bably fr. I. मा + कार), a particular method of ab-stract meditation, kind of reverie.
माकिम्: माकिम् मा-किम्, see Gaṇa Cādi to Pāṇ. 1. 4, 57; [cf. न-किम्।]
माकिस्: मा-किस्, ind., Ved. not (= Lat. ne, e. g. Ṛg-veda 1. 147, 5, मा-किर् no दुरिताय धायीः, consign us not to misfortune); no one (= Lat. ne-quis, e. g. Ṛg-veda VIII. 5, 39, मा-किर् एना पथा गात्, let none proceed by that path; according to Sāy. अनेन मार्गेण अन्यो न गन्तुं शक्नोति).
माकीम्: मा-कीम्, ind., see Gaṇa Cādi to Pāṇ. 1. 4, 57, (according to Sāy.) = १। मा; [cf. न-कीम्।]
माकी: माकी माकी, f. du., Ved. (Sāy.) = निर्मा-त्र्यौ भूत-जातस्य, the two creators or originators of all beings, (said of heaven and earth.)
माकीन: माकीन माकीन, अस्, आ, अम्, (fr. 3. म), Ved. (according to Sāy.) my, mine.
माकुलि: माकुलि माकुलि, इस्, m. a kind of snake.
माकोट: माकोट माकोट, N. of one of the places in which Dākṣāyaṇī is worshipped.
माक्षव्य: माक्षव्य माक्षव्य, अस्, m. (fr. मक्षु), Ved. a patronymic, N. of a preceptor; [cf. मां-क्षव्य।]
माक्षिक: माक्षिक माक्षिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मक्षिका), coming from or belonging to a bee; (अम्), n., scil. मधु, honey; a kind of honey-like mineral sub-stance or pyrites, (various kinds are described, see स्वर्ण-म्°, रूप्य-म्°, कांस्य-म्°, विट्-म्°); [cf. Old Germ. wahs, ‘wax;’ Angl. Sax. väx, vex, veax; Lith. waszka-s; Russ. vosk.] —माक्षिक-ज, अम्, n. ‘honey-born,’ bees’-wax. —माक्षिक-फल, अस्, m. a species of cocoa-nut (= मधु-नालिकेरिक)। —माक्षिक-शर्करा, f. a kind of sugar, candied sugar. —माक्षिक-स्वामिन्, ई, m., N. of a place. —माक्षिकाश्रय (°क-आश्°), अम्, n. bees'-wax; honey-comb.
माक्षीक: माक्षीक, अम्, n. = माक्षिक, honey. —मा-क्षीक-धातु, उ, n. a kind of pyrites (described above). —माक्षिक-शर्करा, f. clarified sugar (= सिताखण्ड).
माख: माख माख, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मख), of or belonging to a sacrifice, sacrificial.
मागद्य: मागद्य मागद्य, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. मगदिन्), see Gaṇa Pragadyādi to Pāṇ. IV. 2, 80.
मागध: मागध मागध, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मगध), relating to or born in or living in or customary among the Magadhas or the Magadha country; मागधी भाषा, the Magadha language; (अस्), m. a king of the Magadhas; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people, the Magadhas; opprobrious epithet of a mixed caste (still numerous in Guzerat, and called the Bhāts), the son of a Kṣatriya mother and Vaiśya father, the poetical panegyrist of a king, a bard, minstrel (whose duty is to recite the praises of kings in their presence with allusions to their genealogy and the deeds of their ancestors, or to attend the march of an army and animate the soldiers by martial songs; frequently associated with सूत and वन्दिन्); N. of one of the seven sages in the fourteenth Manv-antara; of a son of Yadu; white cummin; (आस्), m. pl., N. of the warrior-caste in Śākya-dvīpa; (आ), f. a princess of the Magadhas; long pepper; (ई), f. a princess of the Magadhas; the daughter of a Kṣatriya mother and Vaiśya father; the language of the Magadhas; N. of a river (= शोणा); Jasminum Auriculatum; long pepper; white cummin; anise or dill; a species of cardamoms (grown in Guzerat); refined sugar; a kind of metre (Ved.). —मागध-देशीय, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging to or born in the land of the Ma-gadhas. —मागध-पुर, अम्, n. ‘the city of the Magadhas,’ N. of a city.
मागधक: मागधक, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people; (इका), f. long pepper.
मागधिक: मागधिक, अस्, m. a prince of the Magadhas.
माघ: माघ माघ, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मघा), related to the constellation Maghā; (अस्), m., scil. मास, the month Māgha which begins with the winter solstice (= January-February); N. of a poet (son of Dattaka and author of the Śiśupāla-vadha or Māgha-kāvya); (ई), f., scil. तिथि, the day of full moon in the month Māgha; Hingtsha Repens. —माघ-काव्य, अम्, n. the poem of Māgha, i. e. the Śiśu-pāla-vadha. —माघ-चैतन्य, अस्, m., N. of the author of the eighth book of the Kalpa-latā. —माघ-पाक्षिक, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging to one of the two halves of the month Māgha. —माघ-माहात्म्य, अम्, n. ‘the majesty of the month Māgha,’ N. of a part of the Padma-Purāṇa. —माघ-स्नान, अम्, n. bathing or religious ablution in sacred pools &c. in the month of Māgha. —माघी-पक्ष-यजनीय, अम्, n. the first day of the month Phālguna; [cf. यजनीय।]
माघ्य: माघ्य, अम्, n. the flower of the Jasminum Multiflorum or Pubescens.
माघमा: माघमा माघमा, f. a female crab (= कर्-कटी).
माघवत: माघवत माघवत, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मघ-वत्), belonging to Indra; (ई), f., scil. दिश्, the east. —माघवत-चाप, अस्, m. the rainbow.
माघवन: माघवन, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मघ-वन्), belong-ing to Indra, ruled by Indra (Pāṇ. VI. 4, 128).
माघोन: माघोन, अम्, n. liberality (Ved.); (ई), f., scil. दिश्, the east, the eastern quarter.
माङ्क्ष्: माङ्क्ष् माङ्क्ष् (connected with rt. काङ्क्ष्), cl. I. P. माङ्क्षति, माङ्-क्षितुम्, to wish, long for, desire.
माङ्क्षव्य: माङ्क्षव्य माङ्क्षव्य, अस्, m. (fr. मङ्क्षु), a patronymic (Gaṇa Gargādi to Pāṇ. IV. 1, 105); माङ्क्षव्यायणी, f. (Gaṇa Lohitādi to Pāṇ. IV. 1, 18).
माङ्गल: माङ्गल माङ्गल, अम्, n. (fr. मङ्गल), Ved. epithet of a particular liturgical formula addressed to the Aśvins.
माङ्गलि: माङ्गलि, इस्, m. a patronymic, N. of a preceptor.
माङ्गलिक: माङ्गलिक, अस्, ई, अम्, auspicious, propitious, tending to good fortune, wishing for prosperity, in-dicating good fortune.
माङ्गलिका: माङ्गलिका, f. (fem. of an unused form माङ्ग-लक), N. of a woman.
माङ्गल्य: माङ्गल्य, अस्, आ (?) , अम्, = मङ्गल्य, conferring happiness, auspicious; (अस्), m. Ægle Marmelos; (अम्), n. an auspicious thing, amulet; a benediction; an auspicious or festive ceremony, festivity, festival; prosperity, happiness, welfare, propitiousness. —माङ्-गल्य-मृदङ्ग, अस्, m. a tabour or drum beaten on festive occasions. —माङ्गल्यार्हा (°य-अर्°), f. a species of plant (= त्रायमाणा).
माङ्गुष्य: माङ्गुष्य माङ्गुष्य, अस्, m. (fr. मङ्गुष), a patronymic (Gaṇa Kurvādi to Pāṇ. IV. 1, 151).
माच: माच माच, अस्, m. a way, road; [cf. मा-ठ, माथ।]
माचल: माचल माचल, अस्, m. (perhaps fr. 1. मा + चल), a thief, robber (= वन्दी-कार); a crocodile, &c. (= ग्राह); sickness, illness; [cf. करि-म्°, गज-म्°।]
माचाकीय: माचाकीय माचाकीय, अस्, m., N. of a gram-marian.
माचाल: माचाल माचाल in पर्ण-म्°, q. v.
माचिका: माचिका माचिका, f. = मक्षिका, a fly [cf. गृह-म्°]; a species of plant (= अम्ब-ष्ठा; cf. काक-म्°).
माची: माची in काक-म्° and ध्वाङ्क्ष-म्°; cf. मा-चिका above. —माची-पत्त्र, अम्, n. a species of medicinal plant (= सुर-पर्ण).
माजल: माजल माजल, अस्, m. a kind of bird, the blue roller.
माजलपुर: माजल-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a city.
माजिक: माजिक माजिक, अस्, m., N. of a man.
माजिरक: माजिरक माजिरक, अस्, m. (fr. मजिरक), a patronymic (Gaṇa Śivādi to Pāṇ. IV. 1, 112).
माजीज: माजीज माजीज, N. of a place; (also read माजुज and माजूज।)
माञ्जिष्ठ: माञ्जिष्ठ माञ्जिष्ठ, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मञ्जिष्-ठा), red as madder, red as the dye made from the Mañjiṣṭhā; (अम्), n. red, red colour.
माञ्जिष्ठक: माञ्जिष्ठक or माञ्जिष्ठिक, अस्, ई, अम्, red as Bengal madder, dyed with madder, red.
माञ्जीरक: माञ्जीरक माञ्जीरक, अस्, m. (fr. मञ्जीरक), a patronymic (Gaṇa Śivādi to Pāṇ. IV. 1, 112).
माटाम्रक: माटाम्रक माटाम्रक, अस्, m. a species of tree.
माटियारि: माटियारि माटियारि or माटीयारि, N. of a city.
माठ: माठ माठ or माठ्य, अस्, m. a road; [cf. माथ, माच।]
माठर: माठर माठर, अस्, m. (fr. मठर), a patronymic, a proper N.; = Vyāsa; N. of one of the sun's attendants; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people; (ई), f., N. of a woman.
माठरक: माठरक, see Gaṇa Dhūmādi to Pāṇ. IV. 2, 127.
माठरायण: माठरायण, अस्, m. a patronymic (Gaṇa Hari-tādi to Pāṇ. IV. 1, 100).
माठर्य: माठर्य, अस्, m. (fr. मठर), a patronymic, see Schol. on Uṇādi-sūtras V. 39.
माठव्य: माठव्य माठव्य, अस्, m. a proper N.
माड्: माड् माड्, cl. I. P. A. माडति, -ते, &c., to measure, weigh, (a various reading for rt. माह्।)
माड: माड, अस्, m. measure, weight, quantity; a species of tree (= मद्य-द्रुम, also read माडा-द्रुम).
माडव: माडव माडव, अस्, m. a particular mixed caste.
माडार्य: माडार्य माडार्य (fr. मडार), see Gaṇa Pragadyādi to Pāṇ. IV. 2, 80.
माडि: माडि माडि, इस्, m. a palace.
माड्डुक: माड्डुक माड्डुक or माड्डुकिक, अस्, m. (fr. मड्डुक, q. v.), a drummer, player on the Maḍḍuka.
माढि: माढि माढि, इस्, f. = दल-स्नसा, the fibre or vein of a leaf (= पत्त्र-शिरा); the germ of leaves, the young leaf before it opens; honouring, respecting, reverencing, (in this sense fr. rt. मह्); dejection, sadness, affliction; poverty, indigence, manifestation of poverty, declaration of distress; anger, passion; a back or double tooth; the hem or border of a garment; N. of a district.
माढी: माढी, f. = दन्त-शिरा, a back or double tooth.
माण: माण माण, अस्, m. a species of plant (= माणक).
माणक: माणक, अस्, m. a small shrub, Arum Indicum; the bulbous root of the Arum Indicum; [cf. मा-नक।]
माणव: माणव माणव, अस्, m. a youth, lad, young-ster, (especially) a young Brāhman; a man, little man, manikin (used contemptuously); a pearl orna-ment of sixteen strings [cf. अर्ध-म्°]; epithet of one of the nine treasures of the Jainas.
माणवक: माणवक, अस्, m. a lad or boy not exceeding sixteen years of age; a little man, dwarf, (माया-माणवको हरिः, Viṣṇu disguising himself under the form of a dwarf); a manikin (contemptuously); a silly or childish man, an ignorant or ridiculous man, (in the drama used as an epithet of the Vidū-shaka or jocose friend of the king); a pupil, scholar, religious student; a pearl ornament of a particular number of strings (e. g. of sixteen, twenty, or forty-eight strings); (इका), f. a young girl, damsel, wench; (अम्), n. = माणवक-क्रीड, a kind of metre, four times ¯ ˘ ˘ ¯ ¯ ˘ ˘ ¯. —माणवक-क्रीड, अम्, आ, n. f. ‘boy's play,’ N. of a kind of metre. —माण-वक-क्रीडनक or माणवक-क्रीडितक, अम्, n. = माणवक-क्रीड।
माणवीन: माणवीन, अस्, आ, अम्, proper for boys or lads, boyish, childish.
माणव्य: माणव्य, अम्, n. a multitude or company of boys or lads, boyhood.
माणहल: माणहल माणहल, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people.
माणिका: माणिका माणिका, f. a particular weight, = 2 Kuḍavas, = 1 Śarāva, = 8 Palas.
माणिकाम्बू: माणिकाम्बू माणिकाम्बू, ऊस्, f., N. of a woman, the mother of the Scholiast Viṭṭhala.
माणिक्य: माणिक्य माणिक्य, अम्, n. a ruby [cf. रङ्ग-म्°]; (अस्), m., N. of a man; (आ), f. a kind of small house-lizard. —माणिक्य-चन्द्र, अस्, m., N. of a king of Tīra-bhukti. —माणिक्य-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, made or consisting of rubies. —माणिक्य-मल्ल, अस्, m., N. of a king (patron of Manohara-śarman the commentator on the Śruta-bodha). —माणिक्य-मिश्र, अस्, m. a proper N. —माणिक्य-राय, अस्, m. a proper N. —माणिक्य-सूरि, इस्, m., N. of a Gujarāṭhī author and of other persons.
माणिचर: माणिचर माणिचर, अस्, m., Ved. (accord-ing to a commentator) the tutelary genius of the war-chariot.
माणिपार: माणिपार माणिपार, अस्, m. a proper N.
माणिपाल: माणिपाल माणिपाल, see Gaṇa Mahiṣyādi to Pāṇ. IV. 4, 148.
माणिपालिक: माणिपालिक, see Gaṇa Revatyādi to Pāṇ. IV. 1, 146.
माणिबन्ध: माणिबन्ध माणिबन्ध, अम्, n. = माणि-मन्थ, q. v.
माणिभद्र: माणिभद्र माणिभद्र = मणि-भद्र, a king of the Yakṣas.
माणिमन्थ: माणिमन्थ माणिमन्थ, अम्, n. (fr. मणि-मन्थ), salt brought from the mountain Maṇi-mantha, rock-salt, sea-salt.
माणिरूप्यक: माणिरूप्यक माणिरूप्यक (fr. मणि + रूप्य), see Pāṇ. IV. 2, 104.
माण्टि: माण्टि माण्टि, इस्, m., Ved., N. of a teacher; (अयस्), m. pl., N. of his descendants; [cf. मण्टि, मेण्ठ।]
माण्ड: माण्ड माण्ड, अस्, m., N. of a man.
माण्डकर्णि: माण्डकर्णि माण्डकर्णि, इस्, m. (a patro-nymic fr. मण्ड-कर्ण), N. of a Muni.
माण्डप: माण्डप माण्डप, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मण्डप), belonging to a temple.
माण्डरिक: माण्डरिक माण्डरिक (fr. मण्डर), see Gaṇa Aṅgulyādi to Pāṇ. V. 3, 108.
माण्डलिक: माण्डलिक माण्डलिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मण्-डल), relating to a province, ruling a province; (अस्), m. the governor of a province.
माण्डव: माण्डव माण्डव, अम्, n. (fr. मण्डु), N. of a Sāman; एडम् माण्डवम्, N. of a Sāman.
माण्डवी: माण्डवी, f. (fr. माण्डव्य below), N. of a daughter of Kuśa-dhvaja and wife of Bharata; a N. of Dākṣāyaṇī at Māṇḍavya.
माण्डव्य: माण्डव्य, अस्, m. (fr. मण्डु), a patronymic, N. of a teacher; (आस्), m. pl. the descendants of Māṇḍavya; N. of a people; (अस्, अम्), m. or n. (?), N. of a place. —माण्डव्य-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a city on the Godā. —माण्डव्येश्वर (°य-ईश्°), अम्, n., N. of a Liṅga. —माण्डव्येश्वर-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a place of pilgrimage.
माण्डव्यायन: माण्डव्यायन, अस्, ई, m. f. (fr. माण्डव्य), a patronymic (Gaṇa Lohitādi to Pāṇ. IV. 1, 18).
माण्डूक: माण्डूक माण्डूक, आस्, m. pl. (fr. मण्डूक), N. of a school. —माण्डूकी-पुत्र, अस्, m., N. of a teacher.
माण्डूकायन: माण्डूकायन, आस्, m. pl., N. of a school. —माण्-डूकायनी-पुत्र, अस्, m., N. of a teacher.
माण्डूकायनि: माण्डूकायनि, इस्, m., Ved., N. of a preceptor.
माण्डूकि: माण्डूकि, इस्, m. (fr. मण्डूक), a patronymic (Pāṇ. IV. 1, 119).
माण्डूकेय: माण्डूकेय, अस्, m. (fr. मण्डूक), a patronymic, N. of a teacher; (आस्), m. pl. his descendants; (अम्), n. the doctrine or teaching of Māṇḍūkeya.
माण्डूकेयीय: माण्डूकेयीय, relating to or connected with Māṇ-ḍūkeya.
माण्डूक्य: माण्डूक्य, probably an adj. from माण्डूक। —माण्डूक्य-श्रुति, इस्, f. the Māṇḍukya revela-tion or teaching. —माण्डूक्योपनिषद् (°य-उप्°), त्, f., N. of a short but important Upaniṣad of the Atharva-veda.
मातङ्ग: मातङ्ग मातङ्ग, अस्, m. (fr. मतङ्ग), an elephant; any large animal like an elephant; (at the end of comps.) anything the best of its kind (e. g. वलाहक-मातङ्गास्, ‘elephants of clouds,’ i. e. ‘best of clouds,’ an epithet of the Saṃvartaka clouds; cf. मातङ्ग-नक्र below); Ficus Religiosa; epithet of the twenty-fourth astronomical Yoga; a Cāṇḍāla, a man of the lowest rank, an outcast; a kind of Kirāta mountaineer, barbarian; N. of the servant of the seventh and of the twenty-fourth Arhat of the present Ava-sarpiṇī; of a Pratyeka-buddha; of an author; of a Nāga; (ई), f., N. of a mythical being regarded as progenitress of the whole elephant tribe; of a form of Durgā; of the wife of Vasiṣṭha. —मातङ्ग-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, coming from or belong-ing to an elephant, elephantine. —मातङ्ग-दिवा-कर, अस्, m., N. of a poet. —मातङ्ग-नक्र, अस्, m. a crocodile as large as an elephant. —मा-तङ्ग-मकर, अस्, m. a kind of marine monster. —मातङ्ग-सूत्र, अम्, n., N. of a Buddhist Sūtra. —मातङ्गोत्सङ्ग (°ग-उत्°), अस्, m. the back of an elephant.
मातरिश्व: मातरिश्व मातरि-श्व, मातरि-श्वन्। See p. 765, col. 1.
मातलि: मातलि मातलि, इस्, m., N. of Indra's charioteer, (said to be also read मातुलि।) —मातलि-सारथि, इस्, m. ‘having Mātali for his charioteer,’ an epithet of Indra.
मातलीय: मातलीय, अस्, आ, अम्, relating to or concerning Mātali.
मातली: मातली मातली, ई, m. (only found in the nom. sing. and without any case-ending, cf. पृथी), Ved., N. of a divine being associated with Yama and the Manes.
मातवचस: मातवचस मातवचस, अस्, m., Ved. a patro-nymic from Mata-vacas.
मातापितृ: मातापितृ माता-पितृ, माता-मह, &c. See p. 765, col. 1.
मातुलङ्ग: मातुलङ्ग मातुलङ्ग or मातुलिङ्ग or मा-तुलुङ्ग, अस्, m. (the original form is probably मा-तुलुङ्ग), a citron tree; (आ or ई), f. another species of citron tree, sweet lime; (अम्), n. a citron; (ac-cording to a commentator मातुलङ्ग = रुद्धक, perhaps for रुचक।) —मातुलुङ्ग-फल, अम्, n. the fruit of the above tree. —मातुलुङ्ग-रस, अस्, m. the juice of the above tree. —मातुलुङ्गासव (°ग-आस्°), अस्, m. a liquor distilled from the above tree.
मातुलुङ्गक: मातुलुङ्गक, अस्, m. = मातुलुङ्ग; (इका), f. the wild citron tree.
मात्सर: मात्सर मात्सर, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मत्सर), selfish, envious, jealous, stupid.
मात्सरिक: मात्सरिक, अस्, ई, अम्, envious, jealous, spiteful, malicious; showing envy or jealousy, &c.
मात्सर्य: मात्सर्य, अम्, n. envy, jealousy, malice, spite, (मात्सर्यं कृ, to show jealousy); displeasure, dissatisfaction.
मात्स्य: मात्स्य मात्स्य, अस्, -सी (?) , अम् (fr. मत्स्य), fishy, coming from or belonging to a fish, fish-like (e. g. मात्स्यं रूपम्, a fish-like form, the form or shape of a fish); (अस्), m., N. of a king of the Matsyas; of a Ṛṣi. —मात्स्य-पुराण, अम्, n. = मत्स्य-पुराण, q. v.
मात्स्यक: मात्स्यक, अस्, ई, अम्, = मात्स्य, fishy, relating to a fish; [cf. पौण्ड्र-म्°; cf. also Hib. measach, ‘fishy.’]
मात्स्यगन्ध: मात्स्यगन्ध, आस्, m. pl. (fr. मत्स्य-गन्ध), N. of a race.
मात्स्यिक: मात्स्यिक, अस्, m. a fisherman; (wrongly read मात्सिक।)
मात्स्येय: मात्स्येय, आस्, m. pl. the Matsya people.
माथ: माथ माथ, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 1. मथ्), churn-ing, stirring; hurting, injuring, killing, destruction, annihilation; a way, road; [cf. माठ।]
माथव: माथव माथव, अस्, m., Ved. a patronymic; [cf. माधव।]
माथितिक: माथितिक माथितिक, an adj. fr. मथित by Pāṇ. V. 3, 83, Vārttika 7.
माथुर: माथुर माथुर, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मथुर), coming from or belonging to Mathurā, an inhabitant of Mathurā; composed by Mathura, related to Ma-thura; composed by Mathura-nātha (e. g. माथुरी टिप्पनी, the commentary of Mathura-nātha); (अस्), m., N. of a son of Citra-gupta and of other persons; (अम्), n. the gate leading to Mathurā. —माथुर-देश्य, अस्, आ, अम्, coming from or belonging to the country of Mathurā.
माथुरक: माथुरक, आस्, m. pl. the inhabitants of Ma-thurā.
माद: माद माद, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 2. मद्), = मद, drunkenness, intoxication, stupor; joy, delight, exhi-laration; pride, passion. —मादानन्द (°द-आन्°), अस्, m. a proper N.
मादक: मादक, अस्, इका, अम् (fr. Caus. of rt. 2. मद्), intoxicating, causing intoxication, stupefying; exhi-larating, gladdening; (अस्), m. a gallinule (= दा-त्यूह). —मादक-त्व, अम्, n. the property or state of causing intoxication.
मादन: मादन, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. Caus. of rt. 2. मद्), intoxicating, stupefying, maddening; gladdening, exhilarating; (अस्), m. the god of love; Vanguiera Spinosa; the thorn-apple; (ई), f., N. of two plants, = माकन्दी, = विजया; (अम्), n. the act of intoxi-cating, intoxication, inebriation; exhilaration, the act of delighting; cloves; ‘the stupefier,’ epithet of a mythical weapon, (in this sense also read मदन।)
मादनीय: मादनीय, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. मादन above), intoxi-cating, inebriating; (अम्), n. an intoxicating drink.
मादयित्नु: मादयित्नु or मादयिष्णु, उस्, उस्, उ (fr. Caus. of rt. 2. मद्), Ved. intoxicating, inebriating; glad-dening.
मादायन: मादायन, अस्, m. (fr. मद), a patronymic.
मादिन्: मादिन्, ई, इनी, इ (fr. Caus. of rt. 2. मद्), intoxicat-ing, stupefying; gladdening; [cf. गन्ध-म्°।]
मादुघ: मादुघ मादुघ, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to the plant called Madugha.
मादुर्णा: मादुर्णा मादुर्णा, f., N. of a village.
मादृश्: मादृश् मादृश्, क्, क्, क् (fr. 3. म + 2. दृश्), like me, resembling me.
मादृक्ष: मादृक्ष, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. 3. म + दृक्ष), = मादृश below.
मादृश: मादृश, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. 3. म + दृश), like me, resembling me.
माद्य: माद्य माद्य, incorrectly for मान्द्य, q. v.
माद्रक: माद्रक माद्रक, अस्, m. (fr. मद्र), a prince of the Madras; (इका), f. a woman belonging to the Madra nation, (more properly मद्रिका।)
माद्रकूलक: माद्रकूलक (fr. मद्र-कूल), see Gaṇa Dhū-mādi to Pāṇ. IV. 2, 127.
माद्रनगर: माद्र-नगर (fr. मद्र-नगर), see Scholiast on Pāṇ. VII. 3, 24.
माद्रवती: माद्रवती, f. ‘princess of the Madras,’ N. of the wife of Pari-kṣit; Mādrī the second wife of Pāṇḍu. —माद्रवती-सुत, अस्, m. ‘son of the Madra princess,’ epithet of either Nakula or Saha-deva.
माद्री: माद्री, f. ‘princess of the Madras,’ N. of the second wife of Pāṇḍu and mother of the twins Na-kula and Saha-deva, (they were said to be the two youngest of the sons of Pāṇḍu, q. v., but were really the sons of Mādrī by the Aśvins, cf. नकुल, कुन्ती); the wife of Saha-deva; wife of Kroṣṭu; wife of Kṛṣṇa; a species of plant (= अति-विषा). —माद्रि-नन्दन, अस्, m. (माद्रि for माद्री to suit the metre, cf. कुन्ति-नन्दन), ‘son of Mādrī,’ epi-thet of either Nakula or Saha-deva. —माद्री-पति, इस्, m. ‘husband of Mādrī,’ epithet of Pāṇḍu. —माद्री-पृथा-पति, इस्, m. ‘husband of Mādrī and Pṛthā,’ N. of Pāṇḍu.
माद्रेय: माद्रेय, अस्, m. ‘son of Mādrī,’ epithet of either Nakula or Saha-deva; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people.
माद्रुकस्थलक: माद्रुकस्थलक माद्रुकस्थलक (fr. मद्रु-क-स्थली), see Gaṇa Dhūmādi to Pāṇ. IV. 2, 127.
माधव: माधव माधव, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मधु), made of honey, honey-like, sweet; relating to spring, vernal; belonging or peculiar to the descendants of Madhu, i. e. the Yādavas, (माधवे ऽहनि, on a spring day; माधवी लक्ष्मीः, vernal beauty or, in Hari-vaṃśa 9597, the fortune of the Yādavas; माधवी देवी, N. of the earth); (अस्), m. an epithet of the second month of spring; the month Vai-śākha (= April-May); spring; a son or descendant of Madhu, a man of the race of Yadu; an epithet of Kṛṣṇa (Viṣṇu); of Paraśu-rāma (as an incarnation of Viṣṇu); of Indra; of a son of the third Manu; of one of the seven sages under Manu Bhautya; of another ancient sage; of a leader of the Pañca-rātra sect; of the author of the Rug-viniścaya; of the father of Dādābhāī and grandfather of the astrological writer Nārāyaṇa; of the father of the commentator Someśvara; of various other persons; Bassia Lati-folia or a species of leguminous plant, = कृष्ण-मुद्ग; (ई), f. honey-sugar, clayed or candied sugar; an intoxicating drink made of honey, mead; ‘spring-flower,’ Gærtnera Racemosa [cf. वासन्ती]; a kind of panic-grass; sacred basil; = मिसि (according to some, a sort of dentifrice); a procuress, bawd; afflu-ence in cattle or herds; a woman of the race of Madhu or Yadu (e. g. An-antā, wife of Janam-ejaya; Sampriyā, wife of Vidūratha; Kuntī, wife of Pāṇḍu); N. of Dākṣāyaṇī in Śrī-śaila; of Durgā; of a Mātṛ attending on Skanda; of a daughter of Yayāti; of a commentary (probably named after the author Mādhava); (अम्), n. sweetness; (in Schol. on Pāṇ. IV. 4, 129, a fem. form माधवा is given, agreeing with तनूः।) —माधव-कर, अस्, m., N. of a medical writer. —माधव-काल-निर्णय, अस्, m., N. of a work written by Mādhavācārya. —माधव-गुप्त, अस्, m. a proper N. —माधव-चरित, अम्, n., N. of a work. —माधव-देव, अस्, m. a proper N. —माधव-निदान, अम्, n., N. of a work by Mādhava (= रुग्-विनिश्चय). —माधव-पण्डित, अस्, m., N. of a scholar. —माधव-प्राची, f., N. of a place. —माधव-भट्ट, अस्, m., N. of various persons (= माधवाचार्य). —माधव-भिक्षु, उस्, m. a proper N. (= माधवाश्रम). —मा-धव-मागध, अस्, m., N. of a poet. —माधव-यतीन्द्र, अस्, m. a proper N. —माधव-योगिन्, ई, m. a proper N. —माधव-रामानन्द-सरस्-वती (°म-आन्°), m., N. of the teacher of the com-mentator Śivānanda. —माधव-वल्ली, f. Gærtnera Racemosa. —माधव-श्री, ईस्, f. the beauty or glory of spring. —माधव-सिंह and माधव-सेन, अस्, m., N. of two kings. —माधव-सेना-राजन्, आ, m. ‘king of the army of spring’ or ‘of sweet-ness, N. of a king. —माधव-सोमयाजिन्, ई, m. a proper N. (= माधवाचार्य). —माधवाचार्य (°व-आच्°), अस्, m. ‘the learned Mādhava’ or ‘the teacher Mādhava,’ N. of a celebrated scholar, son of Māyaṇa and brother of Sāyaṇācārya and Bhoga-nātha, q. q. v. v., (he is sometimes called simply Mā-dhava, and regarded, together with Sāyaṇa, as, author of the celebrated commentary on the Ṛg-veda; also author of the Kāla-nirṇaya, of the Nyāya-mālā-vistara, of the commentary Parāśara-smṛti-vyākhyā, of the Saṅkṣepa-śaṅkara-vijaya, of the Sarva-darśana-saṅ-graha.) —माधवानन्द-काव्य (°व-आन्°), अम्, n., N. of a poem by Nanda-paṇḍita. —माध-वानल (°व-अन्°), अस्, m., N. of an author. —मा-धवानलाख्यान (°व-अनल-आख्°), अम्, n., N. of an erotic work by the above. —माधवाश्रम (°व-आश्°), अस्, m. a proper N. —माधवी-लता, f. the creeper Gærtnera Racemosa (bearing white fra-grant flowers). —माधवी-वन, अम्, n., N. of a forest. —माधवेन्द्र-पुरी (°व-इन्°), m., N. of an author. —माधवेष्टा (°व-इष्°), f. a species of tuberous plant (= वाराही-कन्द); an epithet of Durgā. —माधवोचित (°व-उच्°), अम्, n. a kind of perfume (= कक्कोलक). —माधवोद्भव (°व-उद्°), अस्, m. a species of plant (= राजादनी).
माधवक: माधवक, अस्, m. a spirituous liquor (prepared from honey or from the blossoms of the Bassia Lati-folia); (इका), f. Gærtnera Racemosa; a kind of metre, four times ˘¯˘˘¯˘˘¯˘˘¯˘˘¯˘˘¯ ˘˘¯˘¯¯; N. of a woman; a female attendant.
माधवीय: माधवीय, अस्, आ, अम्, relating or belonging or devoted to Mādhava or to Mādhavācārya; composed by him. —माधवीय-धातु-वृत्ति, इस्, f., N. of a treatise on Sanskrit roots by Sāyaṇa (dedicated to his brother Mādhava). —माधवीय-वेदार्थ-प्र-काश, N. of Sāyaṇa's commentary on the Ṛg-veda.
माधव्य: माधव्य, अस्, m. a patronymic from Madhu, see Pāṇ. IV. 1, 106.
माध्व: 1. माध्व, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मधु), sweet; (ई), f. a kind of spirituous liquor; = माधवी, Gærtnera Racemosa; = माधुर-कण्टक, a kind of fish; (ई), m. du., Ved. ‘possessing or loving sweetness,’ an epithet of the Aśvins; (Sāy.) = मधु-पूर्ण-पात्र-युक्तौ; (in this last sense perhaps fr. a base मा-ध्वि।) —माध्वी-मधुरा, f. a species of date (= मधुर-खर्जुरिका).
माध्व 2. माध्व, अस्, m. (for 1. see col. 2), an adherent of Madhva.
माध्वक: माध्वक, अम्, n. = माधवक, an intoxicating beverage prepared from honey.
माध्विक: माध्विक, अस्, m. a person who collects honey.
माध्वीक: माध्वीक, अम्, n. a kind of intoxicating drink distilled from the blossoms of the Bassia Latifolia; wine, spirit distilled from grapes; [cf. मधु-म्°।] —माध्वीक-फल, अस्, n. a species of cocoa-nut (= मधु-नालिकेरक).
माधुक: माधुक माधुक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मधुक), coming from or belonging to the Madhuka tree; ‘mead-maker,’ an epithet of the Maireyakas or of a particular mixed caste.
माधुकर: माधुकर माधुकर, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मधु-कर), coming from a bee or from honey, belonging to a bee, resembling a bee, (माधुकरी वृत्तिः, a mode or course of life resembling that of a bee), be-longing to honey, &c.; (ई), f. gathering alms after the manner of a bee by going from door to door; alms obtained from five different places by the third class of religious mendicants.
माधुकर्णिक: माधुकर्णिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मधु-कर्ण), see Gaṇa Kumudādi 2. to Pāṇ. IV. 2, 80.
माधुच्छन्दस: माधुच्छन्दस, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मधु-च्छन्-दस्), Ved. relating to or coming from Madhu-cchan-das; (अस्), m. a patronymic of Agha-marṣaṇa; of Jetṛ.
माधुपर्किक: माधुपर्किक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मधु-पर्क), relating to the Madhu-parka; offered or presented as a token of respect to a guest.
माधुमत: माधुमत, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मधु-मत्), be-longing to or descended from Madhu-mat; (आस्), m. pl. the inhabitants of Kaśmīra; belonging to the river Madhu-matī, (माधुमतं जलम्, water from the Madhu-matī.)
माधुमतक: माधुमतक (fr. मधु-मत्), see Gaṇa Kac-chādi to Pāṇ. IV. 2, 134.
माधूकर: माधूकर, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मधु-कर), gathered or collected after the manner of bees.
माधुर: माधुर माधुर, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मधुर), composed by Madhura; relating to Madhurā; (ई), f. sweetness, amiableness; mead; spirituous or vinous liquor; (अम्), n. the blossom of Jasminum Zambac.
माधुर्य: माधुर्य, अस्, आ or -री (?), अम् (fr. मधुर), speaking sweetly or kindly; (अम्), n. sweetness, pleasantness, attractiveness, gracefulness; kindness, friendliness, amiability; (in rhetoric) the succession of single words in a sentence.
माधूक: माधूक माधूक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मधूक), made from Bassia Latifolia; (according to Kullūka) = मधुर-भाषिन्, sweetly speaking, kindly speaking; an epithet of the Maitreyakas (a mixed caste; cf. माधुक, col. 2).
माधूची: माधूची माधूची, m. du., Ved. (probably formed after the analogy of माध्वी, see under 1. माध्व, col. 2), an epithet of the Aśvins.
माधूल: माधूल माधूल, अस्, m. (fr. मधूल), a patronymic.
माध्य: माध्य माध्य, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. मध्य), middle, central, mid.
माध्यन्दिन: माध्यन्दिन, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मध्यन्-दिन), Ved. belonging to midday, meridional, midday, (माध्यन्दिने सवने, at the midday rite); middle, central; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a branch of the Vājasa-neyins and of an astronomical school who fixed the starting-point of planetary movements at noon; (अम्), n., scil. तीर्थ, N. of a Tīrtha; [cf. माध्यन्दि-नीयक।] —माध्यन्दिन-युग, Ved. belonging to the midday oblation. —माध्यन्दिन-शाखा, f. the school of the Mādhyandinas.
माध्यन्दिनायन: माध्यन्दिनायन, अस्, m. probably a patro-nymic, N. of a preceptor.
माध्यन्दिनि: माध्यन्दिनि, इस्, m. a patronymic, N. of a grammarian.
माध्यन्दिनीय: माध्यन्दिनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, usual or customary at the midday oblation (Ved.); ‘belonging to the school of the Mādhyandinas,’ an epithet of Nārā-yaṇa.
माध्यन्दिनीयक: माध्यन्दिनीयक, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha.
माध्यम: माध्यम माध्यम, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मध्यम), relating to the middle, middlemost, middle, central; middle-born; (आस्), m. pl. epithet of the Ṛṣis to whom the middle portion (Maṇḍala II — VII) of the Ṛg-veda Saṃhitā is attributed; N. of a race.
माध्यमक: माध्यमक, अस्, इका, अम्, = माध्यमिक; (इका), f. epithet of the middle section of the Kā-ṭhaka.
माध्यमकेय: माध्यमकेय, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people, = मध्यमकेय।
माध्यमस्थ्य: माध्यमस्थ्य, अम्, n. (fr. मध्यम-स्थ), the state of standing or being in the middle, see Gaṇa Brāhmaṇādi to Pāṇ. V. 1, 124; [cf. मा-ध्यस्थ्य।]
माध्यमिक: माध्यमिक, अस्, ई, अम्, relating or belonging to the middle, middlemost, middle; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a Buddhist school; of a people in the central part of India.
माध्यमिनेय: माध्यमिनेय, अस्, m. (fr. मध्यमा), a metronymic, see Gaṇa Kalyāṇyādi to Pāṇ. IV. 1, 126.
माध्यस्थ: माध्यस्थ माध्यस्थ, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मध्य-स्थ), being in a middle state, indifferent, impartial, neutral; (अम्), n. middle state or condition; indif-ference, impartiality.
माध्यस्थ्य: माध्यस्थ्य, अम्, n. ‘the state of standing in the middle or between two,’ indifference, impartiality, neutrality; the office of umpire, mediation, inter-cession.
माध्याह्निक: माध्याह्निक माध्याह्निक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मध्याह्न), belonging to midday, taking place at noon.
मान्: मान् मान् (connected with rt. मन्), cl. 1. P. मानति, &c., to honour, respect, revere, worship; cl. 10. P. मानयति, &c. (pro-perly Caus. of rt. मन्), to honour, &c.
मानन: मानन, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. Caus. of rt. मन्), honouring, serving as a honorarium or token of respect; (आ, अम्), f. n. the act of honouring, paying honour, showing respect.
माननीय: माननीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be honoured, deserving honour from any one (with gen.).
मानयितव्य: मानयितव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be honoured or respected, deserving honour.
मानयितृ: मानयितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, honouring, respecting, an honourer, one who honours or respects.
मानित: मानित, अस्, आ, अम्, honoured, respected; (अम्), n. honouring, showing honour or respect, honour. —मानित-सेन, अस्, m., N. of a king.
मानिन्: मानिन्। See s. v., p. 771, col. 1.

मानिन् मानिन्, ई, इनी, इ (fr. rt. मन् or fr. 1. मान), thinking, being of opinion, (in these and the following senses often at the end of comps.); considering, regarding, taking for; fancying or ima-gining one's self, taking one's self for [cf. पण्डित-म्°]; fancying that one possesses (e. g. क्षमता-मानिन्, fancying that one possesses ability); being regarded or taken for; honouring, esteeming highly; having a high opinion of one's self, proud, haughty, proud of anything (e. g. धनतो मानी नरः, a man proud of his wealth); maintaining one's honour, proud (in a good sense); highly honoured or esteemed; disdainful, angry, resentful, sulky; (ई), m. a lion; (इनी), f. an angry or disdainful woman or one offended with her lover; a species of odoriferous plant (= फली, i. e. प्रियङ्गु); N. of a daughter of Vidūra-stha and wife of Ṛājya-vardhana; a kind of metre, (probably incorrect for मालिनी।) —मानि-ता, f. or मानि-त्व, अम्, n. (at the end of a comp.) the fancying that one possesses, imagining or fancying one's self, taking one's self for (e. g. अज्ञाने ज्ञान-मानिता, the fancying when in ignorance that one has know-ledge); haughtiness, pride; honouring, paying respect; the being honoured, receiving honour.
मान्य: मान्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be respected or honoured, worthy of honour, honourable, respectable, venerable, held in honour; a patronymic (Ved.); = मैत्रा-वरुणि, author of Ṛg-veda VIII. 56, (in the last two senses fr. मान, father of Agastya); (आ), f. Trigo-nella Corniculata, (wrongly for माल्या।) —मान्य-त्व, अम्, n. honourableness, respectability, worthiness.
मानक: मानक (at the end of an adj. comp.) = 2. मान, measure, &c.; (अस्, अम्), m. n. = माणक, Arum Indicum, a plant having an edible root; (इका), f. a particular spirituous or vinous liquor; = माणिका, a particular weight (= 2 Añjalis, = 8 Palas; according to others, the fourth or eighth part of a Khāri).
मानःशिल: मानःशिल मानःशिल, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मनः-शिला), consisting of realgar or red arsenic.
मानव: मानव मानव, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मनु), de-scended from man or from Manu, belonging or proper to man or Manu, human; (Ved.) propitious to men; (अस्), m. a human being, man; a lad, boy, (for माणव, q. v.); a patronymic of Nābhā-nediṣṭha; of Śāryāta; of Cakṣus; of Nahuṣa; of Bhṛgu; of Su-dyumna; of Karūṣa; of Deva-hūti; (आस्), m. pl. the children of men, mankind; the subjects (of a king); N. of a school of the black Yajur-veda; (ई), f. a daughter of man or Manu, a woman; N. of a goddess (executing the commands of the eleventh Arhat of the present Ava-sarpiṇī); N. of one of the eleven Vidyā-devīs; (अम्), n. a man's length (as a measure, Ved.); = मानव-कल्प-सूत्र, q. v.; N. of a Sāman; a particular mulct or fine; [cf. Goth. manna, fr. mannan, perhaps for manvan; Germ. Mann, ‘a man.’] —मानव-कल्प-सूत्र or मानव-सूत्र, अम्, n., N. of a well-known Sūtra work on Kalpa or ritual (see मनु). —मानव-देव, अस्, m. ‘man-god, god among men,’ a king, prince. —मानव-धर्म-शास्त्र, अम्, n., N. of the code of laws attributed to Manu (see मनु-संहिता). —मानव-पति, इस्, m. ‘man-lord,’ a king, sovereign. —मा-नवाचल (°व-अच्°), अस्, m., N. of a mountain. —मानवाद्य (°व-आद्°), अम्, n., N. of a Sāman. —मानवेन्द्र (°व-इन्°), अस्, m. ‘man-chief, man-lord,’ a king. —मानवोत्तर (°व-उत्°), अम्, n., N. of a Sāman. —मानवोपपुराण (°व-उप्°), अम्, n., N. of an Upa-Purāṇa. —मानवौघ (°व-ओघ), with गुरु, epithet of a particular class of composers of mystical prayers [cf. the kindred words Divyaugha, Siddhaugha].
मानवस्य: मानवस्य, Nom. P. A. मानवस्यति, -ते, &c., Ved. to act like men; (Sāy.) to wish for men.
मानवस्यत्: मानवस्यत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, acting like men; (Sāy.) wishing for men, i. e. priests.
मानवीय: मानवीय, अस्, आ, अम्, descended or derived from Manu; (अम्), n. a particular fine [cf. मानव].
मानवेय: मानवेय, अस्, आ, अम्, descended or derived from Manu; (अस्), m. a patronymic.
मानव्य: मानव्य, अस्, m. a patronymic from Manu, Pāṇ. IV. 1, 105; (आयनी), f., see Pāṇ. IV. 1, 18; (अम्), n. a number of boys, assemblage of youths, (for माणव्य।)
मानवर्तिक: मानवर्तिक मानवर्तिक, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people; (also read मानवर्जक, मानवलक, गव-वर्तिल; cf. मालवर्ति।)
मानस: मानस मानस, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मनस्), be-longing to the mind or spirit, mental, spiritual, (as opposed to शारीर, corporeal; मानसं तीर्थम्, a spiritual bathing-place or the lake Mānasa so called); expressed only in the mind (e. g. मानसं स्तोत्रम्, a silent hymn of praise), tacit, implied; present in the mind, only to be conceived in the mind, (आभ-रणैर् मानसैः, with every conceivable orna-ment); dwelling on the lake Mānasa, (in this sense fr. मानस, अम्, n. the lake Mānasa, see below); (अस्), m. a form of Viṣṇu; N. of a Nāga; of a class of ascetics; of a son of Vapuṣ-mat; of a pre-ceptor; (आस्), m. pl. a particular class of Manes (regarded as sons of Vasiṣṭha); epithet of the Vaiśyas in Śāka-dvīpa; (ई), f., N. of one of the sixteen Vidyā-devīs [cf. महा-मानसिका]; (अम्), n. the mental powers, mind, spirit, the seat or faculty of reason and feeling, heart, soul, (in these senses frequently at the end of a comp., cf. भय-सन्-त्रस्त-म्°); tacit or implied consent (in law); N. of a sacred lake and place of pilgrimage on mount Kailāsa in the Himālaya mountains, (the native place of the wild geese or swans; constant allusions are made to this lake in Hindū poetry, and the Haṃsa or Rāja-haṃsa, a kind of wild goose, is described as migrating to its shores every year at the breeding season); a kind of salt. —मानस-चारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, frequenting lake Mānasa; (ई), m. a wild goose or swan. —मानस-जन्मन्, आ, m. ‘mind-born,’ the god of love; [cf. मनो-जन्मन्।] —मानस-त्व, अम्, n. thoughtfulness, spirituality, the belonging to spirit, fulfilment of anything in mere thought. —मानस-नयन, अम्, n. ‘guidance to the lake Mānasa,’ N. of a logical work by Jīvana. —मानस-नयन-प्रसादनी, f., N. of a commentary on the above work. —मानस-रुज्, क्, f., Ved. mental or spiritual disease. —मानस-वेग, अस्, आ, अम्, swift as spirit (i. e. thought); (अस्), m., N. of a king. —मानस-शुच्, क्, f., Ved. mental sorrow or grief. —मानस-सन्ताप, अस्, m. mental anguish, sorrow of heart. —मानसालय (°स-आल्°), अस्, m. ‘dwelling on the lake Mānasa,’ a wild goose or swan; [cf. मानसौकस्।] —मानसोत्तर (°स-उत्°), अस्, m., N. of a mountain range; [cf. उत्तर-मानस।] —मानसोल्लास (°स-उल्°), अस्, m., N. of a Vedānta work by Sureśvara Ācārya or Dakṣiṇa Ācārya, a disciple of Śaṅkara Ācārya. —मानसोल्लास-प्र-बन्ध and मानसोल्लास-वृत्तान्त and मान-सोल्लास-वृत्तान्त-विलास, अस्, m. names of commen-taries on the above work. —मानसौकस् (°स-ओक्°), आस्, आस्, अस्, dwelling on the lake Mānasa; (आस्), m. a wild goose or swan, the Rāja-haṃsa.
मानसायन: मानसायन, अस्, m. a patronymic from Manas, see Pāṇ. IV. 1, 110.
मानसिक: मानसिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मनस् or fr. मा-नस), mental, spiritual; (अस्), m. an epithet of Viṣṇu.
मानस्य: मानस्य, अस्, m. a patronymic from Manas, see Pāṇ. IV. 1, 105.
मानस्कृत: मानस्कृत मानस्-कृत, अस्, m., Ved. (ac-cording to Mahī-dhara) = पूजाया अभिमानस्य वा कर्तृ।
मानस्थली: मानस्थली मान-स्थली, f., मानस्थलक, see Pāṇ. IV. 2, 127.
मानाङ्क: मानाङ्क मानाङ्क, अस्, m. (perhaps for मा-लाङ्क), N. of the author of the Vṛndā-vana.
मानायन: मानायन मानायन, अस्, m. a patronymic.
मानाय्य: मानाय्य मानाय्य, मानाय्यायनी, see Gaṇa Gargādi to Pāṇ. IV. 1, 105, and Gaṇa Lohitādi to Pāṇ. IV. 1, 18.
मानिक: मानिक मानिक = मानिन् in पण्डित-म्°, q. v. (For मानिका see मानक, p. 770, col. 2.)
मानिन्ध: मानिन्ध मानिन्ध, अस्, m., N. of an astro-nomer, (also read मनिन्ध; cf. मणित्थ।)
मानुतन्तव्य: मानुतन्तव्य मानुतन्तव्य, अस्, m. (fr. मनु-तन्तु), Ved. a patronymic of Aikādaśākṣa; [cf. मारुतन्तव्य।]
मानुष: मानुष मानुष, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मनुस्), human, belonging to mankind, appertaining to men; humane, kind, favourable or propitious to men; (अस्), m. a man, human being, (often at the end of comps., and sometimes with fem. आ, cf. अ-म्°, अति-म्°; कार्य-म्°, a human being in some sense of the word, incar-nate in human form); epithet of the signs of the zodiac Gemini, Virgo, and Libra; (ई), f. a woman; scil. चिकित्सा, a branch of medicine, the administering of drugs and herbs (as opposed to आसुरी and दैवी चिकित्सा); (अम्), n. the manner or ways of men, condition of man, humanity; the doings or actions of man, human action or effort, manhood; N. of a place. —मानुष-ता, f. or मानुष-त्व, अम्, n. humanity, the state or condition of man, manhood, manliness, human existence, man's estate. —मानु-ष-प्रधन, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. fighting for men, (used in Ṛg-veda 1. 52, 9. as an epithet of the Maruts). —मानुष-बुद्ध, अस्, m. a human Buddha, (opposed to ध्यानि-बुद्ध।) —मानु-ष-मांसाद (स-आद), अस्, आ, अम्, eating human flesh. —मानुष-राक्षस, अस्, m. a fiend in human form, a Rākṣasa-like man. —मानुष-लौकिक, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging to the world of men, proper for man, human. —मानुष-सम्भव, अस्, आ, अम्, coming from a man, produced by men. —मानुषोपेत (°ष-उप्°), अस्, आ, अम्, joined with human effort.
मानुषीभू: मानुषी-भू, cl. 1. P. -भवति, &c., to become man, take human form.
मानुष्य: मानुष्य, अम्, n. (fr. मनुष्य), the being a man, humanity, manhood, manliness, human nature, man's estate; (अस्, -षी, अम्), human, manly, belong-ing to man or humanity.
मानुष्यक: मानुष्यक, अस्, ई, अम्, human; (अम्), n. hu-manity, human condition, human nature; a multi-tude of men.
मानोज्ञक: मानोज्ञक मानोज्ञक, अम्, n. (fr. मनो-ज्ञ), beauty, agreeableness, loveliness.
मान्तव्य: मान्तव्य मान्तव्य, अस्, m. a patronymic from Mantu, see Pāṇ. IV. 1, 105.
मान्त्र: मान्त्र मान्त्र, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मन्त्र), Ved. proper or peculiar to Vedic texts, belonging to sacred texts, relating to mystical verses or spells.
मान्त्रवर्णिक: मान्त्रवर्णिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मन्त्र-वर्ण), contained in the text of a Vedic hymn.
मान्त्रिक: मान्त्रिक, अस्, m. (fr. मन्त्र), one who recites a text or spell, one conversant with spells or incan-tations, an enchanter, sorcerer.
मान्त्रित: मान्त्रित मान्त्रित, आस्, m. pl. the descend-ants of Māntritya, see Pāṇ. IV. 2, III.
मान्त्रित्य: मान्त्रित्य, अस्, m. a patronymic from Mantrita, see Pāṇ. IV. 1, 105.
मान्थ्: मान्थ् मान्थ्, cl. I. P. मान्थति, &c., (according to Vopa-deva, Dhātu-pāṭha III. 9) = rt. मन्थ् or I. मथ्, to hurt, injure, &c.
मान्थ्य: मान्थ्य, अस्, आ, अम्, see Gaṇa Saṅkāśādi to Pāṇ. IV. 2, 80.
मान्थरेषणि: मान्थरेषणि मान्थरेषणि, इस्, m. a patro-nymic from Manthareṣaṇa, see Schol. on Pāṇ. II. 4, 66.
मान्थर्य: मान्थर्य मान्थर्य, अम्, n. (fr. मन्थर), weakness.
मान्थाल: मान्थाल मान्थाल, अस्, m., Ved. a kind of animal, (according to Mahī-dhara) a species of mouse.
मान्द: मान्द मान्द, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. मन्द् or 2. मद्), Ved. ‘gladdening,’ an epithet of water in certain formularies; (अस्, ई, अम्), relating to the higher apsis of a planet's course; मान्दं कर्म, the process of correction for the apsis; मान्दम् फलम्, the equation of the apsis, (in these latter senses fr. मन्द, q. v.)
मान्द्य: मान्द्य, अम्, n. (fr. मन्द), slowness, sluggish-ness, laziness; stupidity, torpor; apathy; weakness; indisposition, illness, sickness; मान्द्यं कृ, to make one's self ill.
मान्द्र: मान्द्र (fr. मन्द्र), see Gaṇa Chattrādi to Pāṇ. IV. 4, 62.
मान्दार: मान्दार मान्दार or मान्दारव, अस्, m. a species of tree (= मन्दार; cf. मन्दारव).
मान्दार्य: मान्दार्य मान्दार्य (fr. मन्दार), see Gaṇa Pragadyādi to Pāṇ. IV. 2, 80; perhaps used as a proper N. in Ṛg-veda 1. 165, 15.
मान्धातृ: मान्धातृ मान्धातृ, ता, m. (according to some fr. माम्, ‘me,’ + धातृ, ‘a drinker,’ this king having once sucked Amṛta from the finger of Indra, who thereupon used the exclamation which afterwards became the prince's name), N. of a king (son of Yuvanāśva, author of Ṛg-veda X. 134; also read मन्धातृ, q. v.); N. of a sovereign in more recent times. —मान्धाता-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a city; (also read मान्धात्ता-त्रिपुर।)
मान्धात्र: मान्धात्र, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to Māndhātṛ; (अस्), m. a patronymic from Mandhātṛ.
मान्ध्योद: मान्ध्योद मान्ध्योद, अस्, m. a patro-nymic (?).
मान्मथ: मान्मथ मान्मथ, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मन्म-थ), relating to or concerning love, excited by love, belonging to the god of love.
मान्यमान: मान्यमान मान्यमान, अस्, m., Ved. a pa-tronymic from Manyamāna; according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda VII. 18, 20, देवकं चिन् मान्यमानं जघन्थ may be translated, ‘thou hast slain Devaka the son of Manyamāna;’ according to others, ‘thou hast slain the god, the proud one.’
मान्यव: मान्यव मान्यव, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to Manyu.
मान्यवती: मान्यवती मान्यवती, f., N. of a princess; (perhaps for माल्य-वती।)
मापक: मापक मापक, अस्, इका, अम् (fr. Caus. of rt. 3. मा), serving for measuring or weighing, a measurer, &c.
मापन: मापन, अस्, m. a pair of scales, balance; (आ), f. measuring; measuring or meting out, making a place for a sacrifice, measure; (अम्), n. the act of measur-ing; forming, making, formation.
मापत्य: मापत्य मापत्य, अम्, n. (perhaps fr. 1. मा + अपत्य, i. e. not a child in the ordinary sense, cf. मनसि-ज; according to others fr. Caus. of rt. मे), a term applied to the god of love or Kāma-deva, (according to some, मापत्य, अस्, m.)
माबर: माबर माबर, N. of a place.
माम: माम माम, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मम, gen. sing. of 3. म), mine, my; mother, uncle, (in this sense like तात, q. v., and commonly in voc. sing.)
मामक: मामक, अस्, इका or Ved. ई, अम्, my, mine; selfish, greedy, covetous; (अस्), m. a miser, niggard; a maternal uncle; (ई), f., N. of a Buddhist goddess; [cf. मामुखी।]
मामकीन: मामकीन, अस्, आ, or ई (?), अम्, my, mine.
मामतेय: मामतेय, अस्, m. (fr. ममता), a metronymic of Dīrgha-tamas; (also read सामन्तेय।)
मामनसायति: मामनसायति मामनसायति, इस्, m. a patro-nymic (?).
मामल्लदेवी: मामल्लदेवी मामल्ल-देवी, f., N. of the mother of Śrī-harṣa (author of the Naiṣadhīya-caritra).
मामिडि: मामिडि मामिडि, इस्, m. a proper N.
मामुखी: मामुखी मामुखी, f., N. of a Buddhist goddess.
मामुदगजनवी: मामुदगजनवी मामुद-गजनवी, m. = محمود غزنوي i. e. Mahmūd of Ghaznī.
माम्पश्य: माम्पश्य माम्-पश्य, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. माम्, acc. of अहम् + पश्य), Ved. regarding or looking at me.
माय: माय माय, अस्, आ, अम् (according to some fr. rt. 3. मा, according to others fr. rt. मन् + य), illusory, possessing magical powers or powers of illu-sion (said of Viṣṇu); (अस्), m. an illusionist, conjurer, juggler; an evil spirit, Asura; (आ), f. art, wisdom, (according to Naighaṇṭuka III. 9 = प्रज्ञा), extra-ordinary or supernatural power, wonderful power, (in these meanings only in the earlier language); illusion, trick, artifice, deceit, deception, fraud, jug-glery, sorcery, witchcraft; wickedness, villany; a political trick, diplomatic artifice; an illusory image or apparition, phantasm, phantom, anything unreal, anything which deceives the sight (e. g. सिंह-म्°, a phantasm in the form of a lion, a phantom lion); philosophical illusion, idealism, unreality, (in the Sāṅkhya system applied to Prakṛti as the source of all apparent material objects); Illusion personified, (sometimes identified with Durgā as the authoress of spells, sometimes regarded as a daughter of Anṛta and Nirṛti or Nikṛti and mother of Mrityu or as a daughter of Adharma); (अस्), m. musk [cf. मृग-मद]; the constellation Mṛga-śiras; the month Mārgaśīrṣa (November-December). —मार्ग-तोरण, अम्, n. a triumphal arch erected over a road. —मार्ग-दर्शक, अस्, m. ‘way-shower,’ a guide. —मार्ग-दायिनी, f. ‘giving up the way,’ N. of Dākṣāyaṇī at Kedāra. —मार्ग-द्रङ्ग, अस्, m. a city or town on the road. —मार्ग-द्रुम, अस्, m. a tree growing by the way-side. —मार्ग-धेनु, उस्, m. or मार्ग-धेनुक, अम्, n. a Yojana, a measure of distance = 4000 fathoms or 4 Kos, above 8 miles, (perhaps originally a mile-stone representing a cow.) —मार्ग-प, अस्, or मार्ग-पति, इस्, m. ‘road-inspector,’ N. of a parti-cular official. —मार्ग-पथ, अस्, m. a course, road, path. —मार्ग-पाली, f. ‘road-protectress,’ N. of a goddess. —मार्ग-बन्धन, अम्, n. a road-obstruction, anything which blocks up a road, a bar-ricade. —मार्ग-मध्य-ग, अस्, आ, अम्, going in the middle of the road, being on the road. —मार्ग-रक्षक, अस्, m. a road-keeper, guard. —मार्ग-रोधिन्, ई, इनी, इ, road-obstructing, blocking up a road. —मार्ग-वटी, f. epithet of the tutelary god-dess of travellers. —मार्ग-वशानुग (°श-अन्°) or मार्ग-वशायात (°श-आय्°), अस्, आ, अम्, remaining on the road, going or situated along the road. —मार्-ग-शाखिन्, ई, m. ‘way-side tree,’ a tree by the road-side. —मार्गशीर्ष, see col. 3. —मार्ग-शोधक, अस्, m. ‘road-clearer,’ a pioneer. —मार्ग-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, being on the road, a traveller. —मार्ग-हर्म्य, अम्, n. a mansion or palace on a high-road. —मार्गागत (°ग-आग्°) or मार्गायात (°ग-आय्°), अस्, आ, अम्, come from the road or a journey, a traveller, wayfarer. —मार्गेश (°ग-ईश°), अस्, m. = मार्ग-प, col. 2. —मार्गैषिन् (°ग-एष्°), ई, इणी, इ, ‘road-seeking,’ searching for a road or path. —मार्गोपदिश् (°ग-उप्°), क्, m. ‘road-shower,’ a guide, leader.
मार्गक: मार्गक, अस्, m. the month Mārgaśīrṣa; [cf. प्रति-म्°।]
मार्गण: मार्गण, अस्, ई, अम्, seeking, searching for; in-vestigating; begging, requiring, asking, desiring; (अस्), m. a beggar, solicitor, suppliant, mendicant; an arrow; a symbolical expression for the number five derived from the five arrows of the god of love; (अम्, आ), n. f. the act of seeking or searching for, inves-tigation; research, inquiry; the act of begging, soli-citation, affectionate solicitation or inquiry, (in some of these senses usually आ, f.) —मार्गण-ता, f. the being an arrow, the state or nature of an arrow; मार्गणतां गतः, become an arrow. —मार्गण-प्रिया, f., N. of a daughter of Prādhā.
मार्गणक: मार्गणक, अस्, m. a beggar, solicitor, mendicant.
मार्गमाण: मार्गमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, seeking, searching for, tracing out, investigating.
मार्गयत्: मार्गयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, seeking, searching for, investigating, hunting after.
मार्गशिर: मार्गशिर, अस्, or मार्गशिरस्, आस्, m. (fr. मृग-शिरस्), the month Mārgaśīrṣa.
मार्गशीर्ष: मार्गशीर्ष, अस्, ई, अम्, born under the constel-lation Mṛga-śiras; (with and without मास), N. of the month in which the full moon enters the con-stellation Mṛga-śiras, the tenth or (in later times) the first month in the year = November-December; (ई), f. (with and without पौर्णमासी), the day on which the full moon enters the constellation Mṛga-śiras, the fifteenth day of the first half of the month Mārgaśīrṣa.
मार्गार: मार्गार, अस्, m., Ved. (according to Mahī-dhara) a patronymic from Mṛgāri; one who catches fish with his hands.
मार्गिक: मार्गिक, अस्, m. a hunter, huntsman; a traveller, wayfarer.
मार्गित: मार्गित, अस्, आ, अम्, sought, searched, sought or inquired after, pursued, hunted after; desired, re-quired.
मार्गितव्य: मार्गितव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be sought or sought after; to be searched through; to be striven after.
मार्गिन्: मार्गिन्, ई, m. one who clears or guards the way, a pioneer, guide.
मार्ग्य: 1. मार्ग्य, अस्, आ, अम् (for 2. see under rt. मार्ज् below), to be sought or searched for.
2. मार्ग्य, अस्, आ, अम् (properly fr. rt. 1. मृज्; for 1. see above), to be wiped away or removed, to be scoured, to be cleansed or purified.
मार्ग्यमाण: मार्ग्यमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, being hunted after or searched for, being chased.
मार्गमर्षि: मार्गमर्षि मार्गमर्षि, इस्, m., N. of a son of Viśvāmitra, (also read मार्दमर्षि।)
मार्गमित्र: मार्गमित्र मार्गमित्र, अस्, m. a patronymic.
मार्गयथ: मार्गयथ मार्गयथ, अस्, m. a patro-nymic (?).
मार्गव: मार्गव मार्गव, अस्, m. a particular mixed caste (born from a Niṣāda and an Ayogava female).
मार्गवेय: मार्गवेय मार्गवेय, अस्, m., Ved. the patro-nymic or metronymic of a Rāma.
मार्गीयव: मार्गीयव मार्गीयव or मार्गीयवाद्य, अम्, n., N. of a Sāman.
मार्ज्: मार्ज् मार्ज्, cl. 10. P. मार्जयति, -यितुम्, to wipe, scour, cleanse, purify, (in these senses allied to rt. 1. मृज्, fr. which the derivatives below may be formed); to sound, make a parti-cular sound, (in this sense connected with rts. मर्च्, मर्व्, मञ्ज्।)
मार्ज: मार्ज, अस्, आ, अम्, cleaning, scouring; a cleaner, scourer [cf. अस्त्र-म्°, शस्त्र-म्°]; (अस्), m. an epi-thet of Viṣṇu; purification, cleansing; a washerman.
मार्जक: मार्जक, अस्, इका, अम्, cleansing, scouring, clean-ing, purifying; a cleaner, scourer, sweeper; (per-haps) = मार्जन, Symplocos Racemosa.
मार्जन: मार्जन, अस्, ई, अम्, wiping away, cleansing, purifying, washing; (अस्), m. Symplocos Racemosa; (आ), f. washing, cleansing, purifying; the sound of a drum [cf. rt. मार्ज्]; (ई), f. a broom, besom, brush; N. of one of Durgā's female attendants; (अम्), n. the act of wiping or rubbing off; the act of cleaning, scouring, cleansing, sweeping; cleansing the person by wiping or bathing or rubbing it with unguents; the act of wiping away or effacing; (उच्छिष्ट-मार्जनम्, removing leavings.)
मार्जनीय: मार्जनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be cleaned, to be cleansed or purified; to be swept or brushed.
मार्जार: मार्जार, अस्, m. a cat, (probably so called from its habit of constantly cleaning itself); a polecat, civet-cat [cf. गन्ध-म्°]; a wild cat, = अरण्य-मार्-जार; (ई), f. a female cat; a civet-cat; musk. —मार्जार-कण्ठ, अस्, m. ‘having the throat or cry of a cat,’ a peacock. —मार्जार-करण, अम्, n. a particular posture in sexual intercourse. —मार्जार-कर्णिका or मार्जार-कर्णी, f. ‘cat-eared,’ an epi-thet of Cāmuṇḍā. —मार्जार-गन्धा, f. a species of Mudga-parṇī or pulse, Phaseolus Trilobus. —मार्-जार-गन्धिका, f. = मुद्ग-पर्णी, q. v. —मार्-जार-लिङ्गिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having the nature or charac-teristics of a cat. —मार्जारी-क्रमण, अम्, n. a particular kind of coitus.
मार्जारक: मार्जारक, अस्, m. a cat; a peacock (so called from its cat-like cry).
मार्जारि: मार्जारि, इस्, m., N. of a son of Saha-deva.
मार्जारीय: मार्जारीय, अस्, m. a cat; a Śūdra; one who cleanses or purifies his body (= काय-शोधन).
मार्जाल: मार्जाल, अस्, m. = मार्जार, a cat.
मार्जालीय: मार्जालीय, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘fond of washing or ablu-tion, delighting in purification,’ an epithet of Śiva in Mahā-bh. Vana-p. 1628, (according to the Scholiast = शुद्ध-देह = किरात); (अस्), m. a cat; a Śūdra; scil. धिष्ण्य, a heap of earth to the right of the Vedi on which the sacrificial vessels are cleansed (Ved.); N. of the seventeenth Kalpa.
मार्जाल्य: मार्जाल्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. fond of washing or ablution, delighting in purification; (according to Sāy.) entitled to worship.
मार्जित: मार्जित, अस्, आ, अम्, (see rt. 1. मृज्, with which this and the following may be connected), scoured, cleansed, purified, swept, brushed, adorned; (आ), f. curds with sugar and spice.
मार्जित, अस्, आ, अम् (equally to be connected with rt. मार्ज्), wiped, cleansed, purified, clean, smooth, bright; washed away, removed; rubbed, smeared, besmeared, &c.; see मार्जित, p. 774, col. 1.
मार्ष्टव्य: मार्ष्टव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be cleansed, to be scoured or purified, to be swept or brushed.
मार्ष्टि: मार्ष्टि, इस्, f. washing, cleaning, cleansing, puri-fying, cleansing the person or anointing it with oil; (इस्), m., N. of a son of Sāraṇa. —मार्ष्टि-मत्, आन्, m., N. of a son of Sāraṇa.
मार्डाकव: मार्डाकव मार्डाकव, अस्, m. a patronymic from Mṛḍāku.
मार्डाकवायन: मार्डाकवायन, अस्, m. a patronymic from Mār-ḍākava.
मार्डीक: मार्डीक मार्डीक, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. मृड्), Ved. gladdening, rejoicing; (अम्), n. compassion, grace, favour, (in this sense fr. मृडीक।)
मार्ड्यर्थ: मार्ड्यर्थ मार्ड्यर्थ, अस्, m., N. of a man; (आस्), m. pl., N. of his descendants.
मार्तण्ड: मार्तण्ड मार्तण्ड, अस्, m. (fr. मृतण्ड, but the old form is probably मार्ताण्ड below), the sun, the sun-god, (sometimes used in titles of books; cf. छन्दो-म्°, प्रमेय-कमल-म्°); an Āditya; a symbolical expression for the number twelve; a hog, boar. —मार्तण्ड-तिलक-स्वामिन्, ई, m., N. of a preceptor. —मार्तण्ड-वल्लभा, f. ‘beloved of the sun,’ the plant Polanisia Icosandra.
मार्ताण्ड: मार्ताण्ड, अस्, m. (fr. मृताण्ड), a bird (Ved.); ‘the bird in the sky,’ the sun, a statue of the sun-god.
मार्तवत्स: मार्तवत्स मार्तवत्स, अम्, n. (fr. मृत-वत्सा), Ved. born dead, still-born.
मार्तिक: मार्त्तिक मार्त्तिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मृत्तिका), made of clay or loam, earthen; (अस्), m. a kind of pitcher or earthenware vessel; the lid of a pitcher.
मार्त्तिक: मार्त्तिक मार्त्तिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मृत्तिका), made of clay or loam, earthen; (अस्), m. a kind of pitcher or earthenware vessel; the lid of a pitcher.
मार्त्तिकावत: मार्त्तिकावत (fr. मृत्तिकावती), N. of a country; epithet of the king of that country; N. of a city; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people; of a princely race.
मार्त्तिकावतक: मार्त्तिकावतक, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to the country Mārttikāvata.
मार्त्य: मार्त्य मार्त्य, अस्, आ (?) , अम् (fr. मर्त्य), mortal, corporeal; (अम्), n. the corporeal or mortal part, mortality.
मार्त्यव: मार्त्यव, अस्, ई, m. f. (fr. मृत्यु), a patronymic of Antaka.
मार्त्युञ्जय: मार्त्युञ्जय, अस्, ई, m. f. a patronymic from Mṛtyuñ-jaya.
मार्त्स्न: मार्त्स्न मार्त्स्न, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. मृत्स्ना), Ved. ground fine or small.
मार्दङ्ग: मार्दङ्ग मार्दङ्ग, अम्, n. (fr. मृदङ्ग), a city, town; (अस्), m. a drummer.
मार्दव: मार्दव मार्दव, अस्, m. (fr. मृदु), a patro-nymic; a particular mixed caste, (in this sense per-haps incorrectly for मार्गव); (अम्), n. softness, weak-ness, suppleness, pliancy, kindness, indulgence, gentle-ness, mildness, leniency, good nature; kindness or gentleness towards (with gen., e. g. मार्दवं सर्व-भूतानाम्, gentleness towards all living creatures). —मार्दव-भाव, अस्, m. the state of being soft or pliant, pliancy, suppleness. —मार्दवी-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, &c., to make soft, make weak or indul-gent. —मार्दवी-कृता, f. made soft, weak, self-indulgent, lax.
मार्दवायन: मार्दवायन, अस्, m. (fr. मार्दव), a patro-nymic.
मार्देय: मार्देय मार्देय, अस्, m. = मृदेर् अपत्यम्। —मार्देय-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a city.
मार्द्वीक: मार्द्वीक मार्द्वीक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मृद्वीका), coming from or made of grapes; (अम्), n. wine.
मार्ष: मार्ष मार्ष, अस्, m. (fr. मर्ष), a vene-rable or honourable man, respectable person; a kind of vegetable; [cf. मारिष।]
मार्षिक: मार्षिक, अस्, m. a kind of vegetable (= मा-रिष)।

(said to be fr. rt. 3. मा), N. of a district (lying west and south-west of Ben-gal); a barbarian or mountaineer of a particular tribe; an epithet of Viṣṇu; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a barbarous tribe of people; (आ), f. a wreath, garland, chaplet, crown; a row, line (= पङ्क्ति, Kirātārju-nīya V. 9); a chain, string, rosary, necklace [cf. अक्ष-म्°]; a collection, group [cf. नक्षत्र-म्°]; a series, regular succession, (नाम्नाम् माला, a col-lection of words arranged in order, a vocabulary, dic-tionary; cf. नाम-म्°); (in rhetoric) a series of epithets, a string of similes; (in the drama) the offering of many things to obtain a wish; a streak, (तडिन्-माला, a flash of lightning); N. of a river; of a lexicon; of a metre containing two lines of ¯¯˘¯¯˘˘¯˘¯¯ and two of ˘¯˘¯¯˘˘¯˘ ¯¯ of another metre, four times ˘˘˘˘˘˘, ˘˘˘˘˘˘˘˘¯ [cf. स्रज्]; of a Prākṛt metre of twice 45 and 43+27 instants; (अम्), n. a field, a forest or wood near a village; deceit, fraud, artifice; (अस्, आ, अम्), low, base. —माल-चक्रक, अम्, n. the hip-joint. —माल-भञ्जिका, f. (माल for माला), ‘breaking the garland,’ N. of a game. —माल-भा-रिन्, ई, इणी, इ (माल for माला), bearing or wearing a garland, having a chaplet or crown, garlanded. —माला-कण्ठ, अस्, m. the plant Achyranthes As-pera. —माला-कन्द, अस्, m. a species of bulbous plant. —माला-कर or माला-कार, अस्, m. a wreath-maker, garland-weaver, florist, gardener; the mixed caste of gardeners; N. of a son of Viśva-karman by a Śūdra woman or by Ghṛtācī; (ई), f. a woman who weaves garlands, a wreath-maker. —माला-कुट-दन्ती, f., N. of a Rākṣasī. —माला-गुण, अस्, m. the string of a garland, a necklace. —मालागुण-परिक्षिप्ता, f. ‘invested with the marriage string,’ a marriageable woman. —माला-गुणा, f., scil. लूता, a species of venomous spider. —माला-ग्रन्थि, इस्, m. = माला-दूर्वा, q. v. —मालाङ्क (°ला-अङ्°), अस्, m., N. of a king (the author of a commentary on the Mālatī-mādhava, and of the Vṛndā-vana). —मा-ला-तृण or मालातृणक, अम्, n. a fragrant grass, Andropogon Schœnanthus. —माला-दीपक, अम्, n.
