मालक: मालक, अस्, m. the Nimb tree, Melia Semper-virens; a wood near a village; (आ), f. a garland; (अकी), f., see Gaṇa Gaurādi to Pāṇ. IV. 1, 41; (इका), f. = माला, a garland, &c.; a necklace; a row, series, collection of things arranged in a line; a species of jasmine (= सप्तला); linseed, Linum Usi-tatissimum [cf. नव-मालिका]; a kind of bird [cf. मालिक]; an intoxicating drink; a daughter; a palace; N. of a river; (अम्), n. a garland, &c., a ring; Hibiscus Mutabilis.
मालय: 1. मालय (for 2. see p. 775, col. 1), Nom. P. मा-लयति (Aor. अममालत् = मालाम् आख्यत्), Schol. on Pāṇ. VII. 4, 2.

मालय 2. मालय, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मलय; for 1. मालय see p. 774, col. 3), coming from the Malaya mountains; (अस्), m. sandal-wood; N. of a son of Garuḍa; (अम्), n. the unguent prepared from sandal; a caravansary.
मालाका: मालाका, f. = मालिका। See under मालक above.
मालि: मालि, इस्, इस्, इ, (at the end of comps.) wreathed, garlanded, crowned [cf. सु-म्°]; (इस्), m., N. of a son of the Rākṣasa Su-keśa.
मालिक: मालिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. माला), relating or belong-ing to a garland; (अस्), m. a garland-maker, a gardener, florist; a painter, colourist, dyer; a species of bird; [cf. मालिका।]
मालिका: मालिका, f. See under मालक above.
मालित: मालित, अस्, आ, अम्, (at the end of comps.) garlanded, crowned, encircled, encompassed, surrounded.
मालिन्: मालिन्, ई, इनी, इ, garlanded, wearing a garland or chaplet, crowned; (at the end of comps.) wearing a garland or necklace of, crowned with, wreathed with, encircled by (e. g. नगरी चम्पक-मालिनी, a city encircled by Campaka trees; पृथिवी समुद्र-मालिनी, the sea-girt earth; cf. अंशु-म्°, ऊर्मि-म्°, किरीट-म्°, मरीचि-म्°, हेम-म्°); (ई), m. a wreath-maker, garland-maker; a florist, gardener; N. of a son of the Rākṣasa Su-keśa [cf. मालि]; (इनी), f. the wife of a wreath-maker or gardener, a female florist; N. of a city (= चम्पा); N. of two plants (= अग्नि-शिखा and दुर्-आलभा); N. of a celestial maiden; of a divine Mātṛ (one of the seven Mātṛs of Skanda); an epithet of Durgā; N. of one of Durgā's female attendants; epithet of a girl seven years old (representing Durgā at the festival of that goddess); N. of a Rākṣasī, the mother of Vibhī-ṣaṇa; N. assumed by Draupadī (while resident with king Virāṭa, cf. Mahā-bh. Virāṭa-p. 246); N. of Śveta-karṇa's wife, daughter of Su-cāru; of the wife of Priya-vrata; of the wife of Ruci and mother of Manu Raucya; of the wife of Prasena-jit; of the celestial Ganges (= गङ्गा = मन्दाकिनी); of various other rivers; N. of various metres, four times ¯˘¯¯¯¯, four times ˘˘˘˘¯˘˘¯˘¯ ˘¯, four times ˘˘˘˘˘˘¯¯, ¯˘¯¯˘¯¯; the personification of a particular musical mode; a poeti-cal stanza consisting of alternate verses or hemistichs of eight and seven syllables; it is especially used to conclude a section or canto. —मालिनी-तन्त्र, अम्, n., N. of a Tantra. —मालिनी-विजय, अस्, m., N. of a work.
मालीय: 1. मालीय, Nom. P. मालीयति, &c., to wish one's self a garland, &c.
2. मालीय, अस्, आ, अम्, destined or fitted or suited for a garland, &c.
मालेय: मालेय, अस्, m. (fr. मालि), a patronymic, = मालिन्, N. of a Rākṣasa; (आ), f. great cardamoms.
माल्य: माल्य, अस्, आ, अम्, relating or belonging to a gar-land, &c., proper or fit for a garland; (अस्), m. a patronymic; (आ), f. the plant Trigonella Corniculata; (अम्), n. a wreath, garland, chaplet, crown; a flower. —माल्यगुणाय, Nom. A. (fr. माल्य-गुण), मा-ल्यगुणायते, &c., to become the string of a garland, to appear like a wreath, to become a garland. —माल्य-जीवक, अस्, m. one who lives by making or selling wreaths. —माल्य-पिण्डक, अस्, m., N. of a Nāga. —माल्य-पुष्प, अस्, m. a kind of hemp (= शण). —माल्य-पुष्पिका, f. a species of plant (= शण-पुष्पी). —माल्य-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, gar-landed, crowned, adorned with crowns or garlands; (आन्), m., N. of a Rākṣasa, the son of Su-keśa; of one of Śiva's attendants; of a mountain or moun-tainous range (described as one of the smaller moun-tains of India proper, lying eastward of mount Meru); (अती), f., N. of a river. —माल्य-वृत्ति, इस्, m. one who subsists by making or selling garlands. —माल्या-पण (°य-आप्°), अस्, m. a market for the sale of wreaths or garlands, garland market, flower market.
मालकौश: मालकौश मालकौश, अस्, m. = कौशिक, a particular Rāga or musical mode.
मालति: मालति मालति, इस्, f. = मालती below.
मालतिका: मालतिका, f., N. of one of the Mātṛs attending upon Skanda; of a woman.
मालती: मालती, f. Jasminum Grandiflorum (both the plant and its blossom; it bears fragrant white flowers which open towards evening); a species of plant (= विशल्या); Bignonia Suaveolens; a shrub, Echites Caryophyllata; a bud, blossom; a maid, virgin, young woman; moonshine, moonlight; night; N. of various metres, viz. four times ˘¯˘˘¯˘, four times ˘˘˘˘¯˘˘¯˘¯˘¯, and four times ¯˘˘ ¯˘˘¯˘˘¯˘˘¯˘˘¯˘˘¯˘˘¯¯; N. of a river; of a woman; of Kalyāṇa-malla's commentary on the Megha-dūta; (probably) = काच-मल, = मालती-तीर-ज. —मालती-क्षारक, अस्, m. (pro-bably) borax. —मालती-तीर-ज, अस्, m. borax (found on the bank of the Mālatī). —मालती-तीर-सम्-भव, अम्, n. white borax. —मालती-पत्त्रिका, f. = जाति-पत्त्री, the outer shell of a nutmeg. —मा-लती-फल, अम्, n. a nutmeg. —मालती-माधव, अम्, n. ‘Mālatī and Mādhava,’ N. of a celebrated drama by Bhava-bhūti (so called from the names of the heroine and hero). —मालती-माला, f. a garland of jasmine blossoms; N. of a lexicon.
मालद: मालद मालद, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people; (also read मानद।)
मालव: मालव मालव, अस्, m., N. of a country (Malwa in central India); of a Rāga or particular scale in music; of a man; (आस्), m. pl. the inha-bitants of Malwa; (आ), f., N. of a river; (ई), f. a princess of the Mālavas; N. of the wife of Aśva-pati and progenitress of the Mālavas; (अम्), n. a kind of Prākṛt metre, 16+12+16+12 instants; (अस्, ई, अम्), relating or belonging to the Mālavas. —मा-लव-गुप्त, अस्, m., N. of an author. —मालव-देश, अस्, m. the country of Mālava or Malwa. —मालव-नृपति, इस्, m. a king of Mālava. —मा-लव-रुद्र, अस्, m., N. of a poet. —मालव-वि-षय, अस्, m. the country of Mālava or Malwa. —मालव-श्री, ईस्, f., N. of a particular musical mode or scale. —मालवाधीश (°व-अध्°) or मा-लवेन्द्र (°व-इन्°), अस्, m. a king of Mālava.
मालवक: मालवक, relating to the province of Mālava or Malwa; (अस्), m. the country of the Mālavas; a native of Mālava or Malwa; (इका), f. Ipomœa Tur-pethum; N. of a woman. —मालविकाग्निमित्र (°का-अग्°), अम्, n. ‘Mālavikā and Agnimitra,’ N. of a drama by Kālidāsa (so called from the names of the heroine and hero).
मालवीय: मालवीय, अस्, आ, अम्, native of or belonging to Mālava.
मालव्य: मालव्य, अस्, m. epithet of one of the Mahā-puruṣas born under particular constellations (Ved.); a prince of the Mālavas. —मालव्य-देश, N. of a country.
मालवर्ति: मालवर्ति मालवर्ति, इस्, m., N. of a people.
मालसी: मालसी मालसी, f., N. of a plant (com-monly called Keśapuṣṭa).
मालहायन: मालहायन मालहायन, अस्, m. a patro-nymic.
माला: माला माला। See under माल, p. 774.
मालायन: मालायन मालायन, अस्, m. a patronymic.
मालिन्द्य: मालिन्द्य मालिन्द्य, अस्, m., N. of a moun-tain.
मालिन्य: मालिन्य मालिन्य, अम्, n. (fr. मलिन), foul-ness, uncleanness, dirtiness, pollution, defilement, im-purity; sinfulness; trouble, affliction; blackness, obscurity.
मालु: मालु मालु, उस्, m., N. of a particular mixed caste; N. of one of Śiva's attendants; (उस्), f. a species of creeper (= पत्त्र-वल्ली, पत्त्र-लता); a woman. —मालु-धान, अस्, m. a particular kind of snake; (ई), f. a species of creeper.
मालुक: मालुक, अस्, m. Ocimum Sanctum; [cf. कृष्ण-मालुक।]
मालुद: मालुद मालुद, (with Buddhists) a parti-cular high number.
मालूर: मालूर मालूर, अस्, m. a fruit tree, Ægle Marmelos; Feronia Elephantum.
माल्ल: माल्ल माल्ल, अस्, m. (fr. मल्ल), N. of a particular mixed caste.
माल्लवास्तव: माल्लवास्तव, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मल्ल-वास्तु), see Schol. on Pāṇ. IV. 2, 120.
माल्लवी: माल्लवी, f. a wrestling or boxing match, exhibi-tion of wrestlers (= मल्ल-यात्रा).
माल्व्य: माल्व्य माल्व्य, अम्, n. (fr. मल्व), foolish-ness, inconsiderateness, thoughtlessness, awkwardness, (opposed to धैर्य।)
मावत्: मावत् मा-वत्, ind., Ved. like me.
माविलम्बम्: माविलम्बम् मा-विलम्बम्, मा-विलम्बितम्। See under 1. मा, p. 764.
मावेल्ल: मावेल्ल मावेल्ल, अस्, m., N. of a son of Vasu (prince of Cedi).
मावेल्लक: मावेल्लक मावेल्लक, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people; (also read मावेलक, मावेल्वक।)
माशब्दिक: माशब्दिक माशब्दिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मा-शब्दः, see 1. मा), commanding silence, prohibi-tive, prohibiting; a prohibitor, forbidder.
माष: माष माष, अस्, m. a bean, (the sing. is used for the plant, the pl. for the fruit); Phaseolus Radiatus, a valued kind of pulse having seeds marked with black and grey spots, (अकृष्टा माषाः, ‘wild beans,’ epithet of a Ṛṣi-gaṇa, to whom Ṛg-veda IX. 86, 1. is ascribed); a particular weight of gold, &c. = 5 Kṛṣṇalas = (1/16) Suvarṇa, (the weight in common use is said to be about seventeen grains troy); a cutaneous eruption resembling beans; a fool, blockhead. —माष-तैल, अम्, n. an oily preparation from beans. —माष-पर्णी, f. a kind of leguminous shrub, Glycine Debilis (= पृश्नि-पर्णी). —माष-वर्धक, अस्, m. a goldsmith, jeweler. —माष-शराविन्, ई, m., N. of a man. —माष-शस्, ind. after the manner of a Māṣa, Māṣa-wise, Māṣa by Māṣa. —माषाज्य (°ष-आज्°), अम्, n. a dish of beans dressed or cooked with ghee. —माषाद (°ष-अद°) or °ष-आद), अस्, m. ‘bean-eater,’ a tortoise. —माषाश (°ष-आश°), अस्, m. ‘bean-eater,’ a horse. —माषोण or माषोन (°ष-ऊन°), अस्, आ, अम्, minus a Māṣa, lacking one Māṣa; see Gaṇa Giri-nadyādi to Pāṇ. VIII. 4, 10.
माषक: माषक, अस्, m. a bean; a particular weight of gold, &c. = 7 or 8 Guñjās, = according to some, about 4(1/2) grains; (अस्, आ, अम्), amounting to or worth a particular number of Māṣas, (at the end of comps., cf. पञ्च-म्°।)
माषशरावि: माषशरावि, इस्, m. a patronymic, (probably fr. माष-शराविन्।)
माषि: माषि, इस्, m. a patronymic from Māṣa.
माषिक: माषिक, अस्, ई, अम्, worth one Māṣa, amounting to or worth a particular number of Māṣas, (at the end of comps., cf. पञ्च-म्°।)
माषीण: माषीण, अस्, आ, अम्, sown with beans; (अम्), n. a bean field, a field producing black kidney-beans.
माष्य: माष्य, अस्, आ, अम्, fitted or suited for beans (= माषीण); amounting to or worth a particular number of Māṣas, (used in this sense at the end of comps. after numerals, &c., cf. द्वि-म्°, अध्यर्ध-म्°); (अम्), n. a field of kidney-beans.
मास्: मास् 1. मास्, आस्, n., Ved. = मांस्, flesh, meat.

मास् 2. मास्, आस्, m. (fr. rt. 3. मा; accord-ing to Pāṇini and Vopa-deva used in all cases except the nom. sing. du. pl. and acc. sing. du., according to the lexicographers and Garga also in the nom. sing.; inst. pl., Ved. माद्भिस्), the moon; a month; [cf. पूर्ण-म्°, पुष्प-म्°; cf. also Zend maoñh, ‘moon, month;’ maoñha, ‘moon:’ Gr. μήν for μήνς, Ion. μείς, μήν-η, μην-ιαῖο-ς, Æol. μῆνν-ος for μῆνσ-ος: Lat. mensis, Mena, men-struus; Goth. mena, menoth-s: Old Germ. ma-not: Angl. Sax. mona, monadh: Lith. menu, ‘moon;’ ménesi-s, ‘month:’ Old Slav. mese-ci, ‘moon, month.’]
मास: मास, अस्, अम्, m. n. (but usually m.), the moon (cf. पूर्ण-म्°; in this sense occurring in Ved. in the comp. सूर्य-मासा, sun and moon, see Ṛg-veda VIII. 83, 2, X. 64, 3, &c., where, however, मासा may be referred to 2. मास्); a month or the twelfth part of the Hindū year, (usually a lunar month con-sisting of thirty Tithis; there may be also a Saura or solar month, equal to the sun's passage through a sign of the zodiac, a Sāvana month consisting of thirty risings and settings of the sun, a Nakṣatra month regulated by the lunar asterisms, and a Bār-haspatya month depending on the motions of the planet Jupiter; the lunar month being of two kinds, as reckoned from the new or full moon, completes six modes of monthly computation); (मासे, after the lapse of a month); a symbolical expression for the number twelve; [cf. Lat. mensi-s; Hib. mios; Cambro-Brit. mis] —मास-कालिक, अस्, आ, अम्, lasting for a month, available for a month, monthly; मासकालिकं वेतनम्, a month's wages. —मास-चारिक, अस्, आ, अम्, practising (anything) for a month. —मास-जात, अस्, आ, अम्, one month old. —मास-ज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्, knowing the months; (अस्), m. a species of gallinule (= दात्यूह). —मास-तम, अस्, आ, अम्, monthly [cf. अर्ध-म्°, संवत्सर-तम]; completing a full month (= मास-पूरण)। —मास-ताल, अस्, आ, अम्, having time measured monthwise? (apparently applied to the sound of cym-bals &c., which lasts a long while). —मास-तुल्य, अस्, आ, अम्, equal to a month or to a number of months.
मासत्रय: —मास-त्रय, अम्, n. three months. —मासत्र-यावधि (°य-अव्°), ind. for the space of three months. —मास-देय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be paid or discharged in a month (as a debt). —मास-धा, ind. by the month, monthly. —मास-पाक, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. maturing or producing results in a month. —मास-पूर्व, अस्, आ, अम्, a month before, a month earlier, (in this sense पूर्व has not the pronominal declension.) —मास-प्रमित, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘measured by months,’ occurring once a month; (अस्), m. new moon. —मास-प्रवेश, अस्, m. the beginning of a month. —मासप्रवेशानयन (°श-आन्°), अम्, n., N. of an astronomical work. —मास-भुक्ति, इस्, f. the (sun's) monthly course; [cf. पक्ष-भुक्ति।] —मास-मान, अस्, m. a year. —मास-वर्त्तिका, f. a species of wagtail (= सर्षपी). —मास-शस्, ind. by the month, monthly, month by month; for months. —मास-सञ्चयिक, अस्, आ, अम्, having provisions for a month. —मास-स्तोम, अस्, m., Ved., N. of an Ekāha. —मासाधिप (°स-अध्°), अस्, and Ved. मासाधिपति (°स-अध्°), इस्, m. the regent or planet presiding over a month. —मासानुमा-सिक, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. मास + अनु-मास), performed from month to month, monthly. —मासान्त (°स-अन्°), अस्, m. the end of a month, day of new moon. —मासापवर्ग (°स-अप्°), अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. con-tinuing a month at the most. —मासावधिक (°स-अव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having a month as the limit, happen-ing in the period of a month at the latest. —मासा-हार (°स-आह्°), अस्, आ, अम्, taking food only once a month. —मासोपवास (°स-उप्°), अस्, m. fasting a whole month. —मासोपवासिनी (°स-उप्°), f. a woman who fasts a whole month; (ironically) a lascivious woman, procuress.
मासिक: मासिक, अस्, ई, अम्, (at the end of a comp.) re-lating or pertaining to a month [cf. अर्ध-म्°]; monthly, happening every month (e. g. मासिकं श्राद्धम्, a monthly Śrāddha; cf. अष्ट-म्°); lasting or continuing for a month (e. g. मासिको व्याधिः, a sickness which continues for a month); performed or paid &c. within or after a month, payable in a month, to be restored in a month; engaged for a month or by the month (as a teacher, servant, &c.); dedicated to a particular month; (अम्), n. a particular Śrāddha or funeral rite per-formed every new moon. —मासिकान्न (°क-अन्°), अम्, n. the food given at a monthly oblation to the Manes (Manu XI. 157).
मासीन: मासीन, अस्, आ, अम्, one month old; monthly.
मास्य: मास्य, अस्, आ, अम्, (at the end of comps.) a month old, lasting or continuing a month.
मासन: मासन मासन, अम्, n. Vernonia Anthelmin-thica; the seed of this plant (?).
मासर: मासर मासर, अम्, n., Ved. a particular made dish, a mixture of the water in which rice and millet are boiled with yeast, grasses, &c.; (अस्), m. the meal of parched barley mixed with sour milk or buttermilk and covered with grass; the scum of boiled rice, rice-gruel.
मासुरकर्ण: मासुरकर्ण मासुरकर्ण, अस्, m. a patro-nymic from Masura-karṇa.
मासूर: मासूर मासूर, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मसूर), of the shape of a lentil, lentil-shaped; consisting or made of lentils or pulse.
माह्: माह् माह्, cl. 1. P. A. माहति, -ते, &c., to measure, mete.
माहकस्थली: माहकस्थली माहक-स्थली, f., N. of a place.
माहकि: माहकि माहकि, इस्, m. (probably a patro-nymic fr. महक), N. of a preceptor; [cf. छन्-दोग-म्°।]
माहत: माहत माहत, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. महत्), see Gaṇa Utsādi to Pāṇ. IV. 1, 86; (अम्), n. great-ness (?), see Gaṇa Pṛthvādi to Pāṇ. V. 1, 122.
माहन: माहन माहन, अस्, m. a Brāhman.
माहा: माहा माहा, f. a cow; [cf. महा, मही, माहेयी।]
माहाकुल: माहाकुल माहाकुल or माहाकुलीन, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. महा-कुल), of noble family or lineage, nobly born, of illustrious descent.
माहाचमस्य: माहाचमस्य, अस्, m., Ved. a patronymic from Mahā-camasa.
माहाचित्ति: माहाचित्ति, इस्, इस्, इ (fr. महा-चित्त), see Gaṇa Sutaṅgamādi to Pāṇ. IV. 2, 80.
माहाजनिक: माहाजनिक or माहाजनीन, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. महा-जन), fit for or suitable to great persons; fit for merchants.
माहात्मिक: माहात्मिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. महात्मन्), high-minded, magnanimous, noble, lofty, exalted, digni-fied, majestic; of great sanctity or honour; glorious.
माहात्म्य: माहात्म्य, अम्, n. (fr. महात्मन्), greatness of soul, high-mindedness, magnanimity, exalted state or position, greatness, majesty, dignity; the peculiar efficacy or virtue of any divinity or sacred shrine; a work giving an account of the merits of any holy place or object; [cf. देवी-म्°, भाव-नारायण-म्°।]
माहानद: माहानद, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. महा-नद), relating to a great river, see Gaṇa Utsādi to Pāṇ. IV. 1, 86.
माहानस: माहानस, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. महानस), relating or belonging to a large carriage; belonging to a kitchen, &c.; see Gaṇa Utsādi to Pāṇ. IV. 1, 86.
माहानामन: माहानामन or माहानामिक or माहानाम्-निक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. महा-नाम्नी), Ved. relating to or connected with the Mahā-nāmnī verses; = महा-नाम्न्यो ब्रह्मचर्यम् अस्य, = महा-नाम्नीश् चरति or तासां व्रतं चरति [cf. महानाम्-निक]; माहानामिक or माहानाम्निक, अस्, m. a Brāhman versed in the above portion of the Vedas.
माहापुत्रि: माहापुत्रि, इस्, इस्, इ (fr. महा-पुत्र), see Gaṇa Sutaṅgamādi to Pāṇ. IV. 2, 80.
माहाप्राण: माहाप्राण, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. महा-प्राण), relat-ing to the hard breathing or aspirate, having the hard breathing, &c.; see Gaṇa Utsādi to Pāṇ. IV. 1, 86.
माहाभाग्य: माहाभाग्य, अम्, n. = महा-भाग्य, great good fortune, great prosperity.
माहारजन: माहारजन, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. महा-रजन), dyed with saffron.
माहाराजिक: माहाराजिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. महा-राज), attached or devoted to or honouring the reigning prince; imperial, fit for a great king, royal.
माहाराज्य: माहाराज्य, अम्, n. (fr. महा-राज), the rank of a reigning prince or great sovereign.
माहाराष्ट्र: माहाराष्ट्र, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. महा-राष्ट्र), belonging to the Mahrattas or Marāṭhas; (ई), f. the Mahratta language, (more properly Marāṭhī.)
माहावार्त्तिक: माहावार्त्तिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. महा-वार्त्तिक), familiar with Kātyāyana's Vārttikas.
माहाव्रती: माहाव्रती, f. (fr. महा-व्रत), the doctrine of the Pāśupatas.
माहाव्रतीय: माहाव्रतीय, a wrong reading for महाव्रतीय, q. v.
माहेन्द्र: माहेन्द्र, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. महेन्द्र), relating or belonging to great Indra (e. g. माहेन्द्रं ध-नुस्, great Indra's bow, i. e. the rainbow; माहेन्-द्रम् अम्भस्, great Indra's water, i. e. rain-water; माहेन्द्री दिश्, great Indra's region, i. e. the eastern quarter); fit or proper for mighty Indra; eastern, running or flowing eastward; (अस्), m. = शुभ-दण्ड-विशेष; a patronymic; epithet of the seventh Muhūrta; (ई), f. the energy of Indra, one of the seven divine Mātṛs and one of the Mātṛs of Skanda; a cow; (scil. दिश्), the east; (scil. ऋच्), a hymn in praise of Indra (Ved.). —माहेन्द्र-ज, आस्, m. pl. (with Jainas) N. of a class of gods. —मा-हेन्द्र-वाणी, f., N. of a river.
माहेशी: माहेशी, f. (fr. महेश), a N. of Durgā.
माहेश्वर: माहेश्वर, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. महेश्वर), relating or belonging to the great lord Śiva; worshipping Śiva; (अस्), m. a worshipper of Śiva; (ई), f. the energy of Śiva, one of the divine Mātṛs (= pārvatī or Durgā); N. of a river; a species of climbing plant (= यव-तिक्ता). —माहेश्वर-तन्त्र and माहेश्वरी-तन्त्र, अम्, n., N. of a work. —मा-हेश्वरोपपुराण (°र-उप्°), अम्, n., N. of an Upa-Purāṇa.
माहिक: माहिक माहिक, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people; (also read माहिष।)
माहिकीप्रस्थ: माहिकीप्रस्थ माहिकीप्रस्थ, N. of a village in the north of India; see also Schol. on Pāṇ. IV. 2, 110.
माहित्थि: माहित्थि माहित्थि, इस्, m., Ved., N. of a preceptor.
माहित्य: माहित्य माहित्य, अस्, m. a patronymic from Mahita, see Gaṇa Gargādi to Pāṇ. IV. 1, 105; (माहितास्, m. pl., see Gaṇa Kaṇvādi to Pāṇ. IV. 2, 111.)
माहित्र: माहित्र माहित्र, अम्, n., scil. सूक्त, epithet of the hymn Ṛg-veda X. 185 (beginning with the words महि त्रीणाम्).
माहिन: माहिन माहिन, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. 1. मह्), Ved. great, exalted, joyful, joyous, gladsome, exhila-rated; giving pleasure, yielding enjoyment; an epi-thet of the place in which Soma is prepared; (अम्), n. sovereignty, dominion, kingdom. —माहिना-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. exhilarated, excited; endowed with might, mighty; (Sāy. = महिमोपेत।)
माहिर: माहिर माहिर, अस्, m. an epithet of Indra.
माहिष: माहिष माहिष, अस्, ई, अम्, (fr. महिष), coming from or belonging to a buffalo or buffalo cow; (अस्), m., N. of a district; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people; [cf. महिष।] —माहिष-स्थली, f., N. of a place.
माहिषक: माहिषक, अस्, m. a buffalo herdsman, buffalo keeper; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people.
माहिषिक: माहिषिक, अस्, m. a buffalo herdsman, one who lives by keeping or breeding buffaloes; (said to mean) the paramour of an unchaste woman, one who lives by the prostitution of his wife; (आ or ई), f., N. of a river.
माहिष्य: माहिष्य, अस्, m. a particular mixed caste, the son of a Kṣatriya father and a Vaiśya mother, (whose business is attendance on cattle with the practice of astronomy and music.)
माहिष्मती: माहिष्मती माहिष्मती, f. of माहिष्मत (fr. महिष्मत्), N. of a city founded by Mahiṣ-mat or by Mucu-kunda.
माहिष्मतेयक: माहिष्मतेयक, see Gaṇa Kattryādi to Pāṇ. IV. 2, 95.
माहीन: माहीन माहीन, अस्, m., Ved. (perhaps) a patronymic.
माहीयत्व: माहीयत्व माहीयत्व, Ved. beginning with the word महीय-त्व (?).
माहुरदत्त: माहुरदत्त माहुरदत्त, N. of a place.
माहुल: माहुल माहुल, अस्, m. a patronymic.
माहेय: माहेय माहेय, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मही), made of earth, earthen, relating to the earth, terrestrial; (अस्), m. the son of the earth, the planet Mars; coral; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people; (ई), f. a cow.
माहेल: माहेल माहेल, अस्, m. a patronymic.
मि: मि 1. मि (in some of its senses connected with rt. 3. मा), cl. 5. P. A. मिनोति, मिनुते, ममौ or मिमाय, मिम्ये, मास्यति, -ते, अमासीत्, अमास्त, मातुम्, Ved. to fix or fasten in the earth; to found, establish; to erect, build; to measure; to judge, observe, perceive; to cast, throw, throw away or about, scatter; [cf. मयूख।]
मित्: मित्, त्, f., Ved. a post (erected or fixed in the ground), a column; [cf. गर्त-म्°, उप-म्°, प्र-ति-म्°।]
मित् मित्। See under rt. 1. मि, p. 776, col. 3.
मिति: 1. मिति, इस्, f., Ved. fixing, erecting, establishing.
2. मिति, इस्, f. (for 1. मिति see col. 1), measuring, measure, weight, value, quantity; determining; accu-rate knowledge [cf. माति]; proof, evidence.
मिक्ष्: मिक्ष् मिक्ष् or मिमिक्ष् (thought by some to be desiderative forms fr. a lost rt. मिश्, contained in the words मिश्र, मिश्ल, but referred by native commentators to the rt. 1. मिह्, q. v.), मिमिक्षति, मिमिक्षुस्, मिमिक्षे, to mix, stir up, to give a relish to; (A.) to mix, be mixed: Caus. मेक्षयति, यितुम्, to stir up, mix, mingle; [cf. म्यक्ष्।]
मिघ्: मिघ् मिघ् = rt. 1. मिह्, only in निमे-घमान, अस्, आ, अम् [cf. मेघ], Ved. emitting moisture; (Sāy. = न्यञ्चि अवाङ्मुखानि वृष्ट्य्-उदकानि सिञ्चत्, sprinkling down rain-water.)
मिचिता: मिचिता मिचिता, f., N. of a river; (various reading for निश्चिता।)
मिच्छक: मिच्छक मिच्छक, अस्, m., N. of a Buddhist patriarch.
मिच्छ्: मिछ् मिछ्, cl. 6. P. मिच्छति, मिमिच्छ, मिच्छितुम्, to annoy, hurt, pain; to obstruct, hinder.
मिछ्: मिछ् मिछ्, cl. 6. P. मिच्छति, मिमिच्छ, मिच्छितुम्, to annoy, hurt, pain; to obstruct, hinder.
मिञ्ज्: मिञ्ज् मिञ्ज्, cl. 10. P. मिञ्जयति, -यितुम्, to speak; to shine.
मिञ्जिकामिञ्जिक: मिञ्जिकामिञ्जिक मिञ्जिका-मिञ्जिक, अम्, n., N. of two beings sprung from the seed of Rudra.
मिण्मिण: मिण्मिण मिण्मिण, अस्, आ, अम्, speaking indistinctly through the nose.
मित्र: मित्र 1. मित्र, अस्, m. (originally मित्त्र, fr. rt. 2. मिद्, or according to some fr. rt. मिथ् + त्र; cf. मेदिन्), a companion, associate, friend, (in this sense generally neut., except in Ved.; see अम्, n. below); N. of an Āditya or form of the sun (as a Vedic deity commonly associated with Varuṇa, both Mitra and Varuṇa being frequently invoked together with another of the Ādityas called Aryaman; Mitra is regarded in Ṛg-veda VIII. 47, 9, as son of Aditi; elsewhere he is called the deity of the constellation Anu-rādhā, and father of Ut-sarga: according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda 1. 89, 3, Mitra presides over the day as Varuṇa over the night; hence the closest con-nection subsists between these two deities, who are more frequently invoked together than Varuṇa is invoked singly; together they uphold and rule the earth and sky, together they guard the world, toge-ther they promote religious rites, avenge sin, and are the lords of truth and light; associated with Aryaman, they are represented as awful deities, haters, and dispellers of all falsehood; in only one hymn, Ṛg-veda III. 59, Mitra is celebrated alone, and is there described as calling men to activity, sustaining earth and sky, and beholding all creatures with un-winking eye; in Ṛg-veda VII. 61, 1, the sun is described as the eye of Mitra-Varuṇa); the sun; N. of a Marut; of a son of Vasiṣṭha; of the third Muhūrta; (आ), f., N. of an Apsaras, (also read चित्र); N. of the mother of Maitreya and Maitreyī; N. of one of the wives of Daśa-ratha, (cf. सु-मित्रा; according to some, in this sense मित्री); (अम्), n. a friend, (औरसम् मित्रम्, a friend con-nected by blood relationship); an ally, the next neighbour of a king; epithet of a mode of fighting, (also read भिन्न); friendship (Ved.). —मित्र-करण, अम्, n. the making of friends, making one's self friends. —मित्र-कर्मन्, अ, n. a friendly office. —मित्र-काम, अस्, आ, अम्, desirous of friends, wishing for friends. —मित्र-कार्य, अम्, n. the business of a friend, a friendly office, friendship. —मित्र-कृत्, त्, m. ‘friend-maker,’ N. of a son of the twelfth Manu. —मित्र-कृति, इस्, f., Ved. (ac-cording to Sāy.) a friendly office. —मित्र-कौस्तु-भ, अस्, m. a proper N. —मित्र-क्रु or मित्र-क्रू, Ved. (probably) N. of an evil being; see Ṛg-veda X. 89, 14. —मित्र-गुप्त, अस्, आ, अम्, protected by Mitra; (अस्), m., N. of a man. —मित्र-गुप्ति, इस्, f. protection of friends. —मित्र-घ्न, अस्, ई, अम्, ‘friend-killing,’ treacherous; (अस्), m., N. of a Rā-kṣasa; (आ), f., N. of a river, (also read चित्र-घ्नी।) —मित्र-ज्ञ, अस्, m., N. of a demon (said to steal oblations). —मित्र-ता, f. or मित्र-त्व, अम्, n. friendship, friendliness, alliance, intimacy, (मि-त्रतां सम्प्राप्तः, one who has become a friend.) —मित्र-तूर्य, अम्, n., Ved. victory or triumph of friends. —मित्र-देव, अस्, m., N. of a man; of one of the sons of the twelfth Manu. —मित्र-द्रुह्, ध्रुक्, क्, क्, or -ध्रुट्, ट्, ट्, (see 2. द्रुह्) or मित्र-द्रोहिन्, ई, इणी, इ, seeking to injure a friend, the be-trayer of a friend, a false or treacherous friend; [cf. Zend mithra-druj.] —मित्र-द्रोह, अस्, m. injury or betrayal of a friend. —मित्र-द्विष्, ट्, ट्, ट्, or मित्र-द्वेषिन्, ई, इणी, इ, hating or injuring a friend; (ट्), m. a treacherous friend. —मित्र-धर्मन्, आ, m., N. of a demon (said to steal oblations). —मित्र-धा, ind., Ved. in a friendly manner. —मित्र-धित, अम्, n. or मित्र-धिति, इस्, f. or मित्र-धेय, अम्, n., Ved. a covenant or contract of friendship, friendly compact. —मित्र-पति, इस्, m., Ved. lord of friends or of friendship. —मित्र-पद, अम्, n. ‘Mitra's place,’ N. of a particular locality. —मित्र-प्रतीक्षा, f. regard for a friend. —मित्र-बन्धु-हीन, अस्, आ, अम्, destitute of friends or relations. —मित्र-बाहु, उस्, m., N. of one of the sons of the twelfth Manu; of a son of Kṛṣṇa. —मित्र-भ, अम्, n., Ved. a friendly constellation, Mitra's Nakṣatra, i. e. Anu-rādhā. —मित्र-भानु, उस्, m., N. of a king. —मित्र-भाव, अस्, m. a state of friendship, friendliness, friendly disposition. —मित्र-भू, ऊस्, m. a proper N. —मित्र-भृत्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. entertaining or receiving a friend. —मित्र-भेद, अस्, m. separation of friends, breach of friendship; N. of the first book of the Pañca-tantra. —मित्र-महस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, Ved. (perhaps) having plenty of friends, rich in friends; having a friendly light, causing a favourable lustre; (Sāy.) = मित्राणाम् पूजक, अनुकूल-दीप्तिमत्, हितकारि-तेजस्, &c. —मित्र-मिश्र, अस्, m., N. of the author of the Vīra-mitrodaya. —मित्र-यज्ञ, अस्, m., N. of a man. —मित्र-युज्, क्, क्, क्, Ved. joining one's self to a friend, joining a friend to one's self; (क्), m., N. of a man; (जस्), m. pl., N. of his descendants. —मित्र-युद्ध, अम्, n. a contest of friends, a strife or quarrel between friends, conflict of allies, feud. —मित्र-लब्धि, इस्, f. = मित्र-लाभ below. —मित्र-लाभ, अस्, m. acquisition of friends or of friendship, forming friendship; N. of the first book of the Hitopadeśa. —मित्र-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having friends, possessing friends; (आन्), m., N. of a demon (said to steal oblations); N. of a son of the twelfth Manu; of a son of Kṛṣṇa; (अती), f., N. of a daughter of Kṛṣṇa. —मित्र-वत्सल, अस्, आ, अम्, affectionate towards friends, winning, captivating, engaging. —मित्र-वन, अम्, n. ‘Mitra's wood,’ N. of a forest. —मित्र-वरण, अम्, n. choice of friends, the act of choosing of friends or acquaint-ances. —मित्र-वर्चस्, आस्, m. a proper N. —मित्र-वर्ध, see Gaṇa Dhūmādi to Pāṇ. IV. 2, 127; [cf. मैत्रवर्धक।] —मित्र-वर्धन, अस्, ई, अम्, making friends prosperous, prospering friends (Ved.); N. of a demon (said to steal oblations). —मित्र-वर्ध्र, see Gaṇa Dhūmādi to Pāṇ. IV. 2, 127. —मित्र-वर्मन्, आ, m. a proper N. —मि-त्र-वाह, अस्, m., N. of a son of the twelfth Manu. —मित्र-विद्, त्, m. ‘a friend-knower,’ one who knows friends, (various reading for मन्त्र-विद्, a spy.) —मित्र-विन्द, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘finding friends, acquir-ing friends,’ epithet of an Agni; (अस्), m., N. of a son of the twelfth Manu; of a son of Kṛṣṇa; of a preceptor; (आ), f. epithet of an Iṣṭi; N. of a wife of Kṛṣṇa. —मित्र-विषय, अस्, m. friendship. —मित्र-वैर, अम्, n., Ved. dissension among friends. —मित्र-शर्मन्, आ, m., N. of various persons. —मित्र-शिस्, ईस्, ईस्, ईस् (शिस् fr. rt. शास्, cf. आशिस्), ruling over friends or allies; see Vopa-deva XXVI. 69. —मित्र-सप्तमी, f. epithet of the seventh day in the light half of the month Mārga-śīrṣa. —मित्र-सम्प्राप्ति, इस्, f. ‘acquistion of friends,’ N. of the second book of the Pañca-tantra. —मित्र-सह, अस्, आ, अम्, tolerant of friends, in-dulgent towards friends; (अस्), m., N. of a king, (also called कल्माष-पाद); N. of a Brāhman. —मित्र-साह, अस्, आ, अम्, = मित्र-सह above. —मित्र-साह्वया, f., N. of a divine being. —मि-त्र-सेन, अस्, m., N. of a son of the twelfth Manu; of a grandson of Kṛṣṇa; of a Buddhist; of a king of the Draviḍa country. —मित्र-हत्या, f. the mur-der of a friend. —मित्र-हन्, आ, m. one who kills or murders a friend; [cf. मित्र-घ्न।] —मित्र-हू = मित्रं ह्वयति, see Vopa-deva XXVI. 72. —मित्राख्य (°र-आख्°), अस्, आ, अम्, named after Mitra. —मित्राचार (°र-आच्°), अस्, m. treatment of friends, conduct to be observed towards a friend. —मित्रातिथि (°र-अत्°), इस्, m., Ved. a proper N. —मित्रानुग्रहण (°र-अन्°), अम्, n. the act of favouring friends or causing them prosperity. —मि-त्राभिद्रोह (°र-अभ्°), अस्, m. = मित्र-द्रोह, q. v. —मित्रा-वरुण, औ, m. du. Mitra and Varuṇa, see p. 777, under 1. मित्र; (मित्रा-वरुणयोर् अय-नम्, N. of a particular festival.) —मित्रावरुण-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. accompanied by Mitra and Varuṇa. —मित्रावरुणीय, अम्, n. the office of the Ṛtvij Mitrā-varuṇa. —मित्रा-वसु, उस्, m., N. of a son of Viśvā-vasu, king of the Siddhas. —मित्री-कृ, cl. 8. P. A. —करोति, -कुरुते, &c., to make a friend, make any one a friend, make any one friendly to one's self. —मित्री-भू, cl. 1. P. -भवति, &c., to become a friend, make friends with (with inst.). —मित्री-भूय, ind. becoming a friend or friendly. —मित्रेरु (°र-ईरु°), उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. (Sāy.) troubling friends, disturbing friends or friendly wor-shippers (= मित्राणां यजमानानाम् ईरयितृ, = मित्राणाम् बाधक). —मित्रेश्वर (°र-ईश्°), scil. हर, N. of a statue of Śiva erected by Mitra-śarman. —मित्रोदय (°र-उद्°), अस्, m. a friend's welfare, the success or prosperity of a friend; sunrise; N. of a work by Mitra-miśra on jurisprudence, (abbre-viated from वीर-म्°।)
2. मित्र, Nom. P. मित्रति, &c., to be friendly, act in a friendly manner.
मित्रक: मित्रक, अस्, m. a proper N.
मित्रय: मित्रय, Nom. P. मित्रयति, &c., (probably) to befriend.
मित्रयु: मित्रयु, उस्, उस्, उ (fr. मित्रय above), friendly-minded; winning or acquiring friends, attractive; = लोक-यात्राभिज्ञ, possessing worldly prudence, ac-quainted with the traditions and customs of mankind; (उस्), m. a friend; N. of a teacher; of a son of Divo-dāsa; (अवस्), m. pl., N. of a race.
मित्राय: मित्राय, Nom. A. मित्रायते, &c., (probably) to desire or wish for a friend.
मित्रायु: मित्रायु, उस्, उस्, उ (fr. मित्राय above), desiring a friend, seeking friendship (Ved.); (उस्), m., N. of a son of Divo-dāsa, (also read मित्रेयु); N. of a preceptor.
मित्रिन्: मित्रिन्, ई, इणी, इ, Ved. befriended, having a friend; united by friendship.
मित्रिय: मित्रिय, अस्, आ, अम्, friendly, coming from or relating to a friend.
मित्रिय, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. = मित्रिय; (at the end of a comp.) see Gaṇa Vargyādi to Pāṇ. VI. 2, 131.
मित्रीय: मित्रीय, Nom. P. मित्रीयति, &c., to treat any one as a friend or companion, to seek to make a friend of any one.
मित्रीयत्: मित्रीयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, becoming a friend, acting as a friend, deserving friendship.
मिथ्: मिथ् मिथ् (connected with rts. मेथ्, मिध्, मेध्, 1. मिद्, मेद्, मिल्), cl. 1. P. A. मेथति, मिथति, मेथते, &c., to meet or associate with; to unite, pair; to meet as rivals, be mutually antagonistic, wrangle, contradict, revile; to take hold of, grasp; to understand, perceive, know; to hurt, injure; to strike, kill.
मिथत्या: मिथत्या, ind., Ved. alternately, emulously; (ac-cording to Sāy. मिथत्या is inst. c. of मिथति = हिंसा।)
मिथस्: मिथस्, ind. together, mutually, reciprocally, with each other, in common, to one another; from each other; between one another, secretly, privately, in secret; alternately, by turns. —मिथस्-तुर्, Ved. following closely on one another (as day and night), alternating, emulous, (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda VI. 49, 3, मिथस्-तुरा = परस्परम् बाध-यन्त्यौ, mutually opposing each other.) —मिथ-स्पृध्य, अस्, आ, अम्, emulating or vying together, mutually emulous. —मिथो-अवद्य-प, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. mutually averting calamities. —मिथो-योध, अस्, m., Ved. hand to hand fighting with one another.
मिथु: मिथु, ind., Ved. falsely, wrongly, pervertedly, confusedly.
मिथुन: मिथुन, अस्, आ, अम्, paired, forming a pair; (अस्), m., Ved. a pair (male and female, boy and girl, son and daughter), a twin couple, a brace, couple or pair in general, (in Ved. usually m. du., e. g. सप्ती मिथुना, a pair of horses; गो-मिथुनौ, a pair of cows; in the later language mostly neut.); (अम्), n. a pair, couple, brace; twins; union, junction; congress of the sexes, pairing, cohabitation, copula-tion; the sign of the zodiac Gemini, or the third arc of 30° in a circle, (in this sense also अस्, m.); (in gram.) a root compounded with a preposition; a term applied to a particular kind of small statue at the entrance of a temple. —मिथुन-त्व, अम्, n. or मिथुन-भाव, अस्, m. the state of being a pair or forming a couple. —मिथुन-व्रतिन्, ई, इनी, इ, devoted to sexual cohabitation, practising copula-tion. —मिथुनी-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, -कर्तुम्, to cause to pair or couple, effect the union of the sexes. —मिथुनी-चारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, coupling together, co-habiting, having sexual intercourse. —मिथुनी-भा-व, अस्, m. copulation, cohabitation, amorous incli-nation. —मिथुनी-भू, cl. 1. P. -भवति, &c., to become paired, to be joined or united in couples, be arranged in pairs. —मिथुनी-भूय, ind. being joined in pairs, forming or uniting in couples. —मि-थुने-चर, अस्, आ, अम्, going in pairs, living in pairs; (अस्), m. the Cakra-vāka.
मिथुनाय: मिथुनाय, Nom. A. मिथुनायते, &c., to co-pulate, couple, pair, cohabit sexually.
मिथुया: मिथुया, ind., Ved. invertedly, distortedly, per-versely, falsely, incorrectly; [cf. मिथ्या below.]
मिथुस्: मिथुस्, ind., Ved. = मिथुया above, (मिथुर् भू, to turn out badly, fail); reciprocally, mutually (= मिथस्).
मिथूदृश्: मिथू-दृश्, क्, क्, क्, Ved. seen or appearing alter-nately.
मिथो: मिथो, ind. = मिथस्, q. v., cf. Gaṇa Svarādi to Pāṇ. I. 1, 37.
मिथ्या: मिथ्या, ind. (probably a contracted form for मिथुया above), invertedly, distortedly, contrarily, perversely, falsely, incorrectly, wrongly, improperly, (कथम् मयि मिथ्या प्रवर्तसे, why dost thou act improperly towards me ?); untruly, deceitfully, in a lying manner, (with वद्, वच्, ब्रू, to speak falsely, to make a false assertion); in vain; मिथ्या at the beginning of a comp. is often equivalent to an adj., and translatable by ‘false, untrue, sham, unjust,’ &c.; Mithyā, Untruth, is personified as the wife of A-dharma. —मिथ्या-कर्मन्, अ, n. false act, failure. —मिथ्या-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, &c., to make false, falsify, utter a falsehood, contradict: Caus. P. -कार-यति, &c., to pronounce [a word] wrongly once: Caus. A. -कारयते, to pronounce wrongly over and over again; see Pāṇ. 1. 3, 71. —मिथ्या-कोप, अस्, m. feigned resentment, pretended anger. —मिथ्या-क्रय, अस्, m. a false price. —मिथ्या-ग्रह or मिथ्याग्रह (°या-आग्°), अस्, m. improper persist-ency, useless obstinacy. —मिथ्याचरत् (°या-आच्°), अन्, अन्ती, अत्, acting or practising falsehood. —मि-थ्या-चर्या, f. false behaviour, hypocrisy. —मिथ्या-चार (°या-आच्°), अस्, आ, अम्, dealing falsely, per-versely; hypocritical, sanctimonious; (अस्), m. im-proper or incorrect conduct, wrong treatment (in medicine). —मिथ्या-जल्पित, अम्, n. a false report or rumour. —मिथ्या-ज्ञान, अम्, n. a false con-ception, misapprehension, error, mistake. —मिथ्या-त्व, अम्, n. falsity, unreality; illusion; (with Jainas) the lowest of the fourteen steps which lead to final emancipation; inversion; perversion (as one of the eighteen faults of a Jaina system). —मिथ्यात्विन्, ई, इनी, इ, being in a state of illusion. —मिथ्या-दर्-शन, अम्, n. a false appearance; false doctrine, heresy. —मिथ्या-दृष्टि, इस्, f. false doctrine, he-resy, denial of future existence, atheism. —मिथ्या-ध्यवसिति (°या-अध्°), इस्, f. ‘fruitless trouble,’ epithet of a figure of speech expressing the impossi-bility of a thing by making it depend upon some impossible contingency (e. g. ‘only one who wears a crown of air can engage the affections of a harlot’). —मिथ्या-निरसन, अम्, n. denial by oath. —मिथ्या-पण्डित, अस्, आ, अम्, one who makes a false pretence to learning, educated or learned only in appearance. —मिथ्यापवाद (°या-अप्°), अस्, m. a false accusation. —मिथ्या-पुरुष, अस्, m. a mere sham person, a man only in appearance. —मिथ्या-प्रतिज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्, false to one's promise, faithless, treacherous. —मिथ्या-प्रवादिन्, ई, इनी, इ, speaking falsely, lying. —मिथ्या-प्रवृत्ति, इस्, f. an erro-neous course of action, wrong function (of the senses), misdirected effort. —मिथ्या-प्रसुप्त, अस्, आ, अम्, falsely or pretendedly asleep, feigning sleep. —मि-थ्या-फल, अम्, n. an imaginary or vain advantage or reward. —मिथ्याभिगृध्न (°या-अभ्°), अस्, आ, अम्, unjustly covetous. —मिथ्याभिधा (°या-अभ्°), f. a false name. —मिथ्याभिधान (°या-अभ्°), अम्, n. a false or untrue expression or assertion. —मिथ्याभियोग (°या-अभ्°), अस्, m. an unjust claim, a false accusation, groundless charge. —मि-थ्याभिशंसन, अम्, n. or मिथ्याभिशस्ति (°या-अभ्°), इस्, f. a false accusation. —मिथ्याभिशंसिन् (°या-अभ्°), ई, m. a false or unjust accuser. —मिथ्या-भिशाप, अस्, m. an unjust claim, false accusation; a false prediction. —मिथ्या-भू, cl. 1. P. -भवति, &c., to be false, &c. —मिथ्या-मति, इस्, f. false opinion, error, ignorance, mistake. —मिथ्या-मान, अस्, m. false pride. —मिथ्या-योग, अस्, m. wrong use or employment. —मिथ्या-वदत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, speaking falsely. —मिथ्या-वध्यानुकीर्तन (°य-अन्°), अम्, n. the proclaiming that any one has been unjustly sentenced to death. —मिथ्या-वाक्य, अम्, n. an untruthful speech, falsehood, lie. —मिथ्या-वाच्, क्, क्, क्, whose words are false, untruthful, lying. —मिथ्या-वाद, अस्, m. false or untruthful speech, a falsehood, lie; declaring the falsehood of an accu-sation; (अस्, आ, अम्), speaking untruly, lying. —मि-थ्या-वादिन्, ई, इनी, इ, speaking untruly, lying, a liar; declaring an accusation to be false. —मिथ्या-वार्त्ता, f. false report. —मिथ्या-व्यापार, अस्, m. wrong occupation, meddling with another's affairs. —मिथ्य-साक्षिन्, ई, m. a false witness. —मिथ्या-साक्षि-प्रदातृ, ता, त्री, तृ, bringing forward false witnessess. —मिथ्याहार (°या-आह्°), अस्, m. impro-per nourishment, wrong diet. —मिथ्योत्तर (°या-उत्°), अम्, n. (in law) an untrue answer, false or prevaricating reply. —मिथ्योपचार (°या-उप्°), अस्, m. a feigned or pretended service or kindness; (in medicine) wrong treatment.
मिथि: मिथि मिथि, इस्, m., N. of a son of Nimi and king of Mithilā.
मिथित: मिथित मिथित, अस्, m. a proper N.
मिथिल: मिथिल मिथिल, अस्, m., N. of a king, the founder of Mithilā; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people, probably the inhabitants; (आ), f., N. of a city said to have been founded by Mithi or Mithila, (it was the capital of Videha or the modern Tirhut, and residence of king Janaka.) —मिथिलाधिपति (°ला-अध्°), इस्, m. lord of Mithilā, i. e. Janaka.
मिद्: मिद् 1. मिद्, cl. 1. P. A. मेदति, -ते, &c., = rt. मिथ्, q. v.

मिद् 2. मिद् or मिन्द्, cl. 1. A. मेदते, मिमिदे, मेदिष्यति, अमिदत्, मेदितुम्; cl. 4. P. A. मेद्यति, -ते, मिमेद, मिमिदे, मेदिष्-यति, अमिदत्, मेदितुम्; cl. 10. P. मिन्दयति, मेदयति, &c., to become fat; to be unctuous or greasy; to liquefy, melt; to feel affection for any one, love [cf. मित्र, rt. स्निह्]; to rejoice (Ved. ?); Caus. मेदयति, -यितुम्, to fatten, make fat (Ved.); [cf. Gr. μειδάω: Old Germ. minna, minni, ‘love:’ Lith. myliu, ‘I love;’ miêlas, ‘dear:’ Russ. milyĭ, ‘kind, affable.’]
मिन्न: मिन्न, अस्, आ, अम्, become fat, fat; unctuous; affectionately disposed towards any one.
मिद्ध: मिद्ध मिद्ध, अम्, n. sloth, indolence; sleepiness, torpor; dulness, heaviness of spirits or intellect.
मिध्: मिध् मिध्, cl. 1. P. A. मेधति, -ते, मेधितुम्, =rt. मिथ्।
मिन्दा: मिन्दा मिन्दा, f., Ved. a bodily defect, fault, blemish; [cf. Lat. menda.]
मिन्व्: मिन्व् मिन्व् (connected with rts. निन्व्, सिन्व्), cl. 1. P. मिन्वति, &c., to sprinkle, moisten, water (= rt. पिन्व्); to worship, serve, gratify by service.
मिमङ्क्षा: मिमङ्क्षा मिमङ्क्षा, f. (fr. Desid. of rt. मज्ज्) the wish to plunge into water, desire of bathing or diving.
मिमङ्क्षु: मिमङ्क्षु, उस्, उस्, उ, being about to plunge into water, desirous of bathing or diving.
मिमत: मिमत मिमत, अस्, m. a proper N.; [cf. मैमत।]
मिमन्थिषा: मिमन्थिषा मिमन्थिषा, f. (fr. Desid. of rt. मथ् or मन्थ्), the desire of stirring up or shaking, desire of destroying, &c.
मिमन्थिषु: मिमन्थिषु, उस्, उस्, उ, wishing to stir up, wishing or being about to shake or destroy.
मिमर्दयिषु: मिमर्दयिषु मिमर्दयिषु or मिमर्दिषु, उस्, उस्, उ (fr. Desid. of rt. 1. मृद्), wishing to crush, being about to crush or grind to powder.
मिमिक्ष: मिमिक्ष मिमिक्ष, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. Desid. of rt. 1. मिह्), Ved. mixed, mingled; (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda VI. 34, 4, मिमिक्ष may = वृष्ट्य्-उदकानां सेक्तृ, the sprinkler of rain-waters.)
मिमिक्षु: मिमिक्षु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. mixed, mingled; being mixed, &c.; wishing to rain down, desirous of bestowing; (Sāy. = वर्षितुम् इच्छत्।)
मियक्ष्: मियक्ष् मियक्ष्। See म्यक्ष्, p. 800, col. 1.
मियेध: मियेध मियेध, अस्, m. food set before the gods, a sacrificial meal or oblation, (perhaps) = मेध, a sacrificial animal or victim, (according to Sāy. de-rived fr. मेध; cf. Zend myazda.)
मियेध्य: मियेध्य, अस्, आ, अम्, partaking of or receiving the sacrificial food, worthy of the oblation; (Sāy. = मेधस्य यज्ञस्य योग्य or यज्ञार्ह।)
मिरफ: मिरफ मिरफ, (with Buddhists) a parti-cular high number.
मिराखान: मिराखान मिरा-खान, अस्, m., N. of a Paṭhān chief (खान = خان).
मिरिका: मिरिका मिरिका, f. a species of plant, (con-nected with इरिका, q. v.)
मिर्मिर: मिर्मिर मिर्मिर, अस्, आ, अम्, (fr. a form मिर् = rt. 1. मिष्), Ved. (according to a commentator) blinking.
मिल्: मिल् मिल् (thought by some to be ori-ginally a Nom. fr. a Prākṛt form मिल्ल = मिश्र), cl. 6. P. A. मिलति, -ते, मिमेल, मि-मिले, मेलितुम्, (generally P.) to unite, be united with, join, accompany; to meet together, come toge-ther; to meet, assemble, associate; to mix, combine, be present at; to be connected with; to meet or fall in with (with inst. or gen. or loc. of the person or with सह and inst.); to find; to meet, encounter, (द्वन्द्व-युद्धेन द्वौ मिलितौ, two persons met in single combat); to clash, impinge, concur; to happen, come to pass: Caus. मेलयति, -यितुम्, to cause to meet, bring together, assemble, convene.
मिलत्: मिलत्, अन्, अती or अन्ती, अत्, joining, accompanying; meeting; assembling; concurring, combining; hap-pening. —मिलद्-व्याध, अस्, आ, अम्, uniting with hunters, accompanied by huntsmen.
मिलन: मिलन, अम्, n. the act of mixing with, coming in contact with, associating with; concurring, en-countering, coalescing, meeting; contact.
मिलित: मिलित, अस्, आ, अम्, united, mixed, combined, connected; found, met, encountered.
मिलित्वा: मिलित्वा, ind. having met together, having united.
मिलिन्: मिलिन्, ई, इनी, इ, mixing with, combined with, provided with, possessing.
मिला: मिला मिला in दुर्-मिला, q. v.
मिलिन्दक: मिलिन्दक मिलिन्दक, अस्, m. a kind of snake.
मिलीमिलिन्: मिलीमिलिन् मिलीमिलिन्, ई, m. an epithet of Śiva (which is said to contain a Mantra addressed to Śiva, consisting of the following eighteen syllables, ॐ, रुद्र चीलि चीलि चिलि चिलि मिलि मिलि, ॐ स्वाहा).
मिल्ला: मिल्ला मिल्ला, f., N. of a woman.
मिश्: मिश् मिश् (connected with rt. मश्), cl. 1. P. मेशति, मेशितुम्, to make a noise, sound; to be angry.
मिशर: मिशर मिशर, N. of a place.
मिशि: मिशि मिशि, इस्, or मिशी, f. Anethum Pan-mori and Anethum Sowa (= मिसि); common anise; Indian spikenard, Nardostachys Jatamansi.
मिशृष: मिशृष मिशृष, N. of a place (also written मिश्रिष).
मिश्र्: मिश्र् मिश्र् or मिस्र् (probably a Nom. fr. मिश्र below), cl. 10. P. मिश्रयति, मिश्रापयति, &c., to mix, mingle, blend, combine, unite, mix with (with inst.); to add; [cf. Gr. μίσγ-ω, μίγ-νυ-μι, ἐ-μίγ-ην, ἐ-μίχθη-ν, μίγ-α, μίγ-δα, μίγ-δην, μιγ-άδες, μίξις: Lat. misc-e-o, mix-tu-s, mis-tu-s, mix-tû-ra, mis-tû-ra, mix-ti-o, mis-ti-o, misc-ellu-s, miscell-âneu-s: Old Germ. miscjan, misk-iu, ‘mix thou:’ Angl. Sax. miscan: Slav. mes-i-ti: Lith. misz-ti; misz-ini-s, ‘a mongrel;’ maisz-y-ti, ‘to mix.’]
मिश्र: मिश्र, अस्, आ, अम्, (thought by some to be fr. a lost rt. मिश्, connected with मिक्ष्, desiderative of rt. 1. मिह्; by others referred to rt. मिश् above), mixed, mingled, blended, joined; mixed or blended with (with inst. or sometimes gen.), combined; associated, connected, (न मिश्रः स्यात् पापकृद्-भिः, one should not associate with the wicked); mixing, adulterating (e. g. mixing or adulterating corn); tangled, intertwined; manifold, diverse; (at the end of a comp.) having a mixture or mixed collection of anything, for the most part consisting of, consisting chiefly of (e. g. बदरी-मिश्रं का-ननम्, a forest consisting for the most part of Badarī trees; आर्य-विदग्ध-मिश्रास्, for the most part worthy and learned persons); (अस्), m. a respect-able person (cf. आर्य-म्°; in this sense frequently used at the end or beginning of a proper name, especially that of a scholar, by way of respect, cf. कृष्ण-म्°, भाव-म्°, मधु-म्°; and some-times used alone as an abbreviation for a name ending in मिश्र, e. g. मिश्र = मण्डन-मिश्र); N. of the author of the Karma-pradīpa and of various other persons; epithet of a kind of elephant; (अम्), n. mixing, mixture; a species of radish (= चाणक्य-मूलक). —मिश्र-केशव, अस्, m., N. of an author (= केशव-दास). —मिश्र-केशी, f., N. of an Apsaras. —मिश्र-चतुर्भुज, अस्, m. a proper N. —मिश्र-ज, अस्, m. ‘of mixed birth or breed,’ a mule. —मिश्र-जाति, इस्, इस्, इ, being of mixed birth or breed, of mixed parentage, any one whose parents belong to different castes. —मिश्र-ता, f. mixedness, the being mixed, mixing, mingling. —मिश्र-दिन-कर, अस्, m., N. of a commentator on the Śiśupāla-badha. —मिश्र-धान्य, अस्, आ, अम्, made by mixing various kinds of grain; (अम्), n. mixed grain. —मि-श्र-पुष्पा, f. Trigonella Fœnum Græcum (= मे-थिका). —मिश्र-भाव, अस्, m., N. of the author of the Bhāva-prakāśa, a medical work, (also भाव, भाव-मिश्र।) —मिश्र-लटकन, अस्, m., N. of the father of Miśra-bhāva. —मिश्र-वर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, being of a mixed colour; (अम्), n. a kind of black aloe wood (= कृष्णागुरु). —मिश्रवर्ण-फला, f. Solanum Melongena. —मिश्र-व्यवहार, अस्, m. (in arithmetic) investigation of mixture, ascertainment of composition (as principal and in-terest joined, &c.). —मिश्र-शब्द, अस्, m. a mule (= मिश्र-ज). —मिश्री-करण, अम्, n. the act of mixing, an ingredient, seasoning. —मिश्री-कृ, cl. 8. -करोति, &c., to make mixed, mix, mingle. —मिश्री-भाव, अस्, m. becoming mixed, mixing, mingling. —मिश्री-भू, cl. 1. P. -भवति, -भवितुम्, to become mixed, mix, intertwine.

मिश्रित: मिश्रित, अस्, आ, अम्, mixed, mingled, blended, united, joined; added; respected, respectable.
मिश्रिन्: मिश्रिन्, ई, m., N. of a Nāga.
मिश्रेया: मिश्रेया, f. (connected with मिशि, q. v.), Anethum Panmori or a species of anise.

मिस्: मिस् मिस्, cl. 4. P. मिस्यति, &c., Ved. to go.

मिहिराण: मिहिराण, अस्, m. an epithet of Śiva.
मीढ: मीढ, अस्, आ, अम्, passed (as urine); urined, watered; (अम्), n., also मीऌह, अम्, n., Ved. a battle, combat, struggle.
मीढ मीढ, मीढ्वस्, मीढुषे, मीऌहुषे, &c. See col. 1.
मीढुष: मीढुष, अस्, m., N. of a son of Indra by Paulomī.
मीढ्वस्: मीढ्वस्, आन्, असी, अस् (the declension follows that of a perf. part., e. g. acc. sing. masc. मीढ्वांसम्, dat. मीढुषे or मीऌहुषे, cf. Mahā-bh. Vana-p. 1628, voc. मिहिलारोप्य: मिहिलारोप्य मिहिलारोप्य, अम्, n., N. of a city in the south of India; [cf. महिलारोप्य।]
मी: मी 1. मी, cl. 9. P. मी 3. मी, cl. 1. 10. P. मयति, माययति, &c., to go, move; to understand, know; [cf. Lat. meare, movere.]
मीत: मीत, अस्, आ, अम्, in प्र-मीत। See प्र-मी।
मीन: मीन, अस्, m. (according to Uṇādi-s. मीनर: मीनर, अस्, m. a kind of sea-monster (= मकर).
मीनाम्रीण: मीनाम्रीण, अस्, m. = दर्दुराम्र, a kind of sauce or condiment, fish-sauce; a wag-tail.
मीडम्: मीडम् मीडम्, ind. in a low tone, softly.
मीम्: मीम् मीम्, cl. 1. P. मीमति, मीमितुम्, cl. 10. P. (or Caus.) मीमयति, -यितुम्, to go, move; to sound; [cf. rt. 2. मा।]
मीमांस: मीमांस मीमांस, Desid. base of rt. मन्, q. v.
मीमांसक: मीमांसक, अस्, m. one who thinks over or reflects deeply upon, one who examines or proves; an examiner, investigator, prover; a follower of the Pūrva-mīmāṃsā system, (see below.)
मीमांसन: मीमांसन, अस्, m. one who examines or proves, a tester, prover, examiner, investigator.
मीमांसा: मीमांसा, f. reflection, consideration, opinion, investigation, examination, discussion, (काव्य-म्°, the theory of poetry, art of poetry; N. of a work); ‘examination (of the sacred text),’ N. of one of three great divisions of orthodox Hindū philosophy (divided like the Nyāya and Sāṅkhya into two systems, viz. the Pūrva-mīmāṃsā or Karma-mīmāṃsā founded by Jaimini, and the Uttara-mīmāṃsā or Brahma-mīmāṃsā or Śārīraka-mīmāṃsā by Bādarāyaṇa, the latter, how-ever, is more commonly called the Vedānta system, while the Pūrva-mīmāṃsā is usually called the Mīmāṃsā; though the Mīmāṃsā by Jaimini is classed among the six orthodox systems of philosophy, it does not concern itself like the others with the nature of soul, mind, and matter, but rather with a correct interpretation of the ritual of the Veda and the solution of doubts and discrepancies in regard to the Vedic texts caused by the discordant explanations of opposite schools; it may therefore be described as a critical commentary on the first or ritual portion of the Veda, and its only claim to the title of a philosophy consists in its philosophical method of interpretation, the topics being arranged according to particular categories, such as authoritativeness, indirect precept, &c., and treated according to a kind of logical sequence, which commences with the proposition to be discussed, the doubt arising about it, the Pūrva-pakṣa or primâ facie and wrong view of the question, the right argument or refuta-tion of the Pūrva-pakṣa, and the conclusion; see, moreover, पूर्व-मीमांसा: Jaimini, whose date is unknown, taught his system in twelve books, each book containing either four or eight chapters, and each chapter being subdivided into sections compris-ing one or more Sūtras; the oldest commentary on these obscure aphorisms being the Bhāṣya of Śabara-svāmin, explained by the great Mīmāṃsā authority Kumārila-svāmin or Kumārila-bhaṭṭa, and again elu-cidated by Mādhavācārya in the Jaiminīya-nyāya-mālā-vistara). —मीमांस-कृत्, त्, m. ‘the author of the Mīmāṃsā system,’ an epithet of Jaimini. —मी-मांसा-कौतूहल-वृत्ति, इस्, f., N. of a commen-tary by Vāsudeva Adhvarin (also called Vāsudeva Dīkṣita) on the Mīmāṃsā-sūtras of Jaimini. —मी-मांसा-कौस्तुभ, अस्, m., N. of a commentary by Khaṇḍa-deva on the Mīmāṃsā-sūtras of Jaimini. —मीमांसा-जीव-रक्षा, f., N. of a Mīmāṃsā work. —मीमांसा-तत्त्व-चन्द्रिका, f., N. of a work by Gopāla-bhaṭṭa on various Mīmāṃsā topics. —मीमांसा-तन्त्र-वार्त्तिक, अम्, n., N. of a com-mentary by Kumārila-svāmin on the Sūtras of Jai-mini. —मीमांसा-नय-विवेक, अस्, m., N. of a commentary by Bhavanātha-miśra on the Mīmāṃsā-sūtras of Jaimini. —मीमांसा-न्याय-प्रकाश, अस्, m., N. of a celebrated elementary work on the Mīmāṃsā system by Āpa-deva (son of Ananta-deva and pupil of Govinda). —मीमांसा-परिभाषा, f., N. of an elementary treatise by Kṛṣṇa-dīkṣita on the Mīmāṃsā. —मीमांसा-भाष्य-विवरण, अम्, n., N. of a commentary by Kumāra-svāmin on a work entitled Mīmāṃsā-bhāṣya. —मीमांसार्थ-प्रदीप (°सा-अर्°), अस्, m., N. of a disquisition by Śaṅkara-śukla on the provableness of the Veda. —मी-मांसा-विधि-भूषण, अम्, n., N. of a Mīmāṃsā work by Gopāla-bhaṭṭa, written in refutation of the Vidhi-rasāyana. —मीमांसा-शिरोमणि, इस्, m. ‘crest-gem of the Mīmāṃsā,’ epithet of an author, (also called Nīla-kaṇṭha.) —मीमांसा-सर्वस्व, अम्, n., N. of a work by Halāyudha. —मीमांसा-सूत्र, अम्, n., N. of the twelve books of aphorisms by Jaimini on the interpretation of the Veda; see मीमांसा, col. 2. —मीमांसा-स्तवक, अस्, m., N. of a Mīmāṃsā work by Rāghavānanda.

मीव्: मीव् 1. मीव्, cl. 1. P. मीवति, मीवितुम्, to move.
मीव् 2. मीव् (connected with rt. पीव्), cl. 1. P. मीवति, मीवितुम्, to grow fat, to be large or corpulent.
मूत: 1. मूत, अस्, आ, अम् (for 2. see rt. 1. मू), moved, in काम-मूत, q. v.

2. मूत, अस्, आ, अम् (for 1. see rt. 1. मीव्), bound, tied; woven; (अस्, अम्), m. n., Ved. a woven basket; a woven band of cloth or fillet. —मूत-कार्य, अस्, आ, अम्, consisting of plaited work or basket work.
मूत 1. and 2. मूत। See under rt. 1. मीव् and rt. 1. मू।
मीवग: मीवग मीवग, (with Buddhists) a parti-cular high number.
मीवर: मीवर मीवर, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. rt. 1. मी), hurting, killing, hurtful, injurious, mischievous; vene-rable, worthy of esteem; (अस्), m. a general, leader of an army.
मीवा: मीवा मीवा, f. (probably fr. 2. मी; said to be fr. 1. मी), the tape-worm, a worm generated in the intestines, Ascarides; air, wind, (in this sense also, according to some, मीवन्, आ, m.); = शीकर (?); = सार (?)।
मु: मु मु, उस्, m. (fr. rt. 1. मू, q. v.), a bond, binding, confinement; an epithet of Śiva; final emancipation; a funeral pile; a reddish brown or tawny colour.
मुंसल: मुंसल मुंसल, N. of a place.
मुकन्दक: मुकन्दक मुकन्दक, अस्, m. probably an error for सु-कन्दक, an onion.

मुकु: मुकु मुकु, उस्, m. = मुक्ति, liberation; (an artificial word, formed fr. rt. 2. मुच्, to explain मु-कुन्-द, q. v., for which purpose others assume मु-कुम्, ind.)
मुकुट: मुकुट मुकुट, अम्, n. a tiara, diadem, crown (said to be crescent-shaped; the किरीट being pointed, and the मौलि having three points); a crest; a peak, point, head [cf. त्रि-म्°]; N. of a place; (अस्), m. a proper N. मुकुटिन्: मुकुटिन्, ई, इनी, इ, crowned, wearing a diadem.
मुकुट्ट: मुकुट्ट मुकुट्ट, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people; (also read सुकुट्ट।)
मुकुण्टी: मुकुण्टी मुकुण्टी, f. a kind of weapon; (perhaps an error for सु-कुण्ठी।)
मुकुन्द: मुकुन्द मुकुन्-द, अस्, m. (according to an artificial etymology, fr. मुकु, q. v., मुकुन्-द being said to mean ‘giver of liberation’), N. of Viṣṇu (sometimes transferred to Śiva); of a parti-cular treasure; a kind of precious stone; quicksilver; the resin of Boswellia Thurifera, gum olibanum; a kind of drum or kettle-drum; N. of various learned men (= गोविन्द, वाराहताजिक-मुकुन्द, मु-कुन्द-पण्डित); N. of a mountain. —मुकुन्द-देव, अस्, m., N. of various princes of Orissa (= वीर-म्°). —मुकुन्द-प्रिय, अस्, m., N. of a certain teacher; of the father of the commentator Rāmā-nanda. —मुकुन्द-भट्ट, अस्, m. a proper N. —मुकुन्द-माला, f. ‘Mukunda-garland,’ N. of a prayer in twenty-two verses addressed to Mukunda (Viṣṇu). —मुकुन्द-मिश्र, अस्, m., N. of a Brāhman. —मुकुन्द-मुनि, इस्, or मुकुन्द-राज, अस्, m. a proper N. —मुकुन्द-राम, अस्, m. a proper N. —मुकुन्द-शर्मन्, आ, m., N. of a scribe.
मुकुन्दक: मुकुन्दक, अस्, m. a species of grain reckoned among the Ku-dhānyas; an onion (= सु-कुन्दक, सु-कन्दक; cf. मुकन्दक).
मुकुन्दु: मुकुन्दु, उस्, m. = मुकुन्द, the resin of Bos-wellia Thurifera; gum olibanum.
मुकुम्: मुकुम् मुकुम्, ind. See मुकु, col. 1.
मुकुर: मुकुर मुकुर, अस्, m. a mirror (= मकुर; cf. कर्ण-मुकुर, मति-म्°); the stick or handle of a potter's wheel; Mimusops Elengi; Jasminum Zambac (= कुल-वृक्ष); a bud (= मुकुल below).
मुकुरित: मुकुरित, अस्, आ, अम्, (probably) = मुकुलित below; see Gaṇa Tārakādi to Pāṇ. V. 2, 31.
मुकुल: मुकुल मुकुल, अस्, अम्, m. n. (perhaps con-nected with rt. 2. मुच्), a bud, opening bud or calyx of a flower, (in these senses also written म-कुल, q. v.); anything shaped like a bud, (दशन-म्°, a bud-like tooth); a bud-like junction or bring-ing together of the fingers of the hand, (in this sense only अस्, m.); the body; the soul or spirit; N. of a king; of another person; (अम्), n. a kind of metre, four times ¯ ¯ ¯ ˘ ˘ ¯. —मुकुलाग्र (°ल-अग्°), अम्, n. a particular surgical instrument with a bud-like point. —मुकुली-कृ, cl. 8. मुकुलय: मुकुलय, Nom. P. मुकुलयति, &c., to close, cause to close (the eyes, &c.).
मुकुलित: मुकुलित, अस्, आ, अम्, budded, having buds, blos-soming, full of blossoms; closed like a bud, half closed; half shut (as the eye), blinking, winking; closed, shut. —मुकुलिताक्ष (°त-अक्°), अस्, ई, अम्, having half closed eyes.
मुकुलिन्: मुकुलिन्, ई, इनी, इ, budding, budded, having buds.
मुकुष्ठ: मुकुष्ठ मुकुष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, = मन्थर; (अस्), m. a species of bean; [cf. मकुष्ठ।]
मुकुष्ठक: मुकुष्ठक, अस्, m. a species of bean.
मुकूलक: मुकूलक मुकूलक, अस्, m. = मकूलक, a species of plant (commonly Danti).
मुक्त: मुक्त मुक्त, मुक्ति, &c. See p. 782, col. 3, and p. 783, col. 2.

मुक्त, अस्, आ, अम्, loosened, loosed, let loose, set free, relaxed, (मुक्तैर् अवयवैः, with loos-ened or relaxed limbs); unloosed, opened, open [cf. मुक्त-हस्त]; redeemed, released, extricated, libe-rated, emancipated (from sin or from worldly exist-ence), finally happy, saved; abandoned, relinquished, quitted, left, put off, laid aside; given up; bestowed, granted, given; discharged, emitted, shed, thrown, cast, hurled, darted, shot, sent, sent forth, poured forth, (वर्णोदकैः काञ्चन-शृङ्ग-मुक्तैः, with coloured waters poured forth from golden vials); ejected, spit out; fallen; deprived; (अस्), m., N. of one of the seven sages under Manu Bhautya; N. of a cook in Rāja-taraṅgiṇī VII. 1635, &c.; (आ), f., scil. दिश्, the quarter just quitted by the sun (e. g. if the sun be in the south, the south is said to be प्राप्तार्का, and the south-east मुक्ता); a pearl (as loosened or set free from the pearl-oyster shell); a courtezan, harlot; a species of plant, = रास्ना; (अम्), n. the spirit released from corporeal existence. —मुक्त-कच्छ, अस्, आ, अम्, letting the hem of the lower garment hang down or leaving it loose and untucked; (अस्), m. a Buddhist. —मुक्त-कञ्-चुक, अस्, m. a snake that has cast its slough. —मुक्त-कण्ठ, अस्, आ, or ई, अम्, having a loos-ened or free throat, raising a cry, shrill; (अम्), ind. aloud. —मुक्त-कर, अस्, आ, or ई, अम्, open-handed, liberal, bountiful. —मुक्त-केश, अस्, आ, or ई, अम्, ‘loose-haired,’ having flowing hair, having the hair dishevelled or hanging down. —मुक्त-चक्षुस्, उस्, उस्, उस्, having the eyes opened; hissing. —मुक्त-बन्धन, अस्, आ, अम्, released from bonds, freed from fetters. —मुक्त-बुद्धि, इस्, इस्, इ, one whose soul is liberated, emancipated. —मुक्त-मण्डूक-कण्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, having frogs croaking loudly (lit. with loosened throats). —मुक्त-मूर्धज, अस्, आ, अम्, = मुक्त-केश, q. v. —मुक्त-रोधो-नितम्ब, अस्, आ, अम्, quitting the hip-like bank. —मुक्त-रोष, अस्, आ, अम्, one who has laid aside or relinquished anger. —मुक्त-लज्ज, अस्, आ, अम्, casting away shame. —मुक्त-वसन, अस्, आ, अम्, one who has put off his clothes, going about naked; (अस्), m. an epithet of a Jaina ascetic. —मुक्त-व्यापार, अस्, आ, अम्, one who has re-signed an office or occupation. —मुक्त-संशय, अस्, आ, अम्, free from doubt, certain. —मुक्त-सङ्ग, अस्, आ, अम्, free from worldly or selfish attachment, disinterested. —मुक्त-स्वामिन्, ई, m. ‘lord of eman-cipation,’ N. of a statue erected by a king (Rāja-taraṅgiṇī IV. 188). —मुक्त-हस्त, अस्, आ, अम्, open-handed, liberal, easily parting with possessions, giving away, profuse; loosed, let go. —मुक्ता-कण, अस्, m. (for मुक्ता-कर्ण), a proper N. —मुक्ता-कलाप, अस्, m. an ornament made of strings of pearls, pearl necklace. —मुक्ताकार (°ता-आक्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having the look or appearance of a pearl. —मुक्ताकार-ता, f. the form of a pearl, likeness to a pearl. —मुक्ता-केशव, अस्, m., N. of a statue of Kṛṣṇa. —मुक्तागार (°ता-अग्°) or -आग्°), अम्, n. ‘pearl-abode,’ the pearl-oyster. —मुक्ता-गुण, अस्, m. a string of pearls; the excellence of a pearl, lustre or water of a pearl. —मुक्ता-जाल, अम्, n. an orna-ment of pearls, a string or multitude of pearls, a pearly zone; [cf. मुक्ता-फल-जाल।] —मुक्ता-जाल-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, made or consisting of pearls. —मुक्तात्मन् (°त-आत्°), आ, m. the emancipated soul, the soul released from matter; (आ, आ, अ), one whose soul is liberated, emancipated. —मुक्ता-दा-मन्, आ, m. a string of pearls. —मुक्ता-पटल, अम्, n. a mass of pearls. —मुक्तापीड (°त-आप्°), अस्, m., N. of a king; of a poet. —मुक्ता-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a mythical city in the Himālaya moun-tains. —मुक्ता-पुष्प, अस्, m. Jasminum Multi-florum or Pubescens. —मुक्ता-प्रसू, ऊस्, f. ‘pearl-bearing,’ mother of pearl, the pearl-oyster; [cf. मुक्ता-मातृ, मौक्तिक-प्रसवा।] —मुक्ता-प्रा-लम्ब, अस्, m. a string of pearls, pearl ornament, (also read मुक्ता-प्रलम्ब।) —मुक्ता-फल, अम्, n. a pearl; a species of flower; the fruit of the Lavalī plant, the custard apple; camphor; title of a work by Vopa-deva; N. of a king of the Śavaras. —मु-क्ताफल-केतु, उस्, m., N. of a king of the Vidyā-dharas. —मुक्ताफल-जाल, अम्, n. = मुक्ता-जाल। —मुक्ताफल-ध्वज, अस्, m., N. of a king. —मुक्ताफल-परीक्षा, f., N. of the eighty-first Adhyāya in the Varāha-brāhmaṇa-saṃhitā. —मुक्ता-फल-लता, f. a string of pearls; [cf. मुक्ता-लता।] —मुक्ता-मणि, इस्, m. ‘pearl-gem,’ a pearl; [cf. मुक्ता-रत्न।] —मुक्ता-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, made or consisting of pearls, pearly. —मुक्ता-मातृ, ता, f. mother of pearl, a pearl-oyster; [cf. मुक्ता-प्रसू।] —मुक्तामुक्त (°त-अम्°), अस्, आ, अम्, loosed and not loosed (applied especially to weapons which may be wielded or hurled, as clubs, javelins, &c.). —मु-क्ताम्बर (°त-अम्°), अस्, आ, अम्, one who has put off his clothes, naked; N. of various works; of a dictionary; of a commentary on the Megha-dūta; of the wife of Candra-ketu. —मुक्तावली-प्रकाश, अस्, m., N. of a commentary by Dinakara-bhaṭṭa on the Nyāya-siddhānta-muktāvalī;
