मुक्षीजा: मुक्षीजा मुक्षीजा, f. a net, snare.
मुख: मुख मुख, अम्, n. (said in Uṇādi-s. V. 20. to be fr. rt. खन्, to dig, with the final rejected and मु prefixed), the mouth; the face, countenance, (in this sense often at the end of comps., e. g. भ्रू-कुटी-मुख, a frowning face; especially at the end of adj. comps. when the fem. is generally मुखी, e. g. सकलेन्दु-मुखी, a woman with a full moon-like face; cf. अश्रु-म्°); the beak of a bird, snout or muzzle of any animal, (in these senses said to be also अस्, m.); a direction, quarter, (in this sense also often at the end of comps., e. g. आशा-मुख, दिङ्-मुख, quarter or region of space; अन्तर्-मुखम्, ind. in the direction of or towards the interior; and more frequently at the end of adj. comps. in the sense of ‘looking towards, facing,’ when the fem. is generally -मुखी, cf. उभयतो-म्°, अधो-म्°, उदङ्-म्°; मख-मुख, going to the sacrifice); opening, aperture, mouth of a vessel, &c.; entrance, egress (e. g. विन्ध्याटवी-मुखे, at the entrance of the Vindhya forest; स्वर्गस्य मुखम्, the entrance into heaven); the entrance to a house; the mouth or embouchure of a river; the fore part, front, van (of an army), head, top; the head, tip or point of anything, (स्तन-मुख, the tip or nipple of the breast; अङ्गुली-मुख, the tip of the finger; शर-मुख, the point of an arrow); the edge of any sharp instrument; surface, upper side (e. g. विष-कुम्भम् पयो-मुखम्, a vessel of poison with milk on the surface); the chief, principal, best, most excellent (e. g. नक्षत्राणाम् मुखं चन्-द्रः, the moon is chief of the Nakṣatras); intro-duction, beginning, commencement, (often at the end of comps. when the fem. is -मुखा or -मुखी, but oftener the latter, e. g. गङ्गा-मुखीनां or गङ्गा-मुखानां सरिताम्, of the rivers beginning with the Ganges; महा-रथा जयद्रथ-मुखाः, the heroes beginning with Jayad-ratha, i. e. Jayad-ratha and the other heroes; cf. the use of आदि); the opening or previous incidents of a drama, the original cause or source of the action, the first act; (in algebra) the first term, the intial quantity of the progression; the apex or side opposite to the base of a mathematical figure; source, cause, occasion, ground; means, expedient; scripture, the Veda; sound (?); Artocarpus Locucha or Lakuca, (in this sense अस्, m.); (एन), ind. with reference to, according to. —मुख-कमल, अम्, n. ‘face-lotus,’ a lotus-like face. —मुख-खुर, अस्, m. ‘mouth-razor,’ a tooth. —मुख-गन्धक, अस्, m. ‘mouth-scent-ing,’ an onion. —मुख-घण्टा, f. ‘mouth-bell,’ a particular sound made with the mouth (= हुल-हुली). —मुख-चन्द्र, अस्, m. ‘face-moon,’ a moon-like face, lovely face. —मुख-चपल, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘one whose mouth is ever moving,’ talkative, loquacious, garrulous; (आ), f. a kind of Āryā metre. —मुख-चपेटिका, f. a slap on the face, box on the ear; [cf. दुर्जन-म्°।] —मुख-चीरी, f. the tongue. —मुख-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, produced from or in the mouth; (अस्), m. ‘mouth-born,’ a Brāhman, (so called as being sprung from the mouth of Brahmā; cf. Manu 1. 31.) —मुख-जाह, अम्, n. the root or point of issue of the mouth, the top of the pharynx. —१। मुख-तस्, ind. from or out of or at the mouth, in the mouth, in the face; at the head, in the front. —२। मुख-तस् = मुखे तस्यति, see Scholiast on Pāṇ. III. 4, 61. —मुख-दघ्न, अस्, ई, अम्, reaching to the mouth. —मुख-दू-षण, अस्, m. ‘mouth-defiler,’ an onion. —मुख-दूषिका, f. ‘face-disfiguring,’ an eruption which dis-figures the face of young people. —मुख-धौता, f. a plant, Clerodendrum Siphonanthus. —मुख-नासिक, अम्, n. the mouth and nose. —मुख-निरीक्षक, अस्, m. ‘face-gazer,’ an idler, lazy person. —मुख-निवासिनी, f. ‘dwelling in the mouth,’ an epithet of Saravatī. —मुख-पट, अस्, m. ‘face-cloth,’ a veil. —मुख-पाक, अस्, m. in-flammation of the mouth. —मुख-पिण्ड, अस्, m. a lump or piece of food in the mouth, mouthful of food. —मुख-पूरण, अम्, n. filling the mouth, a mouthful of water, a mouthful in general. —मु-ख-प्रतिमुख, speech and reply (?). —मुख-प्रसाद, अस्, m. the light of the countenance, graciousness of aspect. —मुख-प्रिय, अस्, आ, अम्, pleasant in the mouth; (अस्), m. an orange. —मु-ख-प्रेक्ष, अस्, आ, अम्, or मुख-प्रेक्षिन्, ई, इणी, इ, observing or watching the face (to detect any one's intentions). —मुख-बन्ध, अस्, m. a preface. —मुख-बन्धन, अम्, n. ‘mouth-bind-ing,’ the fastening of an aperture, a lid, cover; an introduction, preface. —मुख-बहूरु-पज्-ज (°हु-ऊर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, sprung from the mouth, arm, thigh, and foot (Manu. 1. 87). —मुख-बाहूरु-पाद-तस् (°हु-ऊर्°), ind. from the mouth, arms, thighs, and feet. —मुख-भूषण, अम्, n. ‘mouth-ornament,’ betel; tin (?). —मुख-भेद, अस्, m. distortion of the face. —मुख-मण्डनक, अस्, m. a species of tree (= तिलक). —मुख-मण्डल, अम्, n. ‘face-orb,’ the face, countenance. —मुख-मण्-डिका, f. a particular disease or the deity presiding over it; (also read मुख-मण्डिनिका।) —मुख-मण्डी, f., N. of one of the Mātṛs attending on Skanda. —मुख-माधुर्य, अम्, n. a particular disease of the phlegm. —मुख-मार्जन, अम्, n. washing or cleansing the mouth (after meals, &c.). —मुख-मोद, अस्, m. Hyperanthera Moringa. —मुखम्-पच, अस्, m. a beggar. —मुख-यन्त्रण, अम्, n. ‘mouth-curb,’ the bit of a bridle. —मुख-राग, अस्, m. colour of the face. —मुख-रुज्, क्, f. or मुख-रोग, अस्, m. ‘mouth-disease,’ any disease of the mouth. —मुखरोगिक, अस्, आ, अम्, relating to mouth-disease. —मुख-रोगिन्, ई, इणी, इ, diseased in the mouth. —मुख-लाङ्गल, अस्, m. ‘using the snout for a plough,’ a hog. —मुख-लेप, अस्, m. anointing the face, anointing the upper side (of a drum); a disease of the phlegmatic humor; [cf. आस्यो-पलेप] —मुख-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, possessing a mouth, having a mouth. —मुख-वल्लभ, अस्, m. a pomegranate tree. —मुख-वाटिका, f. a species of plant (= अम्ब-ष्ठा). —मुख-वाद्य, अम्, n. a wind-instrument, any instrument of music sounded with the mouth; (in the worship of Śiva) a kind of musical sound made with the mouth (by striking it with the hand). —मुख-वास or मुख-वासन, अस्, m. ‘mouth-perfume,’ a perfume used to scent the breath; fragrant grass (= गन्ध-त्रिण). —मु-ख-विपुला, f. a kind of Āryā metre. —मुख-विलुण्ठिका, f. a she-goat. —मुख-विष्ठा, f. a species of cockroach. —मुख-व्यादान, अम्, n. the act of opening the mouth wide, gaping. —मु-ख-शफ, अस्, आ, अम्, foul-mouthed, scurrilous. —मुख-शुद्धि, इस्, f. cleanness of the face or mouth, cleansing or purifying the mouth (as by eating betel-nut, &c.). —मुख-शेष, अस्, आ, अम्, having only the face left; (अस्), m. an epithet of Rāhu. —मुख-शोधन, अस्, ई, अम्, ‘mouth-cleansing,’ cleansing the mouth; sharp, pungent; (अस्), m. pungency, sharp or pungent flavour; (अम्), n. the cleansing of the mouth; cinnamon. —मुख-शोधिन्, ई, इनी, इ, cleansing the mouth; (ई), m. a lime or citron, citron tree. —मुख-शोष, अस्, m. dryness of the mouth. —मुख-शोषिन्, ई, इणी, इ, suffering from dryness of the mouth. —मुख-श्री, ईस्, f. beauty of countenance, a beautiful face. —मु-ख-ष्ठील, अस्, आ, अम् (probably for मुखा-ष्ठील), = मुख-शफ. —मुख-सम्भव, अस्, m. ‘mouth-born,’ a Brāhman; [cf. मुख-ज।], —मुख-सुख, अम्, n. ‘ease of pronunciation,’ causing ease of pronunciation or facility of utterance. —मुख-सुर, अम्, n. ‘lip-nectar,’ the moisture of the lips. —मुख-स्राव, अस्, m. flow of saliva, salivation, saliva. —मुखाकार (°ख-आक्°), अस्, m. ‘form of the countenance,’ mien, look, appearance. —मुखाग्नि (°ख-अग्°), इस्, m. a forest conflagra-tion; a sort of goblin with a face of fire; fire put into the mouth of a corpse at the time of lighting the funeral pile; a sacrificial or consecrated fire; [cf. मुखोल्का।] —मुखाग्र (°ख-अग्°), अम्, n. the extremity of the mouth, extremity. —मुखानिल (°ख-अन्°), अस्, m. ‘mouth-wind,’ wind of the mouth, breath. —मुखामय (°ख-आम्°), अस्, m. disease of the mouth. —मुखामृत (°ख-अम्°), अम्, n. the nectar of the mouth or countenance, (a term used in flattering addresses.) —मुखार्चिस् (°ख-अर्°), इस्, n. ‘mouth-flame,’ hot breath (?). —मुखार्जक (°ख-अर्°), अस्, m. a species of plant (= अर्जक). —मु-खासव (°ख-आस्°), अस्, m. ‘lip-moisture,’ nectar of the lips. —मुखास्त्र (°ख-अस्°), अस्, m. ‘mouth-armed,’ a crab. —मुखास्राव (°ख-आस्°), अस्, m. = mukha-srāva. —मुखी-भू, cl. 1. P. -भवति, -भवितुम्, see Scholiast on Pāṇ. III. 4, 61. —मु-खेन्दु (°ख-इन्°), उस्, m. a moon-like face, beau-tiful face. —मुखे-भव, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. formed in the mouth. —मुखोत्कीर्ण (°ख-उत्°), अस्, m. a proper N. —मुखोल्का (°ख-उल्°), f. = मुखाग्नि, a forest fire.
मुखतीय: मुखतीय, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. 1. मुख-तस्; cf. पार्श्वतीय), being in the mouth or in the front.
मुखर: मुखर, अस्, आ, अम्, talkative, loquacious, gar-rulous, noisy, making any continuous or tedious sound (said of birds and bees and tinkling orna-ments, cf. उन्-म्°); sounding, resonant or resound-ing with (at the end of a comp., e. g. प्रतिश्रुन्-मुखर, resonant with echoes); expressive of, (अवर्ण-मुखरा गिरः, voices expressive of re-proach); foul-mouthed, scurrilous, speaking harshly or abusively; ridiculing, mocking; (अस्), m. a crow; a conch shell; a leader, principal, chief, ringleader; N. of a Nāga; (ई), f. the bit of a bridle. —मु-खर-ता, f. talkativeness, garrulity, noisiness. —मु-खरी-करण, अम्, n. making resonant, speaking harshly, rallying, mocking. —मुखरी-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, -कर्तुम्, to make resonant, cause to resound.
मुखरक: मुखरक, अस्, m. a proper N.; (इका), f. = मुखरी, the bit of a bridle; talking, conversation.
मुखरय: मुखरय, Nom. P. मुखरयति, -यितुम्, to make noisy or resonant; to notify, declare.
मुखरित: मुखरित, अस्, आ, अम्, rendered noisy, made resonant, sounding, ringing.
मुखीय: मुखीय, अस्, आ, अम्, (at the end of a comp.) being at the top or head, being foremost, being at the entrance.
मुख्य: मुख्य, अस्, आ, अम्, being in or on the mouth or face; belonging to the mouth or face, coming from the mouth, &c.; being at the head or at the begin-ning, principal, chief, prime, primary, original, first, eminent, pre-eminent, first-rate, most excellent or important, original; (at the end of a comp.) the chief, most excellent among, first or best of (cf. द्विजाति-म्°, द्विज-म्°, मन्त्रि-म्°, वार-मुख्या; sometimes even used like आदि, e. g. नारायणी-मुख्यम् मातृ-चक्रम्, the whole circle of Mātṛs beginning with Nārāyaṇī); (अस्), m. a leader, guide; N. of a tutelary deity presiding over one part of an astrological house which is divided into 81 or 63 divisions or Padas; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a class of gods under Manu Sārvaṇi; (अम्), n. a principal or essential rite, chief ordinance; reading or teaching the Vedas; the month reckoned from new moon to new moon. —मुख्य-चान्द्र, the principal lunar month which ends with the conjunction (as opposed to the गौण-चान्द्र or secondary lunar month which ends with the opposition). —मुख्य-तस्, ind. principally, chiefly, particularly, especially, par excellence. —मुख्य-ता, f. or मुख्य-त्व, अम्, n. pre-eminence, the being best or chief, principal-ness, primacy, highest rank or position. —मुख्य-नृप, अस्, or मुख्य-राज्, ट्, m. a paramount sovereign, reigning monarch. —मुख्यमन्त्रि-ता, f. the office or rank of prime minister. —मुख्य-मन्त्रिन्, ई, m. a prime minister, chief councillor; [cf. मन्त्रि-मुख्य।] —मुख्य-शस्, ind. princi-pally, particularly, chiefly, before all, next. —मु-ख्यार्थ (°य-अर्°), अस्, m. primary meaning (of a word, as opposed to its गौणार्थ or secondary or metaphorical meaning), original sense, first signifi-cation; (अस्, आ, अम्), employed in or having the original sense.
मुखण्डी: मुखण्डी मुखण्डी, or मुखुण्डी, f. a kind of weapon.
मुखुली: मुखुली मुखुली, f., N. of a Buddhist goddess.
मुगदस: मुगदस मुगदस, मुगदेमु, मुगल-स्था-न, names of places.
मुगूह: मुगूह मुगूह, अस्, m. a species of gallinule (= दात्यूह).
मुग्ध: मुग्ध मुग्ध, &c. See under rt. 1. मुह्।

मुग्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, stupefied, perplexed, stupid, ignorant; infatuated, enamoured; foolish, silly, sim-ple, mistaken, erring; inexperienced, artless, inno-cent, rendered attractive by youthful simplicity, charming, tender, lovely, beautiful; (आ), f. a young and beautiful female. —मुग्ध-कथा, f. a story of a fool, tale about a fool. —मुग्ध-ता, f. or मुग्ध-त्व, अम्, n. stupidity, silliness, ignorance; simplicity, artlessness, loveliness, charmingness, grace-fulness. —मुग्ध-दृश्, क्, क्, क्, lovely-eyed, hav-ing beautiful eyes. —मुग्ध-धी, ईस्, ईस्, इ, or मुग्ध-बुद्धि, इस्, इस्, इ, silly, simple, a simpleton. —मुग्ध-बोध, अम्, n. ‘instructing the igno-rant’ (scil. व्याकरण), N. of a celebrated grammar by Vopa-deva (a grammarian who is supposed to have flourished in the thirteenth century, and who is regarded as a great authority in Bengal). —मुग्ध-बोध-परिशिष्ट, अम्, n. a supplement or appendix to the Mugdha-bodha. —मुग्धबोध-प्रदीप, अस्, m., N. of a commentary on the Mugdha-bodha. —मुग्धबोध-सम्बोधिनी, f., N. of a com-mentary on the Mugdha-bodha. —मुग्ध-बोधिनी, f., scil. टीका, N. of a commentary by Bharata-malla on the Amara-koṣa and of a commentary by Bha-rata-mallika (probably identical with the preceding author) on the Bhaṭṭi-kāvya. —मुग्ध-भाव, अस्, m. stupidity, simplicity, inexperience. —मुग्ध-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, perplexed, embarrassed, infatuated, mistaken. —मुग्धाक्षी (°ध-अक्°), f. a lovely-eyed woman. —मुग्धाग्रणी (°ध-अग्°), ईस्, m. the greatest of simpletons, the stupidest of the stupid. —मुग्धा-चक्र, अम्, n. a particular mystical circle. —मुग्धानन (°ध-आन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, lovely-faced.
मुङ्ग: मुङ्ग मुङ्ग, अस्, m. a proper N.
मुङ्गट: मुङ्गट, अस्, m. a proper N.
मुच्: मुच् 1. मुच् [cf. rt. मुञ्च्], cl. 1. A. मो-चते, मोचितुम्, = rt. मच्, q. v., to cheat, &c.

मुच् 2. मुच्, cl. 6. P. A. मुञ्चति, -ते, मुमोच, मुमुचे, मोक्ष्यति, -ते, अमु-चत्, अमुक्त (Vedic forms मुचन्ति, मुञ्चातु, मुमुच्रे, मुमोक्तु, मुमुगधि, मा मौक् = मा मुञ्च in Vājasaneyi-s. 1. 25, अमुमुक्तम्, मुमोचत, मुमोचति, मुमोचतम्, मुक्षत), मोक्तुम्, to loose, loosen, let loose, free, let go, release, liberate, (कण्ठम् मुञ्चति, he loosens his throat or voice, i. e. raises a cry; वनाय धेनुम् मुमोच, he let the cow go into the wood; प्राणान् मुच्, to let loose the breath of life, i. e. to deprive of life, kill); to set free, unloose, open; to let go, relinquish, abandon, forsake, leave, quit, put off, shake off, lay aside, give up, (देहम् मुञ्चति, he quits the body, i. e. dies; मुच्यतां विषादः, let despondency be shaken off); to give up, grant, bestow; to sacrifice; to set on one side, take away, set apart, except; to let go, discharge, emit, effuse, shed, send forth, send, throw, cast, fling, hurt, shoot, (वाणमयं वर्षम् मुमोच, he discharged a shower of arrows; इन्द्रो वज्रम् मोक्ष्यते, Indra will hurl his thunderbolt; कूटाद् आत्मानम् मुमोच, he threw himself down from a peak); to send away, dismiss; to spit out; to void; to emit sounds, utter; to put on (A.): Pass. मुच्यते (ep. also मुच्यति, 2nd Fut. मोक्ष्यति), to be loosed, to be let loose or set free, to be released from (with abl. or some-times with inst., e. g. मुच्यते पातकैः, he is loosed from sins); to become loose, free or deliver one's self, escape, (यद्य् एतेभ्यो मुच्यसे, if thou deliver thyself from these men; न मे मोक्ष्यति जीवन्, he shall not escape from me alive); to abandon, to deviate or go astray from, (यदि धर्माद् न मुच्यते, if he go not astray from virtue): Caus. मोचयति, -ते, Aor. अमूमुचत्, मोचयितुम्, to cause to loose, cause to be liberated, cause to let go, cause to shed; to loose, unloose, set loose or free, set at large, liberate; to open (a road); to redeem from (with abl., Manu III. 37); to unyoke, unhar-ness, (अश्वान् मोचयति, he unyokes the horses); to let go, give away, bestow; to cause to give up or let go or discharge or shed; to gladden, delight, rejoice, yield enjoyment: Desid. of Caus. मुमोच-यिषति, Ved. to wish or intend to liberate, desire to be freed from (the bondage of existence, &c.): Desid. मुमुक्षति, -ते, to wish or be about to set free or let go or give up; to wish or be about to hurl, wish to cast, (वज्रम् मुमुक्षन्, being about to hurl a thunderbolt); to wish to free one's self or get loose; to desire final liberation or beati-tude [cf. rt. मोक्ष्, मोक्ष]: Intens. मोमोक्ति, मोमुच्यते; [cf. Gr. μύσσ-ω, μῦκ-ος, μυκτήρ, ἀπομυκτίζω, μύξα, Μυκάλη (?), Μυκήνη (?), μύξινος: Lat. mung-o, mucu-s, mûcêre, mûcor, mûcêdo: Slav. mok-na-ti, ‘to be wet;’ moc†iti, ‘to wet.’]

3. मुच्, क्, क्, क्, (at the end of a comp.) freeing or delivering from [cf. अंहो-म्°]; discharging, drop-ping, letting fall, emitting, throwing, shooting, sending, (शर-वृष्टि-मुच्, discharging showers of arrows; जल-लव-मुच्, letting fall drops of rain; cf. अ-म्°, जल-म्°, तोय-म्°, पयो-म्°, पर्ण-म्°।)
मुक्तक: मुक्तक, अस्, आ, अम्, detached, separate, inde-pendent; (अम्), n. a missile, any missile weapon; a separate or detached Śloka the meaning of which is complete in itself; simple prose (freed from all compound words); a kind of metre.
मुक्ति: मुक्ति, इस्, f. loosing, release, deliverance, liberation, setting free, becoming free, freedom, emancipation (e. g. दासत्व-मुक्ति, release from servitude; cf. शाप-म्°); final liberation or emancipation, final beatitude, the delivery of the soul from the body and exemption from further transmigration, the re-absorption of the Jīvātman into the Paramātman or Supreme Soul of the universe; unloosing, opening; abandonment, putting off, giving up, leaving off; discharging (rain, a missile, &c.); throwing, casting, flinging, hurling, shooting, sending; discharge (of a debt, cf. ऋन-म्°); N. of a divine being, the wife of Satya. —मुक्ति-क्षेत्र, अम्, n. a place where final emancipation is attainable; N. of a sacred place. —मुक्ति-ग्रन्थ, अस्, m. a book of precepts for the attainment of final emancipation. —मुक्ति-चिन्-तामणि-माहात्म्य, अस्, m., N. of a work. —मुक्ति-पति, इस्, m. lord of bliss or beatitude. —मुक्ति-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a Dvīpa. —मुक्ति-मण्डप, अस्, m., N. of a temple. —मुक्ति-मती, f., N. of a river, (also read भुक्ति-मती and शुक्ति-मती।) —मुक्ति-मार्ग, अस्, m. the way of liberation, path to final emancipation. —मुक्ति-मुक्त, अस्, m. incense, frank-incense. —मुक्ति-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having freedom, freed from (with abl.). —मुक्ति-वाद, अस्, m., N. of a work. —मुक्ति-विचार, अस्, m., N. of a philoso-phical work. —मुक्ति-सेन, अस्, m. a proper N.
मुक्तिका: मुक्तिका, f., N. of an Upaniṣad.
मुक्त्वा: मुक्त्वा, ind. having loosed or freed or let go, (मु-क्त्वा हासम्, having broken out into loud laughter); having left or abandoned, having resigned; having put on one side, having excepted, excepting, except, (युद्धम् मुक्त्वा नान्यद् अस्ति मे, except a battle there is nothing else for me); having discharged or shed, having thrown or flung.
मुच: मुच, अस्, ई, अम्, in नख-मुच and अ-मुची, q. v.
मुचिर: मुचिर, अस्, आ, अम्, liberal, munificent, generous [cf. मुक्त-हस्त]; (अस्), m. virtue; wind; a deity.
मुच्यमान: मुच्यमान, अस्, आ, अम्, being freed or released, being abandoned by.
मुञ्चत्: मुञ्चत्, अन्, अती, or अन्ती, अत्, or मुञ्चान, अस्, आ, अम्, loosing, freeing; giving up, relinquishing; dis-charging, shooting, casting, shedding.
मुमुक्षत्: मुमुक्षत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, desiring emancipation.
मुमुक्षा: मुमुक्षा, f. desire of liberation or final eman-cipation.
मुमुक्षा मुमुक्षा, मुमुक्षु। See p. 783, col. 2.
मुमुक्षु: मुमुक्षु, उस्, उस्, उ, desirous of freeing, wish-ing to deliver or liberate; eager to be free (from mundane existence), striving after emancipation; wishing to let go or give up; wishing to emit or discharge; about to shoot; (उस्), m. a sage striving after emancipation. —मुमुक्षु-ता, f. or मुमु-क्षु-त्व, अम्, n. desire of liberation or of final emancipation.
मुमुचान: मुमुचान मुमुचान, मुमुचु। See p. 783, col. 2.
मुमुचु: मुमुचु, उस्, m. (mentioned with Un-mucu and Pra-mucu), N. of a Ṛṣi.
मुमोचयिषु: मुमोचयिषु, उस्, उस्, उ, desirous of liberating, wishing to set free.
मोक्तव्य: मोक्तव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be set free or released or liberated; to be let go or given up or delivered; to be flung or hurled, to be wielded, to be sent (as a missile).
मुचक: मुचक मुचक, अस्, m. lac, gum-lac.
मुचि: मुचि मुचि, इस्, m., N. of a Cakra-vartin.
मुचिलिन्द: मुचिलिन्द मुचिलिन्द, अस्, m. a species of flower; N. of a Nāga; of a Cakra-vartin; [cf. महा-म्°।] —मुचिलिन्द-पर्वत, अस्, m., N. of a mythical mountain; [cf. महा-म्°।]
मुचुकुन्द: मुचुकुन्द मुचुकुन्द, अस्, m. Pterospermum Suberifolium; N. of an ancient king (or Muni); N. of a son of Mandhāṛ (who asked the gods to grant him the enjoyment of long and unbroken sleep as a reward for the assistance he had rendered them in subduing the demons; the gods complied with his request, and decreed that whosoever disturbed him should be burnt to ashes by fire emanating from his body; Kṛṣṇa, in order to destroy Kāla-yavana, enticed him into the cave where Mucukunda was asleep, and the latter being thus roused cast upon Kāla-yavana an angry glance which reduced him to ashes; see translation of Viṣṇu-Purāṇa, p. 567); N. of a son of Yadu; of the father of Candra-bhāga; of a poet of Kaśmīra; of a Daitya. —मुचुकुन्द-प्रसादक, अस्, m. an epithet of Kṛṣṇa.
मुचुटी: मुचुटी मुचुटी, f. (fr. rt. 2. मुच्), snapping the fingers [cf. पुच्छटि]; the fist; a pair of forceps.
मुछ्: मुछ् मुछ्, cl. 1. P. मुच्छति, &c., a various reading for rt. युछ्, q. v.
मुज्: मुज् मुज्, cl. 1. P. मोजति, &c., and मुञ्ज्, cl. 1. P. मुञ्जति, &c., to sound, give out a particular sound; (according to Vopa-deva also) cl. 10. P. मोजयति, &c., and मुञ्जयति, &c., to sound; to cleanse; [cf. rt. 1. मृज्: cf. also Gr. μύζ-ω, ἔ-μυ-σα, μυγ-μό-ς, μῡκ-ά-ο-μαι, μέμυκα; Lat. mugio.]
मुञ्च्: मुञ्च् मुञ्च् (connected with rts. मञ्च्, म्रुञ्च्, म्लुञ्च्), cl. 1. P. मुञ्चति, &c., to go, move; cl. 1. A. मुञ्चते, &c. = rt. मच्, q. v., to cheat, to be wicked, &c.
मुञ्च् मुञ्ज्। See rt. मुज् above.
मुञ्चक: मुञ्चक, अस्, m. a species of tree (= मुष्कक-वृक्ष).
मुञ्ज: मुञ्ज, अस्, m. a sort of rush or grass, Saccharum Munja (which grows to the height of ten feet and is used to form the Brāhmanical mekhalā or girdle as well as in basket-work); the Brāhmanical girdle or the sacred cord of a Brāhman (as made of the Muñja grass, but in this sense the more proper form is मौञ्ज; cf. Manu II. 27, 42, 43); an arrow (?); N. of a person with the patronymic Sāma-śravasa; of a Brāhman; of a poet and king of Dhārā; of a prince of Campā. —मुञ्ज-केतु, उस्, m. a proper N. —मुञ्ज-केश, अस्, m. ‘rush-haired,’ epithet of Śiva; of Viṣṇu; of a king; of a teacher; of a dis-ciple of Vijitāsu. —मुञ्जकेश-वत्, आन्, m. ‘having rush-like hair,’ epithet of Kṛṣṇa. —मुञ्ज-केशिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having rush-like hair; (ई), m. an epithet of Viṣṇu; a proper N. —मुञ्ज-ग्राम, अस्, m., N. of a village, (also read रम्य-ग्राम।) —मुञ्ज-नेजन, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. (according to Sāy.) freed from grass or rushes (= तृणेन शोधित, अपगत-तृण). —मुञ्जन्-धय, अस्, ई, अम्, sucking rushes. —मुञ्ज-पृष्ठ, अस्, m., N. of a place on the Himālaya mountains. —मुञ्ज-बन्धन, अम्, n. investiture with the Brāhmanical girdle or cord. —मुञ्ज-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, made of Muñja grass. —मुञ्ज-मेखलिन्, ई, m. ‘Muñja-girdled,’ an epi-thet of Viṣṇu; of Śiva. —मुञ्ज-वट, N. of a place of pilgrimage; [cf. मुञ्जावट।] —मुञ्ज-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, overgrown with rushes, rushy; (आन्), m. epithet of a particular species of Soma plant; N. of a mountain of the Himālaya range. —मुञ्ज-वासस्, आस्, m. ‘rush-clothed,’ epithet of Śiva. —मुञ्-जादित्य (°ज-आद्°), इस्, m., N. of an author. —मुञ्-जादिरि (°ज-अद्°), इस्, m., N. of a mountain. —मुञ्जा-वट (°ज-अव्°), N. of a place (= मुञ्ज-पृष्ठ)। —मुञ्जी-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, -कर्तुम्, to reduce to Muñja grass, i. e. to tear to shreds.
मुञ्जक: मुञ्जक, a various reading for मौञ्जक, q. v.
मुञ्जर: मुञ्जर, अम्, n. the fibrous root of the lotus.
मुञ्जात: मुञ्जात, अस्, m. a species of plant.
मुञ्जातक: मुञ्जातक, अस्, m. a species of tree; a kind of vegetable (= पुष्प-शाक-भेद); = मुञ्ज।
मुञ्जाल: मुञ्जाल, अस्, m., N. of an astronomer.
मुट्: मुट् मुट् (connected with rts. 1. मृद्, पुट्, पुण्ड्, पुड्, पुथ्), cl. 1. 6. 10. P. मोटति, मुटति, मोटयति, &c., to crush, grind, break, (see मोटक, मोटन); to blame, rebuke, (in this sense only cl. 6. मुटति।)
मुड्: मुड् मुड्, cl. 1. P. मोडति, &c., = rt. मुट् above.
मुण्: मुण् मुण्, cl. 6. P. मुणति, &c., to promise.
मुण्ट्: मुण्ट् मुण्ट्, cl. 1. P. मुण्टति, &c., = rt. मुट् above.
मुण्ठ्: मुण्ठ् मुण्ठ्, cl. 1. A. मुण्ठते, &c., to run away; to protect, (पालने being given as a various reading for पलायने।)
मुण्ड्: मुण्ड् मुण्ड्, cl. 1. P. मुण्डति, &c., to grind, (in this sense = rt. मुट् and con-nected with rt. 1. मृद्); to shave, shear; cl. 1. A. मुण्डते, मुण्डितुम्, to be pure; to sink; [cf. Lat. mund-o, mundu-s.]
मुण्ड: मुण्ड, अस्, आ, अम्, (perhaps connected with rt. 1. मृद्), shaved, bald, having no hair on the head; hornless, destitute of horns, having no horns (Ved.); stripped of top leaves or branches, lopped (as a tree); pointless, blunt; low, mean; (अस्), m. a man with a shaved head; a bald or shaven head, bald pate, shorn poll; the forehead; a tree stripped of its top branches, the trunk of a lopped tree, a pollard; a barber (= मुण्डक); N. of a king; of a Daitya; an epithet of Rāhu; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people; (आ), f. a (close-shaved) female mendicant; a species of plant (= मुण्डीरिका); Bengal madder; (ई), f. a species of plant (= महा-श्रावणिका); N. of one of the Mātṛs attending on Skanda; (अम्), n. the head; iron [cf. मुण्ड-लोह, मुण्डायस]; myrrh. —मुण्ड-चणक, अस्, m. a kind of pulse (= कलाय). —मुण्ड-धान्य, अम्, n. a kind of grain (without awns; cf. मुण्ड-शालि). —मुण्ड-पृष्-ठ, N. of a place. —मुण्ड-फल, अस्, m. a cocoa-nut tree, (the fruit being one step towards a human head made by Viśvāmitra when he proposed attempt-ing a creation in opposition to that of Brahmā.) —मुण्ड-मण्डली, f. a number of shaven heads; a number of troops of an inferior description. —मुण्ड-माला, f. or मुण्डमाला-तन्त्र, अम्, n., N. of a Tantra. —मुण्ड-मालिनी, f. a form of Durgā. —मुण्ड-लोह, अम्, n. iron; [cf. अष्ट-लोहक, मुण्डायस, मुण्डित।] —मुण्ड-वेदाङ्ग, अस्, m., N. of a serpent-demon. —मुण्ड-शालि, इस्, m. a species of rice. —मुण्डाख्या (°ड-आख्°), f. a species of plant (= महा-श्रावणिका). —मुण्डा-यस (°ड-अय्°), अम्, n. iron. —मुण्डासन (°ड-आस्°), अम्, n. a particular posture in sitting. —मुण्डेश्वर-तीर्थ (°ड-ईश्°), अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha.
मुण्डक: मुण्डक, अस्, m. the lopped trunk or stem of a tree, a tree stripped of its branches; a shaver, barber; (इका), f. a species of plant; (अम्), n. the head; N. of the chapters into which the Muṇḍakopaniṣad is divided. —मुण्डकोपनिषद् (°क-उप्°), f., N. of a well-known Upaniṣad of the Atharva-veda (con-taining three short chapters or Muṇḍakas, each of which comprises two sections or Khaṇḍas, and said to take its name from the word मुण्ड because every one who comprehends its secret doctrine is ‘shorn,’ i. e. liberated from all error, a similar idea being probably involved in the name of the Kṣuri-kopanishad or ‘Razor Upaniṣad:’ the Muṇḍaka is one of the most interesting of the numerous Upa-niṣads, on account of the reasons which it gives for the superiority of these works over the Veda and its ritual; thus, according to Muṇḍaka I. 4, there are two sciences, the higher and the inferior; the inferior is the knowledge of the Ṛg-veda, Yajur-veda, Sāma-veda, Atharva-veda, pronunciation, ritual, grammar, explanation of Vedic texts, prosody, and the astronomical calendar; but the higher knowledge is that by which the imperishable Brahma is com-prehended). —मुण्डकोपनिषद्-दीपिका, f., N. of a commentary on the above.
मुण्डन: मुण्डन, अम्, n. shaving the head, tonsure; protecting, defending, [cf. rt. मुण्ठ्।]
मुण्डनक: मुण्डनक, अस्, m. a species of rice, = मुण्ड-शालि; (इका), f. in महा-म्°, q. v.
मुण्डय: मुण्डय, Nom. P. मुण्डयति, -यितुम्, to shave, shear, cut off the hair, shave the head closely.
मुण्डार: मुण्डार, अम्, n., N. of a place at which the sun was worshipped.
मुण्डित: मुण्डित, अस्, आ, अम्, shaved, closely shaven, bald. shorn, lopped; (अम्), n. iron; [cf. मुण्ड-लोह।] —मुण्डित-शिरस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, shaven-headed, bald-pated.
मुण्डितिका: मुण्डितिका, f. a species of plant, (commonly मुण्डीरी or मुण्डिनिका; cf. मुण्डन्क।)
मुण्डिन्: मुण्डिन्, ई, इनी, इ, shaven, close-shaved, bald; horn-less, having no horns; (ई), m. an epithet of Śiva; a barber. —मुण्डीश्वर-तीर्थ (°डि-ईश्°), अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha; [cf. दण्डि-मुण्डीश्वर।]
मुण्डिभ: मुण्डिभ, अस्, m., Ved. a proper N., (the author of Vājasaneyi-saṃhitā XXV. 9. is so called.)
मुण्डीरिका: मुण्डीरिका, f. a species of plant (= मुण्डा = मुण्डितिका।]
मुण्डीरी: मुण्डीरी, f. a species of plant (= श्रमणा, प्र-व्रजिता).
मुत्कल: मुत्कल मुत्कल, अस्, m., N. of a man.
मुत्खलिन्: मुत्खलिन् मुत्खलिन्, ई, m., N. of a Deva-putra.
मुत्य: मुत्य मुत्य, अम्, n. a pearl.
मुथशिल: मुथशिल मुथशिल, (in astrology) N. of the third Yoga (= مُتّصِل).
मुद्: मुद् 1. मुद्, cl. 10. P. मोदयति, मोद-यितुम्, to mix, mingle, blend, unite.

मुद् 2. मुद्, cl. 1. A. मोदते (ep. occa-sionally P. मोदति, &c.), मुमुदे, मो-दिष्यते, अमोदिष्ट, मोदितुम्, to be glad or joyous or happy, to rejoice, enjoy one's self, rejoice in, have pleasure in (with inst. or loc., e. g. पुत्र-पौत्रैर् मोदस्व, rejoice thou in children and children's children; तस्मिन् न मोदामहे, we do not take pleasure in that): Caus. मोदयति, अमू-मुदत्, मोदयितुम्, to rejoice, delight, give pleasure or joy, exhilarate, yield enjoyment; [cf. Lith. mu-drùs.]

3. मुद्, त्, f. joy, pleasure, delight, joyfulness, joyousness, gladness, happiness, rejoicing; Joy per-sonified as the daughter of Tuṣṭi (Contentment); intoxication; a species of medicinal plant (= वृद्-धि); a wife, woman (?). —मुद्-भाज्, क्, क्, क्, Ved. possessing joy, feeling or experiencing pleasure.
मुदकर: मुदकर, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people.
मुदा: मुदा, f. pleasure, enjoyment, joy, gladness. —मु-दान्वित (°दा-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, filled with joy, pleased, delighted. —मुदा-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, rejoic-ing, glad, delighted; (अती), f., N. of a daughter of king Vidūratha. —मुदा-वसु, उस्, m., N. of a son of Prajāti.
मुदित: मुदित, अस्, आ, अम्, rejoiced, joyful, happy, de-lighted, glad; (अस्), m. epithet of a particular sort of servant; (आ), f. joy, gladness; (अम्), n. pleasure, happiness; a particular kind of sexual embrace. —मुदित-भद्र, अस्, m. a proper N.
मुदिर: मुदिर, अस्, m. a cloud; a lover, libertine; a frog.
मुद्ग: मुद्ग, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. 2. मुद् above, Uṇādi-s. 1. 127), a sort of kidney-bean, Phaseolus Radiatus or Phaseolus Mungo (both the plant and its beans); a cover, covering, lid; a kind of sea-bird, (in this sense for मद्गु, q. v.) —मुद्ग-गिरि, इस्, m., N. of a city. —मुद्ग-पर्णी, f. a sort of kidney-bean, Phaseolus Trilobus. —मुद्ग-भुज्, क्, or मुद्ग-भोजिन्, ई, m. ‘eating Mudga-beans,’ a horse. —मुद्ग-मोदक, अस्, m. a kind of sweet-meat or confectionery. —मुद्ग-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having beans, &c. —मुद्गार्द्रकवट (°ग-आर्°), अस्, m. a kind of sweetmeat.
मुद्गप: मुद्गप, अस्, m., N. of a man.
मुद्गर: मुद्गर, अस्, m. (probably connected with मुद्-ग), a hammer, mallet; a hammer-like weapon, mace; a staff weighted at the bottom with iron for breaking clods of earth; a kind of dumb-bell or club-like piece of wood used for exercising the arms; a bud (= कोरक); a species of jasmine, (also अम्, n. probably the blossom); N. of a Nāga; (अम्), n. a particular posture in sitting. —मुद्गर-गोमिन्, ई, m. a proper N. —मुद्गर-पर्णक, अस्, m., N. of a Nāga. —मुद्गर-पिण्डक, अस्, m., N. of a Nāga. —मुद्गराकार (°र-आक्°), अस्, आ, अम्, hammer-shaped, shaped like a mallet.
मुद्गरक: मुद्गरक, अस्, इका, अम्, (at the end of a comp.) a hammer; (अस्), m. Averrhoa Carambola; [cf. फल-मुद्गरिका।]
मुद्गल: मुद्गल, अस्, m. मुद्गलानी: मुद्गलानी, f., Ved. the wife of Mudgala.

मूर्त मूर्त, मूर्ति। See p. 786, col. 1.
मूर्ति: मूर्ति, इस्, f. (often written मूर्त्ति), any solid body, any tangible or material form, (in philosophy) anything which has definite shape and limits (as earth, air, fire, water, and mind, but not आकाश, ether), a material element (especially as a component part of the human body), body, form, visible shape, matter, substance; embodiment, manifestation, in-carnation, personification, (मूर्तिर् धर्मस्य शाश्-वती, an eternal personification of justice; cf. तपो-म्°); an image, statue, figure, form; beauty; N. of the first astrological house; N. of a daughter of Dakṣa and wife of Dharma; (इस्), m., N. of one of the sages under the tenth Manu; [cf. perhaps Gr. βρέτας, μορφή.] —मूर्ति-तस्, ind. from the form, bodily, substantially. —मूर्ति-त्व, अम्, n. the being or having a body, corporeity, embodiment, materiality, (मूर्तित्वे परिकल्पितः, made into bodily shape.) —मूर्ति-धर, अस्, आ, अम्, having a body, em-bodied, corporeal, incarnate. —मूर्ति-प, अस्, m. ‘image-keeper,’ a priest who guards an idol. —मूर्ति-भाव, अस्, m. the state of assuming a solid form, corporeity. —मूर्ति-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having a material or bodily form, material, embodied, corpo-real, incarnate, personified [cf. ख-म्°, विश्व-म्°]; (आन्), m., N. of a son of Kuśa; (अत्), n. a body. —मूर्ति-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, possessing a particular form. —मूर्ति-मात्रा, f. a particle of matter. —मूर्ति-लिङ्ग, perhaps = Prāg-jyotiṣa, the city of Naraka.
मुर्भिणी: मुर्भिणी मुर्भिणी, f. a chafing-dish, small fire-place, fire-pan.
मुर्मुर: मुर्मुर मुर्मुर, अस्, m. (an onomatopoetic word), a fire made of chaff, burning chaff; the god of love; N. of one of the horses of the sun; (आ), f., N. of a river.
मुर्व्: मुर्व् मुर्व् [cf. rt. 1. मू], cl. 1. P. मूर्वति, मूर्वितुम्, to bind, tie; [cf. मूर्वा।]
मुल्: मुल् मुल् = rt. मूल्, q. v.
मुलालिन्: मुलालिन् मुलालिन्, ई, m. or मुलाली, f., Ved. (probably) a species of edible lotus.
मुशटी: मुशटी मुशटी, मुशल, मुशलिका, मुशलिन्। See मुसटी, मुसल, मुसलिका, मुसलिन्।
मुशल्लह: मुशल्लह मुशल्लह or मुसल्लह, an astro-logical term (مصالحة).
मुष्: मुष् 1. मुष्, cl. 1. P. मोषति, मोषि-तुम्, = rt. मष्, to kill, q. v.

मुष् 2. मुष् [cf. rt. 1. मूष्], cl. 9. P. मुष्णाति (rarely cl. 6. P. मुषति), मु-मोष, मोषिष्यति, अमोषीत् (Ved. forms मो-षति, मोषथ, मुषायते), मोषितुम्, to steal, filch, pilfer, rob, plunder, seize, carry off; to steal, away, tear away, ravish; to captivate, enrapture; to surpass, excel; cl. 4. P. मुष्यति, मोषितुम्, = rt. मुस्, to break, destroy, (according to the commen-tator on Bhaṭṭi-kāvya XV. 16, where अमुषः is explained by खण्डितवान् असि): Pass. मुष्यते: Caus. मोषयति, Aor. अमूमुषत्: Desid. मु-मुषिषति, -षितुम्, see Pāṇ. I. 2, 8: Intens. मोमुष्यते, मोमोष्टि।
3. मुष्, ट्, f. stealing, theft; (ट्, ट्, ट्), robbing, stealing, taking away (at the end of comps.); dis-pelling (darkness, &c.); surpassing, excelling.
मुषक: मुषक, अस्, m. a mouse, = मूषक, q. v.
मुषि: मुषि, इस्, इस्, इ, stealing, &c. (in मनो-म्°, q. v.).
मुषित: मुषित, अस्, आ, अम्, stolen, robbed, plundered; stript; deceived, cheated; ravished, carried off, torn away, bereft of, deprived of, free from. —मुषित-चेतस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, bereft of sense, deprived of con-sciousness.
मुषितक: मुषितक, अस्, इका, अम्, stolen in a low or vile manner; (अम्), n. stolen property.
मुषित्वा: मुषित्वा, ind. having stolen, having carried off, &c.
मुषीवन्: मुषीवन्, आ, m. (मुषीवाणम्, acc. c.), Ved. a thief, robber.
मुष्क: मुष्क, अस्, m. (perhaps originally ‘a little mouse,’ fr. मुष् = 2. मूष् + क), a testicle; the scrotum; a species of tree (= मुषक); a muscular or stout person (= मांसल); a thief; a crowd, heap, quantity, multitude, mass; (औ), m. du. pudenda muliebria. —मुष्क-कच्छू, ऊस्, f. an eruption on the scrotum. —मुष्क-देश, अस्, m. the region of the scrotum. —मुष्क-द्वय, अम्, n. the two testicles. —मुष्क-भार, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having large testicles, (Sāy. = प्रवृद्ध-मुष्क।) —मु-ष्क-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. having testicles; an epithet of Indra as author of Ṛg-veda X. 38. —मुष्क-शून्य, अस्, m. ‘one who is without testicles,’ a castrated person, eunuch, guard of the women's apartments. —मुष्क-शोफ, अस्, m. swell-ing of the testicles. —मुष्क-स्रोतस्, अस्, n. the vas deferens (in anatomy). —मुष्काबर्ह (°क-आब्°), अस्, m., Ved. one who gelds or castrates.
मुष्कक: मुष्कक, अस्, m. a species of tree (the ashes of which are used as a cautery).
मुष्कर: मुष्कर, अस्, आ, अम्, having testicles; (अस्), m. a man with large testicles; a species of small animal or insect (Atharva-veda VI. 14, 2).
मुष्ट: मुष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, a rare form for मुषित, q. v.; (अम्), n. theft, robbery.
मुष्टि: मुष्टि, इस्, m. f. stealing, filching, pilfering; the closed or clenched hand (perhaps originally ‘the hand closed to grasp anything stolen’); the fist, (गूढाङ्गुष्ठ-कृत-मुष्टि, the clenched fist with the thumbs turned in); a fistful, handful [cf. दर्भ-म्°, कुश-म्°, केश-म्°, गाढ-म्°]; a par-ticular measure (= a handful = 1 Pala); a hilt or handle (of a sword, &c.); a compendium, abridg-ment; (according to Mahī-dhara on Vājasaneyi-s. XXIII. 24) the penis (= लिङ्ग); [cf. Old Germ. fust; Angl. Sax. fyst.] —मुष्टि-करण, अम्, n. clenching the fist. —मुष्टि-ता, f. firmness of grasp. —मुष्टि-देश, अस्, m. the part of a bow which is grasped in the hand, the middle of a bow. —मु-ष्टि-द्यूत, अम्, n. a kind of game, odd or even, (commonly called पुरमुट्खेला।) —मुष्टिन्-धम, अस्, ई, अम्, blowing into the closed hand. —मुष्टिन्-धय, अस्, आ, अम्, sucking the fist or closed hand; (अस्), m. a child, boy. —मुष्टि-पात, अस्, m. pummelling, boxing. —मुष्टि-प्र-हार, अस्, m. a blow with the fist. —मुष्टि-बन्-ध, अस्, m. clenching the fist, closing the hand (in taking hold of anything); a handful. —मुष्टि-बन्धन, अम्, n. the act of clenching the fist. —मुष्टि-मुख, अस्, ई, अम्, having a fist-like face. —मुष्टि-मेय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be measured or spanned with the hand, (मध्येन मुष्टि-मेयेन, with a waist which might be spanned with the fingers.) —मुष्टि-युद्ध, अम्, n. a fight with fists, pugilistic encounter. —मुष्टि-सङ्ग्राह-पी-डित, अस्, आ, अम्, squeezed by a grasp with the fist, griped. —मुष्टि-हत्या, f., Ved. a hand to hand engagement. —मुष्टि-हन्, आ, घ्नी, अ, Ved. fight-ing hand to hand (said of common soldiers as opposed to those who fought in chariots). —मुष्टी-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, &c., to close the hand, clench the fist. —मुष्टी-कृत्य, ind. having clenched the fist. —मुष्टी-मुष्टि, ind. fist to fist, hand to hand fighting, fisticuffs.
मुष्टिक: मुष्टिक, अस्, m. a particular position of the hands; a goldsmith; N. of an Asura; (आस्), m. pl., N. of an outcast race, = डोम्बास्; (आ), f. the fist, hand; (अम्), n. a fight with fists, pugilistic encounter, fisticuffs. —मुष्टिक-घ्न, अस्, m. ‘slayer of Muṣṭika,’ an epithet of Viṣṇu. —मुष्टिक-स्वस्-तिक, अस्, m. a particular position of the hands in dancing. —मुष्टिका-कथन, अम्, n. talking with the fingers. —मुष्टिकान्तक (°क-अन्°), अस्, m. ‘annihilator of Muṣṭika,’ an epithet of Bala-deva, the brother of Kṛṣṇa.
मुष्णत्: मुष्णत्, अन्, अती, अत्, stealing, robbing, taking away, depriving of; captivating; excelling, surpass-ing, eclipsing.
मुष्यमाण: मुष्यमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, being robbed, being plundered.
मुस्तु: मुस्तु, उस्, m. f. = मुष्टि, the fist.
मुष्ठक: मुष्ठक मुष्ठक, अस्, m. black mustard.
मुस्: मुस् मुस् [cf. rt. 2. मुष्, cl. 4], cl. 4. P. मुस्यति, &c., to break in pieces, cleave, divide, cut, destroy.
मुसल: मुसल, अस्, अम्, m. n. (often spelt मुषल and less correctly मुशल), a pestle, a kind of wooden pestle used for cleaning rice; a mace, club, (चक्र-मुसलः सङ्ग्रामः, a battle fought with discuses and clubs); a particular surgical instrument; a par-ticular constellation; the twenty-second astronomical Yoga or division of the moon's path; N. of a son of Viśvāmitra; (ई), f. the plant Curculigo Orchioides; Salvinia Cucullata; the house-lizard. —मुसला-मु-सलि, ind. club against club. —मुसलायुध (°ल-आय्°), अस्, आ, अम्, club-armed; (अस्), m. an epithet of Bala-deva. —मुसली-भू, cl. 1. P. -भवति, -भ-वितुम्, to become a club. —मुसलोलूखल (°ल-उल्°), अम्, n. a pestle and mortar.
मुसलक: मुसलक, अस्, m., N. of a mountain; (इका), f. a common lizard.
मुसलित: मुसलित, अस्, आ, अम्, see Gaṇa Tārakādi to Pāṇ. V. 2, 36.
मुसलिन्: मुसलिन्, ई, इनी, इ, armed with a club; (ई), m. an epithet of Śiva; of Bala-deva.
मुसलीय: मुसलीय or मुसल्य, अस्, आ, अम्, deserving to be pounded to death or to be put to death with a club.
मुस्र: मुस्र, अम्, n. a pestle; a tear (in this sense = अश्रु, q. v.).
मुसटी: मुसटी मुसटी, f. a white variety of Pani-cum Italicum, (also read मुशटी।)
मुसारगल्व: मुसारगल्व मुसारगल्व, coral or a kind of white coral.
मुस्त्: मुस्त् मुस्त्, cl. 10. P. मुस्तयति, मुस्त-यितुम्, to gather, collect, heap up, accu-mulate.
मुस्त: मुस्त, अस्, आ, अम्, m. f. n. a species of grass, Cyperus Rotundus; (अम्), n. the root of the Musta grass; [cf. भद्र-म्°।] —मुस्त-गिरि, इस्, m., N. of a mountain. —मुस्ताद (°त-अद or °त-आद), अस्, m. ‘grass-eater,’ a hog, a wild boar. —मुस्ताभ (°त-आभ्°), अम्, n. a species of Cyperus.
मुस्तक: मुस्तक, अस्, आ, अम्, m. f. n. a species of grass, Cyperus Rotundus; (अस्), m. a particular vegetable poison.
मुह्: मुह् 1. मुह्, cl. 4. P. मुह्यति, मुमोह, मोहिष्यति or मोक्ष्यति, अमुहत्, मो-हितुम् or मोग्धुम् or मोढुम्, to become stupe-fied or unconscious, to be faint, lose consciousness, to be perplexed or embarrassed; to be disturbed in mind; to err or be mistaken; to be foolish or stupid or infatuated; to fail: Caus. मोहयति, -यि-तुम्, Aor. अमूमुहत्, to stupefy, bewilder, per-plex, infatuate, deprive of consciousness; to throw into disorder; to cause to err; to mistake (A., e. g. अध्वानम् मोहयन्ते, they mistake the way): Intens. मोमुह्यते, मोमोग्धि, मोमोढि, to be in great perplexity or greatly embarrassed.
2. मुह्, क्, क्, क्, or ट्, ट्, ट्, perplexing, embarrass-ing, infatuating; [cf. मनो-मुह्।]
मुहिर: मुहिर, अस्, आ, अम्, foolish, stupid; (अस्), m. a blockhead [cf. मुहेर]; ‘the bewilderer,’ epithet of the god of love.
मुहु: मुहु, ind. = मुहुस्, Ved. suddenly, in a moment.
मुहुक: मुहुक, अम्, n., Ved. a moment, instant; [cf. मुहूर्त।]
मुहुस्: मुहुस्, ind. (perhaps originally ‘in a bewildering manner’), suddenly, all at once, in a moment, in an instant (Ved.); for a moment, for a time, awhile; at every moment, repeatedly, constantly; मुहुस् — मुहुस्, at one moment — at another; at one time  — at another; मुहुर् मुहुस्, at every moment, repeatedly, again and again, over and over again; on the other hand; [cf. पुनर्।] —मुहुर्-गीर्, ईर्, ईर्, ईर्, Ved. swallowing suddenly; (Sāy.) ever being hymned (= सर्वदा गीयमानः). —मुहुर्-भा-षा, f. or मुहुर्-वचस्, अस्, n. repeating what is said, repetition, tautology. —मुहुर्-भुज्, क्, m. ‘constantly eating,’ a horse. —मुहुश्-चारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, occurring repeatedly, recurring over and over again. —मुहुस्-काम, अस्, आ, अम्, loving or desiring again and again. —मुहुस्-तनैस्, ind. at repeated intervals, repeatedly, constantly.
मुहूर्त: मुहूर्त, अस्, अम्, m. n. a moment, an instant, any short space of time, (मुहूर्तात्, after an instant, immediately, directly, at once; मुहूर्तेन, after an instant, after a little while; कु-मुहूर्त, an inau-spicious moment, cf. दुर्-म्°, प्रति-म्°); a particu-lar division of time (see Manu 1. 64); the thirtieth part of a day, a period of forty-eight minutes; (अस्), m. an astrologer; (आस्), m. pl. the Muhūrtas or Hours personified as the children of Muhūrtā; (आ), f., N. of a daughter of Dakṣa (wife of Dharma or Manu and mother of the Muhūrtas). —मुहूर्त-कल्प-द्रुम, अस्, m. and मुहूर्त-गण-पति, इस्, m., N. of works. —मुहूर्त-चिन्तामणि, इस्, m., N. of an astrological work by Rāma the son of Ananta. —मुहूर्त-ज, आस्, m. pl. children of Mu-hūrtā; [cf. मौहूर्तिक।] —मुहूर्त-तत्त्व, अम्, n., N. of a work. —मुहूर्त-दीपक, अस्, m., N. of an astrological work by Mahā-deva. —मुहूर्त-दीपिका, f., N. of a work. —मुहूर्त-मार्तण्ड, अस्, m., N. of an astrological work by Nārāyaṇa. —मुहूर्त-वल्लभा, f., N. of a commentary on the Muhūrta-mārtaṇḍa. —मुहूर्त-स्तोम, आस्, m. pl., N. of an Ekāha.
मुहूर्तक: मुहूर्तक = मुहूर्त, a moment, instant; an hour.
मुहेर: मुहेर, अस्, m. = मुहिर, a fool, blockhead; [cf. perhaps Gr. μῶρο-ς; Lat. moru-s, mor-osu-s.]
मूढ: मूढ, अस्, आ, अम्, stupefied, bewildered, per-plexed, confounded, confused [cf. दिङ्-म्°], uncer-tain how to act; infatuated; stupid, dull, silly, foolish, simple, ignorant; mistaken, deceived, erring, gone astray or adrift; wrong, out of the right place (as the fetus in delivery), abortive; causing confusion, confounding; epithet of a particular position in the Yoga system; (अस्), m. a fool, blockhead, dolt, idiot; a sluggard; (आस्), m. pl. an epithet of the elements in the Sāṅkhya philosophy. —मूढ-गर्भ, अस्, m. difficult delivery; a dead fetus. —मूढ-ग्राह, अस्, m. a confused notion, misconception, infatuation. —मूढ-चक्षुर्-गद-च्छेतृ, ता, m. the remover of the defect of vision of the foolish. —मूढ-चेतन, अस्, आ, अम्, or मूढ-चेतस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, bewildered in mind, foolish, simple, silly. —मूढ-ता, f. or मूढ-त्व, अम्, n. stupidity, infatuation, bewilderment, confusion, simplicity, folly, ignorance; error, mistake, (ग्रन्थि-मूढता, mis-take or confusion in disentangling a knot.) —मूढ-धी, ईस्, ईस्, इ, or मूढ-बुद्धि, or मूढ-मति, इस्, इस्, इ, ‘silly-minded, ’ silly, simple, foolish. —मू-ढ-प्रभु, उस्, m. the chief of fools, a great blockhead. —मूढ-रथ, अस्, m., N. of a man; (आस्), m. pl., N. of his descendants. —मूढ-वत्, ind. like a fool. —मूढ-सत्त्व, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘silly-minded,’ infatuated, insane. —मूढात्मन् (°ढ-आत्°), आ, आ, अ, bewildered or stupefied in mind, un-conscious, insensible, foolish, a fool. —मूढेश्वर (°ढ-ईश्°), अस्, m. the greatest of fools, a great sim-pleton, arrant blockhead; N. of an ascetic.
मू: मू 1. मू (connected with rts. मव्, मव्य्), cl. 1. A. मवते (sometimes P. -ति), to bind, tie, make fast: Caus. Aor. अमीमवत्: Desid. of Caus. मिमावयिषति, see Scholist on Pāṇ. VII. 4, 80.
मूक: मूक, अस्, आ, अम्, dumb, silent, speechless, mute [cf. एड-म्°, कल्ल-म्°]; wretched, poor; (अस्), m. a mute; a poor man; N. of a Dānava; of a Nāga; [cf. Lat. mutus.] —मूक-ता, f. or मूक-त्व, अम्, n. dumbness, muteness, silence. —मूक-भाव, अस्, m. the state of being dumb, dumbness. —मूकाण्-डज (°क-अण्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having the birds silent (said of a forest). —मूकाम्बिका (°क-अम्°), f. (per-haps) a form of Durgā; मूकाम्बिकायाः सदनम्, N. of a place. —मूकी-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, -कर्-तुम्, to make dumb, render speechless, put to silence.
मूकिमन्: मूकिमन्, आ, m. dumbness, muteness, silence.
मूतक: मूतक, अम्, n., Ved. a little basket.
मूकलराय: मूकलराय मूकलराय, अस्, m., N. of a king.
मूचीप: मूचीप मूचीप, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people; [cf. मूतिब।]
मूजवत्: मूजवत् मूज-वत्, आन्, m., N. of a moun-tain; (अन्तस्), m. pl., N. of a people.
मूजालदेव: मूजालदेव मूजाल-देव, अस्, m. a proper N.
मूतिब: मूतिब मूतिब, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people.
मूत्र: मूत्र मूत्र, अम्, n. (probably connected with rt. 1. मिह्; but according to Uṇādi-s. IV. 162. fr. rt. मुच्, to discharge; by others connected with rts. 1. मीव् and मिन्व्), the fluid secreted by the kidneys, urine. —मूत्र-कर, अस् ई, अम्, producing urine. —मूत्र-कृच्छ्र, अम्, n. painful discharge of urine in minute quantities, strangury; a class of urinary affections (of which eight kinds are enume-rated, including gravel, stone, &c.). —मूत्र-कृच्-छ्रिन्, ई, इणी, इ, labouring under painful discharge of urine, suffering from strangury. —मूत्र-कृत-वासस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, Ved. steeped or soaked in urine. —मूत्र-कोश, अस्, m. the scrotum. —मूत्र-क्षय, अस्, m. insufficient secretion of urine. —मू-त्र-ग्रन्थि, इस्, m. a knot or induration on the neck of the bladder. —मूत्र-घात = मूत्राघात, q. v. —मूत्र-जठर, अस्, अम्, m. n. swelling of the belly in consequence of retention of urine. —मू-त्र-दोष, अस्, m. urinary disease. —मूत्र-निरो-ध, अस्, m. obstruction or retention of urine. —मू-त्र-पतन, अस्, m. the civet cat. —मूत्र-पथ, अस्, m. the urinary passage. —मूत्र-परीक्षा, f. examination of urine, uroscopy; N. of a chapter of the Śārṅgadhara-saṃhitā. —मूत्र-पुट, अम्, n. ‘urine-cavity,’ the lower belly. —मूत्र-पुरीष, अम्, n. urine and excrement. —मूत्र-प्रसेक, अस्, m. the urethra. —मूत्र-फला, f. Cucumis Utilissi-mus (= कर्कटी); another species of cucumber (= त्रपुषी). —मूत्र-भावित, अस्, आ, अम्, saturated with urine. —मूत्र-मार्ग, अस्, m. ‘urine-canal,’ the urethra. —मूत्रमार्ग-निरोधन, अम्, n. obstruction of the urethra. —मूत्र-वर्धक, अस्, इका, अम्, increasing urine, diuretic. —मूत्र-वह, अस्, आ, अम्, conveying urine. —मूत्र-विबन्ध-घ्न, अस्, ई, अम्, preventing suppression of urine, causing discharge of urine. —मूत्र-विष, अस्, आ, अम्, poisonous with urine. —मूत्र-वृद्धि, इस्, f. copious secretion of urine. —मूत्र-शकृत्, त्, n. urine and excrement. —मूत्र-शुक्र, अम्, n. a disease in which semen and urine are ejected toge-ther. —मूत्र-शूल, अस्, m. urinary colic. —मूत्र-सङ्क्षय, अस्, m. insufficient secretion of urine (= मूत्र-क्षय). —मूत्र-सङ्ग, अस्, m. urinary obstruction, a painful and bloody discharge of urine. —मूत्र-सङ्गिन्, ई, इनी, इ, suffering from the above disease. —मूत्राघात (°र-आघ्°), अस्, m. affection of the urine, urinary disease (of which twelve or thirteen kinds are enumerated). —मूत्रातीत (°र-अत्°), अस्, m. ‘past the proper time for voiding urine,’ a particular kind of retention of urine. —मू-त्राशय (°र-आश्°), अस्, m. ‘urine-receptacle,’ the lower belly. —मूत्रासाद = मूत्रौक-साद, q. v. —मूत्रोत्सङ्ग (°र-उत्°) = मूत्र-सङ्ग, q. v. —मूत्रौक-साद (°र-ओक्°), अस्, m. a disease in which the urine assumes various colours and is voided with pain.
मूत्रय: मूत्रय, Nom. P. मूत्रयति, -यितुम्, to dis-charge urine; to make water against or upon (with acc.): Intens. मोमूत्र्यते।
मूत्रल: मूत्रल, अस्, आ, अम्, promoting (the secretion of) urine, diuretic; (आ), f. Cucumis Utilissimus; another species of cucumber, = वालुकी; (अम्), n. a species of cucumber (= त्रपुष).
मूत्रित: मूत्रित, अस्, आ, अम्, voided as urine, discharged like urine; soiled with urine.
मूत्र्य: मूत्र्य, अस्, आ, अम्, urinary, belonging or relating to urine.
मूर: मूर 1. मूर, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. = मूढ, stupefied, bewildered, stupid, dull, foolish; [cf. अ-म्°, अ-प्रम्°।]

मूर 2. मूर, अस्, आ, अम् (perhaps fr. a form मू = rt. 1. मीव्), Ved. rushing, impetuous; (accord-ing to Sāy.) destroying killing (= मारक, fr. rt. मृ). —मूर-देव, अस्, m., Ved. epithet of a par-ticular kind of demon; (Sāy.) sporting in destruction (= मारण-क्रीड).
मूर 3. मूर, अम्, n., Ved. = मूल, a root.
मूरु: मूरु मूरु, N. of a country.
मूर्खलिका: मूर्खलिका मूर्खलिका, f. an arrow in the form of a bird's heart.
मूर्ण: मूर्ण मूर्ण। See under rt. मॄ, p. 793.
मूर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, crushed, broken; = 2. मूत, bound; [cf. rt. मुर्व्।]
मूर्धन्: मूर्धन् मूर्धन्, आ, m. (in Uṇādi-s. 1. 158. said to be fr. rt. मुर्व्, to bind), the forehead, brow, skull; the head in general; a head, chief, leader, superior, (सर्वेषाम् भूतानाम् मूर्धा राजा, the king is the head of all creatures); the highest or foremost or most prominent part, surface, top, point, peak, summit, (पर्वतस्य मूर्धा, the top or peak of a mountain); ‘the summit,’ epithet of a particular spiritual condition with Buddhists; (in geometry) the base, (opposed to अग्र); मूर्ध्नि or मूर्धनि, at the head or highest point, at the beginning or commencement, in the front, (अतिष्-ठन् मनुजेन्द्राणाम् मूर्ध्नि, he stood at the head of the kings of men; सङ्ग्राम-मूर्धनि, in the front of the battle); before, above, over. —मूर्ध-कर्णी or मूर्ध-कर्परी, f. or मूर्-ध-खोल, अम्, n. a broad-brimmed hat (worn as a shelter from rain); an umbrella. —मूर्ध-ज, अस्, m. ‘head-born,’ the hair of the head, (in this sense usually आस्, m. pl.); the mane; N. of a king (a Cakra-vartin). —मूर्धज-राग, अस्, m. colouring or dyeing the hair. —मूर्ध-ज्योतिस्, इस्, n. = ब्रह्म-रन्ध्र, q. v. —मूर्ध-तस्, ind., Ved. upon the head. —मूर्ध-तैलिक, अस्, m., with वस्ति, epithet of a kind of Errhine for the head. —मूर्धन्-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. containing the word मूर्धन्; (आन्), m., N. of a Gandharva; of an Āṅgirasa or Vāma-devya, author of the hymn Ṛg-veda X. 88. —मूर्ध-पात, अस्, m. the splitting of the skull. —मूर्ध-पिण्ड, अस्, m. a lump upon the head (of an elephant in rut). —मूर्ध-पुष्प, अस्, m. the tree Mimosa Sirissa (शिरीष). —मूर्ध-रस, अस्, m. the scum of boiled rice, rice-water. —मूर्-ध-वेष्टन, अम्, n. a turban, fillet, diadem. —मूर्धान्त (°ध-अन्°), अस्, m. the crown of the head. —मूर्धाभिषिक्त (°ध-अभ्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having the head sprinkled, anointed, inaugu-rated, consecrated, installed; (अस्), m. a consecrated king; a man of the Kṣatriya or warrior caste; a royal counsellor, minister; = मूर्धावसिक्त below. —मूर्धाभिषेक (°ध-अभ्°), अस्, m. ‘head-sprinkling,’ the act of consecrating any one (as king), anointing, inaugurating. —मूर्धावसिक्त (°ध-अव्°), अस्, m. epithet of a particular mixed caste, the son of a Brāhman father by a Kṣatriya mother; = मूर्धाभिषिक्त, a consecrated king.
मूर्ध: मूर्ध = मूर्धन् (at the end of certain comps., cf. द्वि-म्°, त्रि-म्°).
मूर्धन्य: मूर्धन्य, अस्, आ, अम्, being on or in the head, belonging to the head, capital; coming from the head or skull, cerebral (a term applied to a class of letters representing sounds formed high in the mouth or by keeping back the tip of the tongue as far as possible in the head and slightly turning it upwards, e. g. ऋ, ॠ, ट्, ठ्, ड्, ढ्, ण्, र्, ष्; these letters are sometimes called linguals); uppermost, highest, su-perior, pre-eminent; (आ), f., N. of the mother of Veda-śiras.
मूर्वा: मूर्वा मूर्वा, f. (according to some also मूर्वी, f.; probably fr. rt. मुर्व्), Sanseviera Rox-burghiana, a sort of creeper from the fibres of which bow-strings and the girdle of the Kṣatriyas are made, a sort of hemp for bow-strings; [cf. मौर्व।] —मूर्वा-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, made of Mūrvā.
मूल्: मूल् मूल् (more properly to be regarded as a Nom. fr. मूल below), cl. 1. P. मूलति (according to Vopa-deva also A. -ते), मु-मूल, मूलितुम्, to be rooted or firm, stand fast, take or strike root: Caus. मूलयति (according to Vopa-deva also मोलयति), मूलयितुम्, Aor. अमू-मुलत्, to plant, transplant; to grow, sprout, shoot, germinate.
मूल: मूल, अम्, n. a root (literally and metaphorically); the root of any plant or tree, (मूलं कृ, to take or strike root); the root of Arum Campanulatum; the root of long pepper and of Costus Speciosus or Ara-bicus; basis, groundwork, beginning, origin, com-mencement, cause, (मूलाद् आरभ्य, having com-menced at the beginning); the bottom of anything, foot, (शैलस्य मूलम्, the foot of a mountain); basis, lower part, lower end, (वीणाया मूलम्, the lower end of a lute which rests against the body of a player); the end or juncture of anything by which it is joined to anything else [cf. बाहु-म्°, कर्ण-म्°]; outermost edge or border; original, original text of any work (as distinguished from the scholia or commentary); an old or hereditary servant or dependant, an aboriginal native or inhabitant; ori-ginal property, capital, principal, stock; a chief or capital city; square root; the twenty-fourth or, according to some, seventeenth or nineteenth lunar asterism containing eleven stars, (in this sense अस्, अम्, m. n.; cf. नक्षत्र); immediate neigh-bourhood or proximity; a copse, thicket; a vendor not a true owner, (according to Kullūka on Manu VIII. 202. मूलम् = अ-स्वामी विक्रेता); a particular position of the fingers [cf. मूल-बन्ध]; (अस्), m. an epithet of Sadā-śiva; (आ), f. Asparagus Race-mosus; the asterism Mūla; (ई), f. a species of small house-lizard; (अस्, आ, अम्), original, first; own, proper, peculiar, (in Manu VII. 184. मूल is said to mean a king's own territory.) —मूल-कर्मन्, अ, n. ‘root-machination,’ magical employment of roots, magic; [cf. मूली-कर्मन्, मूल-कृत्।] —मूल-कार, अस्, m. the author of an original work. —मूल-कारण, अम्, n. first or original cause. —मूल-कारिका, f. a fire-place, furnace, oven. —मूल-कृच्छ्र, अस्, अम्, m. n. ‘root-austerity,’ a kind of penance, living solely on roots. —मूल-कृत्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. preparing roots for magical uses. —मूल-केशर, अस्, m. a citron. —मूल-खा-नक, अस्, m. ‘root-digger,’ one who digs for roots, a collector of roots. —मूल-गुण, अस्, m. ‘root-multiplier,’ the coefficient of a root (in algebra). —मूलगुण-जाति, इस्, f. assimilation and reduction of the root's coefficient with a fraction. —मूल-ग्रन्थ, अस्, m. an original text; an epithet of the very words uttered by Śākya-muni. —मूल-च्छेद, अस्, m. ‘root-cutting,’ cutting away the roots, cutting up by the roots, uprooting. —मूल-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘root-born,’ growing from roots, pro-duced from a root, radical; formed at the roots of trees (as an ant-hill); (अस्), m. a plant growing from a root (as a lotus); (अम्), n. green ginger. —मूल-जाति, इस्, f. chief or principal origin; = मू-लगुण-जाति, col. 2. —मूल-तस्, ind. from the root, on the root, on the lower side (Ved.), (आ मूलतस्, from the root upwards, from the beginning.) —मू-ल-त्रिकोण, अम्, n. epithet of the third astrological house. —मूल-त्व, अम्, n. the state or condition of a root, the being a root, the having a foundation or source in anything, (मूलत्वात् प्रजानां राजा स्कन्धः, the king is the stem through his subjects being the root; वेद-मूलत्व, the statement that the Veda is the original source of all knowledge; शास्त्र-मूलत्व, the being founded upon the Śās-tras.) —मूल-देव, अस्, m. = मूर-देव, an epithet of Kaṃsa [cf. मूल-भद्र]; N. of the murderer of Su-mitra the son of Agni-mitra; of an author; of a preceptor. —मूल-द्रव्य, अम्, n. original pro-perty, capital, principal, stock; [cf. मूल-धन।] —मूल-द्वार, अम्, n., Ved. principal door. —मू-ल-द्वारवती, f. the original or ancient Dvāra-vatī, the older part of that city; [cf. लघु-द्वारवती, मूल-नगर।] —मूल-धन, अम्, n. original property, capital. —मूल-धातु, उस्, m. lymph. —मूल-नगर, अम्, n. old town, (opposed to the suburbs or शाखा-नगर।) —मूल-नाश or मूल-नाशक, अस्, m. a proper N. —मूल-निकृन्तन, अस्, ई, अम्, cutting away the roots, utterly destroying, destroying root and branch. —मूल-पर्णी, f. a species of plant (= मण्डूक-पर्णी). —मूल-पाक, अस्, m., see Pāṇ. VII. 3, 53. —मूल-पुरुष, अस्, m. the male representative of a family, the last male of a race. —मूल-पुलिश-सिद्धान्त, अस्, m. the original Siddhānta of Puliśa. —मूल-पुष्-कर, अम्, n. = पुष्कर-मूल, q. v. —मूल-पोती, f. a species of culinary plant (= पोतिका). —मूल-प्रकृति, इस्, f. (in phil.) the original root or germ out of which matter or all apparent forms are evolved, the primary cause or ‘originant;’ (अयस्), f. pl. the four principal sovereigns to be considered in time of war (viz. the Vi-jigīṣu, Ari, Madhyama, and Ud-āsīna; cf. प्र-कृति, शाखा-प्रकृति). —मूल-प्रणिहित, अस्, आ, अम्, (perhaps) placed under the surveillance or brought under the notice of old (thieves employed as spies; according to Kullūka on Manu IX. 269 = राज-नियुक्त-पुराण-चौर-वर्गे सावधान-भूताः). —मूल-फल-द, अस्, m. the Jaka or bread-fruit tree. —मूल-फलाशन (°ल-अश्°), अम्, n. feeding on roots and fruits. —मूल-बणिग्-धन, अम्, n. a merchant's original property or capital. —मूल-बन्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, (probably) having roots, deep-rooted; (अस्), m. a particular po-sition of the fingers. —मूल-बर्हण, अस्, ई, अम्, Ved. tearing up by the roots, uprooting; (ई, अम्), f. n. the Nakṣatra Mūla; (अम्), n. the act of uprooting. —मूल-भद्र, अस्, m. an epithet of Kaṃsa, the uncle of Kṛṣṇa; [cf. मूल-देव।] —मूल-भव, अस्, आ, अम्, springing or growing from roots. —मूल-भार, अस्, m. a load of roots. —मूल-भूत, अस्, आ, अम्, become the root or original. —मूल-भृत्य, अस्, m. an old or here-ditary servant, one whose father, grandfather, &c. were servants before him, (opposed to आ-गन्तु।) —मूल-मन्त्र, अस्, m. an original or funda-mental text; an epithet of a particular sacred text. —मूल-माधव, N. of a place. —मूलमा-धव-तीथ, अम्, n., N. of a sacred bathing-place. —मूल-मित्र, अस्, m. a proper N. —मूल-रस, अस्, m. Sanseviera Zeylanica. —मूल-राज, अस्, m., N. of a king. —मूल-रामायण, अम्, n. the ori-ginal Rāmāyaṇa, i. e. Vālmīki's Rāmāyaṇa. —मूल-वचन, अम्, n. ‘primary word,’ an original text. —मूल-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, possessing edible roots; (perhaps) practising magic with roots. —मूल-वाप, अस्, m. one who plants roots. —मूल-वारिन्, ई, m. a proper N. —मूल-वित्त, अम्, n. ‘original property,’ capital, principal. —मूल-विद्या, f. ‘principal science,’ epithet of a particular Mantra (= द्वादशाक्षर, q. v.). —मूल-विनाशन, अम्, n. radical or entire destruction. —मूल-विभुज, अस्, आ, अम्, bending down roots; (अस्), m. a chariot. —मूल-विरेचन, अम्, n. a purgative prepared from roots. —मूल-व्यसन-वृत्ति, इस्, f. the hereditary occupation of executing criminals (Manu X. 38). —मूल-व्रतिन्, ई, इनी, इ, living exclusively on roots. —मूल-शकुन, अस्, m. (in augury) the first bird. —मूल-शाकट or मूल-शाकिन, अम्, n. a field planted with edible roots. —मूल-श्रीपति-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha. —मूल-सङ्घ, अस्, m. a society or sect. —मूल-सर्वास्तिवाद (°व-अस्°), आस्, m. pl., N. of a Buddhist school. —मूल-साधन, अम्, n. a chief instrument, principal expedient. —मूल-सूत्र, अम्, n. a principal Sūtra. —मूल-स्थल, अम्, n., N. of a place. —मूल-स्थान, अम्, n. principal place; foundation, base; the air, atmosphere; God; Mool-tan; (ई), f. an epithet of Gaurī. —मूलस्थान-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha (= भास्कर). —मूल-स्थायिन्, ई, इनी, इ, existing from the begin-ning; (ई), m. an epithet of Śiva. —मूल-स्रोतस्, अस्, n. the fountain-head of a river, principal current. —मूल-हर, अस्, आ, अम्, taking away the roots of anything, uprooting, utterly destroying, eradicating. —मूल-हर-त्व, अम्, n. the state of plucking up by the roots, eradicating, utter ruin. —मूलाधार (°ल-आध्°), अम्, n., scil. चक्र, epithet of a mystical circle situated above the generative organs; (accord-ing to a Scholiast) the navel. —मूलाभ (°ल-आभ्°), अम्, n. a radish. —मूलाभिधर्म-शास्त्र (°ल-अभ्°), अम्, n. the original Abhidharma-śāstra —मू-लायतन (°ल-आय्°), अम्, n. an original residence. —मूलाविद्या-विनाशक (°ल-अव्°), अस्, इका, अम्, (probably) destroying ignorance at its roots, eradi-cating ignorance. —मूलाशिन् (°ल-आश्°), ई, इनी, इ, ‘root-eating,’ living upon roots. —मूलाह्वा (°ल-आह्°), अम्, n. a radish. —मूली-कर्मन्, अ, n. = मूल-कर्मन्, q. v. —मूली-भूत, अस्, आ, अम्, become a root, become a source or origin. —मूलोच्छेद (°ल-उच्°), अस्, m. cutting up the roots, utter destruction. —मूलोत्खात (°ल-उत्°), अस्, आ, अम्, dug up by the roots, utterly destroyed; (अम्), n. digging up roots. —मूलोत्पाटन (°ल-उत्°), अम्, n. the digging up of roots. —मूलोत्पाटन-जीविन्, ई, m. one who lives by digging for roots (= मूल-खानक). —मू-लौषधि (°ल-ओष्°), इस्, f. a species of plant.
मूलक: मूलक, अस्, इका, अम्, (at the end of comps.) having roots, rooted in, springing from; born under the constellation Mūla; (अस्, अम्), m. n. an esculent root; a radish [cf. चाणक्य-म्°, नेपाल-म्°]; a sort of yam; (अस्), m. a kind of vegetable poison; N. of a prince, a son of Aśmaka; (इका), f. a root. —मूलक-पण, अस्, m. a handful or bunch of radishes, &c. (for sale). —मूलक-पर्णी, f. Moringa Pterygosperma. —मूलक-पोतिका, f. a radish. —मू-लक-मूला, f. the plant Lipeocercis Serrata.
मूलस: मूलस, अस्, आ, अम्, see Gaṇa Tṛṇādi to Pāṇ. IV. 2, 80.
मूलिक: मूलिक, अस्, आ, अम्, living on roots; radical, original; primary, principal; (अस्), m. an ascetic, devotee; (आ), f. a multitude or collection of roots. —मूलिकार्थ (°क-अर्°), अस्, m. a radical fact; [cf. योग।]
मूलिन्: मूलिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having a root or stock or origin, &c.; (ई), m. a tree.
मूलिन: मूलिन, अस्, आ, अम्, having a root, growing from a root (not bulbous or tuberous; cf. फल-मूलिन); = मूल-कृत्, q. v.; (अस्), m. a plant, tree.
मूलेर: मूलेर, अस्, m. a king; Indian spikenard, Nar-dostachys Jatamansi (= जटा-मांसी, जटा).
मूल्य: मूल्य, अस्, आ, अम्, being at the root; to be torn up by the roots, to be eradicated; to be bought for a price, to be bought, purchasable; (अम्), n. ori-ginal value; price, worth, value, a sum of money given as payment (e. g. दातुम् मूल्येन, to part with for a certain price, sell; दत्त्वा किञ्चिन् मूल्-येन, having given something in payment; मूल्-येन गृहीत, bought for a price); wages, salary, payment for service rendered; earnings, gain; = मूल, capital, principal; an article purchased. —मू-ल्य-करण, अम्, n. making the worth or value of anything, turning into money. —मूल्य-विवर्जित, अस्, आ, अम्, devoid of price, priceless, invaluable.
मूलाट: मूलाट मूलाट, मूलाटी, see Gaṇa Gaurādi to Pāṇ. IV. 1, 41.
मूष्: मूष् 1. मूष् (= rt. 2. मुष्), cl. 1. P. मूषति, मूषितुम्, to steal, rob, plunder. 2. मूष्, ट्, Ved. a mouse.
मूष: मूष, अस्, आ or ई, m. f. a rat, mouse; (आ), f. a crucible, (said to be also अस्, m. and ई, f.); Lipeo-cercis Serrata; = गवाक्ष, a round window, air-hole; [cf. Gr. μῦς; Lat. mus, mus-culu-s, mus-cip-ula; Old Germ. mûs; Slav. mys-i.] —मू-षा-कर्णी, f. an aquatic plant, Salvinia Cucullata. —मूषा-तुत्थ, अम्, n. a kind of vitriol. —मू-षी-करण, अम्, n. melting in a crucible.
मूषक: मूषक, अस्, m. a thief; a rat, mouse; a kind of metre; a particular part of the face; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people; (इका), f. a rat, mouse, a female rat or mouse; a species of leech; Salvinia Cucullata; a crucible; (अका), f. a rat, mouse, female rat. —मू-षक-कर्णिका or मूषक-कर्णी or मूषक-मारी, f. = मूषा-कर्णी, q. v. —मूषकाद (°क-अद), अस्, m. ‘mouse-eater,’ N. of a Nāga. —मूष-काराति (°क-अर्°), इस्, m. ‘mouse's foe,’ a cat.
मूषण: मूषण, अम्, n. the act of stealing, pilfering, filching.
मूषत्: मूषत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, stealing, filching, plun-dering.
मूषिक: मूषिक, अस्, m. a thief, plunderer; a rat, mouse [cf. गन्ध-मूषिक, महा-मूषिक]; Mimosa Sirissa (= शिरीष); N. of a country (the part of the Malabar coast between Quilon and Cape Como-rin); (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people, (also read भू-षिक); (आ), f., see under मूषक. —मूषिक-निर्विशेष, अस्, आ, अम्, not differing from a mouse, the same as a mouse. —मूषिक-पर्णी, f. an aquatic plant, Salvinia Cucullata. —मूषिक-रथ, अस्, m. ‘rat-vehicled, riding on a rat,’ an epithet of Gaṇeśa (see गणेश, p. 279). —मूषिक-विषाण, अम्, n. a mouse's horn, i. e. an impossibility; [cf. शश-विषाण।] —मूषिक-स्थल, अम्, n. (probably) a mole-hill. —मूषिकाङ्क (°क-अङ्°), अस्, m. ‘cha-racterized by a rat,’ epithet of Gaṇeśa. —मूषिकाञ्-चन (°क-अञ्°), अस्, m. ‘going on a rat,’ an epithet of Gaṇeśa. —मूषिकाद (°क-अद°) = मूषकाद। —मूषिका-दत्, अन्, अती, अत्, or मूषिका-दन्त, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, ‘mouse-toothed,’ having the teeth of a mouse. —मूषिकान्तकृत् (°क-अन्°), त्, m. ‘mouse-destroyer,’ a cat. —मूषिकाराति = मूष-काराति. —मूषिकाह्वय (°क-आह्°), अस्, m. Salvinia Cucullata. —मूषिकोत्कर (°क-उत्°) or °का-उत्°), अस्, m. a mole-hill.
मूषिकका: मूषिकका or मूषिकिका, f. (diminutive of मू-षिका), a little rat or mouse.
मूषिकार: मूषिकार, अस्, m. a male mouse.
मूषित: मूषित, अस्, आ, अम्, stolen, &c. = मुषित, q. v.
मूषीक: मूषीक, अस्, आ, m. f. = मूषिक, a rat, mouse.
मूष्यायण: मूष्यायण मूष्यायण, अस्, आ, अम्, born of unknown parents, (probably for आमुष्यायण।)
मूसरिःफ: मूसरिःफ मूसरिः-फ and मूसरीफ, अस्, m., N. of the fourth Yoga.
मृ: मृ मृ, cl. 6. A., but in Perf., Futures, and Cond. only P. (ep. occasionally both P. and A. in all the tenses), म्रियते, ममार, मरिष्यति, अमृत, मृषीष्ट, मर्तुम् (epic forms म्रियति, म्रियन्ति, म्रियेयम्, म्रियेयुस्, मम्रे, मम्रिरे, Ved. forms मरति, मरते, मराति, अमरत्; the form मुमुरत्, Ṛg-veda VIII. 97, 3, is said by Sāy. to = मारयतु = विनाशयतु), to die, de-cease, depart from life: Pass. म्रियते (sometimes used impersonally with inst. c.), Perf. मम्रे, Aor. अमारि: Caus. मारयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अमीमरत्, to cause to die, kill, slay, put to death: Desid. मु-मूर्षति, to wish to die, be about to die, be at the point of death, face death: Intens. मेम्रीयते, मर्-मर्ति; [cf. Zend mar, ‘to die;’ mare-ta, ‘mortal;’ maretan, ‘man:’ Gr. ἄ-μβρο-το-ς, ἀμ-βρόσ-ιο-ς, βρο-τό-ς, μορ-τό-ς, μαραίν-ω, μαρα-σ-μό-ς: Lat. mor-i-or-r, mor-(ti)-s, mor-tuu-us, mort-âli-s, mor-bu-s, mar-c-e-o, marc-e-sc-o, marc-i-du-s: Angl. Sax. uta-mœran, mordher, myrdhro, mordh: Goth. maur-th-r: Slav. mr-e-ti, ‘to die;’ mor-u, ‘plague, death;’ s-mrĭ-tĭ, ‘death;’ mrĭ-tvu, ‘a dead man:’ Russ. u-miraju, ‘to die;’ mertvyi, ‘dead;’ s-mer-tj, ‘death:’ Lith. mir-ti, ‘to die;’ már-a-s, ‘plague;’ mórai, ‘bier;’ s-mer-ti, ‘death:’ Hib. marbhaim, ‘I kill, slay;’ marbhan, ‘a corpse, dead body.’]
मुमूर्षु: मुमूर्षु, उस्, उस्, उ, wishing to die, being about to die, being at the point of death.
मृत: मृत, अस्, आ, अम्, dead, deceased, deathlike, tor-pid, useless; calcined, reduced (said of metals); (अम्), n. death, (मृतेभ्यः प्रमृतं यान्ति, they pass from death to death, i. e. from one death to another); = चैत्य, a grave; begging, food or alms obtained by begging. —मृत-कल्प, अस्, आ, अम्, almost dead, well-nigh dead, insensible, fainted. —मृत-गृह, अम्, n. ‘house of the dead,’ a grave. —मृत-चेल, अम्, n. the garments of the dead (worn by Caṇḍālas). —मृत-जीवन, अस्, ई, अम्, giving life to the dead, raising the dead to life. —मृत-दार, अस्, m. one whose wife is dead, a widower. —मृत-नाथ, अस्, आ, अम्, one whose lord is dead. —मृत-निर्यातक, अस्, m. one who carries out dead bodies. —मृत-प, अस्, m. a person who guards a dead body. —मृत-पा, आस्, m. a person who watches a dead body, a man of the lowest caste who collects dead men's clothes, conveys dead bodies to the river side to be burnt, executes criminals, &c.; N. of an Asura. —मृत-पुत्र, अस्, m. one whose son is dead. —मृत-प्रज, अस्, आ, अम्, one whose children are dead. —मृत-प्राय, अस्, आ, अम्, well-nigh dead, almost dead. —मृत-भ्रज्, Ved. one who has lost the power of erection. —मृत-मत्त or मृत-मत्तक, अस्, m. a jackal. —मृत-मनस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, Ved. unconscious, insensible. —मृत-वत्, ind. like one dead. —मृत-वत्सा or मृत-वत्सिका, f., Ved. whose offspring or first-born child dies. —मृत-वस्त्र-भृत्, त्, त्, त्, wearing a dead man's clothes. —मृत-वार्षिक, the period of the short rains (said to last twenty-four hours, while the वार्षिक last a month, and the दीर्घ-वार्षिक three months all but a day). —मृत-शङ्का, f. the fear entertained of a person being dead. —मृत-शब्द, अस्, m., Ved. report of any one's death. —मृत-संस्कार, अस्, m. funeral rites or ceremonies. —मृत-सञ्जी-वन, अस्, ई, अम्, reviving the dead, bringing the dead to life; (ई), f. the revival of a dead person, a Mantra for reviving the dead; (अम्), n. the revival of a dead person; bringing the dead to life. —मृत-सञ्जीविन्, ई, इनी, इ, reviving or giving life to the dead, bringing the dead to life; (इनी), f. epithet of a kind of formula; a species of shrub (= गोरक्ष-दुग्धा); N. of a commentary on Piṅgala's Chan-daḥ-śāstra. —मृत-सूतक, अम्, n. bringing forth a still-born child; (अस्), m. a term applied to quicksilver in a particular state. —मृत-स्नात, अस्, आ, अम्, one who has washed himself after a death or funeral, bathed after mourning; dying immediately after ablution. —मृत-स्नान, अम्, n. ablution after a death or funeral. —मृत-स्व-मोक्तृ, ता, m. ‘let-ting alone, i. e. not taking, the property of deceased person,’ an epithet of Kumāra-pāla. —मृत-हार, अस्, or मृत-हारिन्, ई, m. a carrier of the dead, one who bears a corpse to the funeral pile. —मृताङ्ग (°त-अङ्°), अम्, n. a dead body, corpse. —मृताङ्-गार (°त-अङ्°), अस्, m. a proper N. —मृताण्ड (°त-अण्°), अम्, n. a seemingly dead or lifeless egg (as opposed to a living egg or testicle; cf. मार्-ताण्ड, ‘a bird’ which is produced from the seemingly lifeless egg); (अस्), m. the sun; [cf. मृतण्ड।] —मृताधान (°त-आध्°), अम्, n. placing a dead body (on the funeral pile). —मृताशन (°त-अश्°), अस्, आ, अम्, living upon the dead. —मृताशौच (°त-आश्°), अम्, n. impurity contracted through the death of any one. —मृताहन् or मृताहस् (°त-अह्°), n. the day of any one's death. —मृतोत्थित (°त-उत्°), अस्, आ, अम्, risen from the dead. —मृ-तोद्भव (°त-उद्°), अस्, m. the sea, ocean; (per-haps for अमृतोद्भव।)
मृत मृत। See under rt. मृ, p. 789, col. 3.
मृतक: मृतक, अस्, अम्, m. n. a dead man, a corpse; (अम्), n. death, decease. —मृतकान्तक (°क-अन्°), अस्, m. ‘consumer of corpses, demolisher of carcases,’ a jackal.
मृति: मृति, इस्, f. death, dying; [cf. Lat. mors (mor-ti-s); Slav. s-mrĭ-tĭ; Lith. s-mèr-ti-s.]
मृत्यु: मृत्यु, उस्, m. (ep. also f.), death, dying, decease, demise, (a hundred kinds of death are enumerated from disease or accident, and one natural kind from old age); Death personified, the god of death, Yama the judge of the dead; an epithet of Viṣṇu; N. of a son of A-dharma by Nir-ṛti; an epithet of Brahmā; N. of Māyā; of Kali; of a teacher; of Vyāsa in the sixth Dvāpara; of one of the eleven Rudras; of an Ekāha; of the eighth astrological house; of the seventeenth astrological Yoga; the god of love [cf. मार]; मृत्योर् हरः and मृत्योर् विकर्ण-भासे, names of Sāmans; अकाल-मृत्यु, ‘untimely death,’ N. of a being attendant on Padma-pāṇi. —मृत्यु-कन्या, f. the goddess of death. —मृत्यु-जित्, त्, m. ‘conqueror of death,’ N. of an author, (also called Mṛtyujid-bhaṭṭāraka); N. of a work by the same author. —मृत्युञ्-जय, अस्, आ, अम्, overcoming death; (अस्), m. ‘death-conqueror,’ an epithet of Śiva; N. of an author. —मृत्युञ्जय-तीर्थ and मृत्यु-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of two Tīrthas. —मृत्यु-तूर्य, अम्, n. a kind of drum beaten at funeral ceremonies. —मृत्यु-द, अस्, आ, अम्, death-giving, fatal. —मृत्यु-दूत, अस्, m., Ved. ‘death-messen-ger,’ one who brings the news of a death. —मृत्यु-द्वार, अम्, n. death's door, the door that leads to death. —मृत्यु-नाशक, अस्, m. ‘death-averter,’ quicksilver. —मृत्यु-नाशन, अम्, n. ‘death-de-stroying,’ the drink of immortality. —मृत्यु-पथ, अस्, m. a way or path leading to death. —मृत्यु-पा, आस्, m. ‘death-quaffing,’ an epithet of Śiva. —मृत्यु-पाश, अस्, m. death's noose (these are variously rec-koned at 101 or even more than 1000 in number). —मृत्यु-पुष्प, अस्, m. ‘death-flowered,’ the sugar cane (so called because it dies after the loss of its flowers). —मृत्यु-प्रतिबद्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, subject or liable to death. —मृत्यु-फल, अस्, m. a species of cucumber, = महा-काल = महाकाल-फल; (आ or ई), f. the plantain, Musa Sapientum; (अम्), n. a sort of fruit considered as poisonous. —मृत्यु-बन्धु, उस्, m., Ved. ‘companion of death,’ a man. —मृत्यु-बीज, see मृत्यु-वीज। —मृत्यु-भङ्गुरक, अस्, m. a drum beaten at funeral ceremonies. —मृत्यु-भय, अम्, n. danger or peril of death; fear of death. —मृत्यु-भीत, अस्, आ, अम्, afraid of death. —मृत्यु-भृत्य, अस्, m. a servant of death; (figuratively) sickness, ma-lady, disease. —मृत्यु-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having death, subject to death. —मृत्यु-मार, अस्, m. मृगमाण: मृगमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, seeking, pursuing, hunt-ing.

मृगयस्: मृगयस्, आस्, m., Ved. a wild animal.

मृगयु: मृगयु, उस्, m. a huntsman; a jackal; an epi-thet of Brahmā.
मृगव: मृगव, (with Buddhists) a particular high number.
मृगव्य: मृगव्य, अम्, n. hunting, the chase; the butt or mark in archery, a target.
मृगार: मृगार, अस्, m., N. of the author of the hymns Atharva-veda IV. 23-29; of a minister of Prasena-jit [cf. मृग-धर]; = मृगार-सूक्त below. —मृगार-सूक्त, अम्, n. the hymns Atharva-veda IV. 23-29. —मृगारेष्टि (°र-इष्°), इस्, f. epithet of Taittirīya-saṃhitā IV. 7, 15, and of Atharva-veda IV. 23-29.
मृगित: मृगित, अस्, आ, अम्, chased, hunted after, sought, searched for, pursued.

मृग्य: मृग्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be hunted after, to be sought or inquired after.
मृग्यमाण: मृग्यमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, being searched for, being sought or inquired after.
मृच्: मृच् मृच्, क्, f. (fr. rt. मर्च्), Ved. threaten-ing; injury; a snare; [cf. अ-मृक्त।]
मृचय: मृचय, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. (perhaps) liable to destruction or decay, transitory, going, moving.
मृच्चय: मृच्चय मृच्-चय, मृच्-छकटिका। See under 2. मृद्, p. 792, col. 2.
मृछ्: मृछ् मृछ् or मर्छ्, cl. 6. A. मृच्छते, &c., to pass away, perish.
मृज्: मृज् 1. मृज् [cf. rts. मार्ज्, मृश्], cl. 2. P. मार्ष्टि (ep. also A. मार्ष्टे, 3rd pl. मृजन्ति or मार्जन्ति; Ved. 3rd sing. मृजति, -ते), Impf. अमार्ट् (3rd pl. अमृजन् or अमार्जन्), Impv. मार्ष्टु (2nd sing. मृड्ढि), ममार्ज (3rd pl. ममृजुस् or ममार्जुस्), मार्जिष्यति or मार्क्ष्-यति (Ved. म्रक्ष्यते), अमार्जीत् or अमार्क्षीत् (Ved. अमृक्षत्), मार्जितुम् or मार्ष्टुम्, to wipe, rub, cleanse, clean, purify, wash off, clear away; to rub, stroke; to make smooth or glossy, curry (as a horse); to deck, adorn, make ready; (A.) to wipe off (impu-rity from one's self) upon some one else (loc. c.); to go (Ved.); cl. 1. P. मर्जति, मृञ्जति, &c., to sound, (in this sense connected with rts. मुज्, मुञ्ज्, cf. rt. मार्ज्); cl. 10. P. A. or Caus. मार्जयति, -ते (Ved. मर्जयति, -ते), -यितुम्, to wipe off; to wash or cleanse one's self (in this sense only A.), purify one's self, become purified; to adorn; to move about, (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda VII. 39, 3. मर्जयन्त = परिचर्यन्ते): Pass. मृज्यते, Aor. अमार्जि, to be wiped or washed, &c.: Caus. मार्ज-यति, -यितुम्, Aor. अममार्जत् or अमीमृजत्, to cause to wipe or cleanse, &c.: Desid. मिमार्जिषति or मिमृक्षति: Intens. मरीमृज्यते (Ved. मर्-मृज्यते), मरीमार्ष्टि, मरिमार्ष्टि, मर्मार्-ष्टि, to rub or wipe off repeatedly, to keep rubbing or wiping off; (A.) to be continually cleansing one's self; [cf. Zend marez, ‘to wipe:’ Gr. ἀμέλγ-ω, ἄμελξις, ἀμολγεύ-ς, ἀμολγαῖο-ς, ἀμέργ-ω, ἀμοργός, ἀμόργη, ὀμόργ-νυ-μι, ὄμοργ-μα, γλάγος (for μλάγος), γάλα, γάλακτος (for μλακτο): Lat. mulg-e-o, mulc-tu-s, mulctra, mulctru-m, merg-a, merg-e(t)s, mulier, lac (for mlac): Old Germ. milch-u, ‘I milk:’ Goth. miluks, ‘milk:’ Angl. Sax. meoluc, meolc, melcan, mearc, mearcian, ge-mearc: Slav. mlz-a: Lith. melz-u: perhaps Hib. breugaim, ‘I soothe;’ bleaghaim, ‘I milk.’]
2. मृज्, ट्, ट्, ट्, (at the end of a comp.) wiping, rubbing; wiping off or away.
1. मृज्; add — also cl. 1. 3rd sing. मार्जति, 2nd sing. Impv. A. मार्जस्व।
मृज: मृज, अस्, m. a kind of drum.
मृजत्: मृजत्, अन्, अती or अन्ती, अत्, wiping away, cleansing, effacing, (also प्र-मृजत्, Kirātārj. III. 4, 3.)

मृजित: मृजित, अस्, आ, अम्, wiped, wiped away, rubbed off, removed.
मृज्य: मृज्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be cleansed, to be purified; to be wiped away or removed (= 2. मार्ग्य).
मृष्ट: 1. मृष्ट, अस्, आ, अम् (for 2. see p. 793, col. 1), washed, cleansed, clean, pure; smeared, besmeared; prepared, dressed, savoury, (मृष्टम् अन्नम्, deli-cate food, dainties; cf. मिष्ट); (अम्), n. pepper. —मृष्ट-गन्ध, अस्, m. 2. मृष्ट, अस्, आ, अम् (for 1. and 3. see under rts. 1. मृज् and 3. मृष्), touched, stroked, rubbed, handled; considered, reflected upon, deliberated.

मृष्टि: 1. मृष्टि, इस्, f. (for 2. see p. 793, col. 1), cleans-ing, cleaning, preparation, dressing (of food, Manu III. 255); a savoury repast, (according to Kullūka = अन्नादेः संस्कार-विशेष।)
2. मृष्टि, इस्, f. (for 1. and 3. see p. 792, col. 1, and this page, col. 2), touching, stroking, contact.

मृष्टेरुक: मृष्टेरुक, अस्, आ, अम्, eating dainties or deli-cacies, luxurious, selfish; liberal.
मृड्: मृड् मृड् (Ved. मृऌ), cl. 6. 9. P. मृ-डति, मृड्नाति, ममर्ड, मर्डिष्यति, अमर्डीत्, मर्डितुम् (Ved. cl. 6. P. मृऌअति, cl. 10. मृडन: मृडन, अम्, n. the act of showing grace or favour, making happy, delighting.

मृडाकु: मृडाकु, उस्, m. a proper N.

मृडितृ: मृडितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, Ved. = मर्डितृ, one who shows favour.
मृडीक: मृडीक, अस्, m. ‘gracious,’ N. of Śiva; a fish; (according to some) an antelope, [cf. मृग।]

मृळयाकु: मृऌअयाकु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. gracious, kindly dis-posed, showing grace, making happy.
मृळीक: मृऌईक, अम्, n., Ved. grace, mercy, kindness; (अस्), m., N. of a Vāsiṣṭha, author of the hymns Ṛg-veda IX. 97, 25-27, and X. 150.
मृडङ्कण: मृडङ्कण मृडङ्कण, अस्, m. (according to Uṇādi-s. IV. 24. fr. rt. मृड्), a child, boy.
मृण्: मृण् मृण् (connected with rts. मृ, मॄ), cl. 6. P. मृणति, ममर्ण, मृणितुम्, to kill, slay; [cf. Gr. μάρναμαι.]
मृणाल: मृणाल मृणाल, अस्, अम्, m. n. (said to be also ई, f.), the edible fibrous root of some kinds of lotus, a lotus fibre or small fibre attached to the stalk of a water-lily; (ई), f. a lotus fibre; (अम्), n. the root of the fragrant grass Andropogon Muricatus. —मृणाल-भङ्ग, अस्, m. the fracture of a lotus fibre. —मृणाल-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, possessing lotus fibres or roots. —मृणाल-सूत्र, अम्, n. the fibre of a lotus stalk.
मृणालक: मृणालक, अस्, आ, अम्, (at the end of comps.) = मृणाल; (इका), f. the edible root of a lotus; a proper N.
मृणालिन्: मृणालिन्, ई, m. a lotus; (इनी), f. a lotus plant; a group of lotuses; a place where lotuses grow.
