मृदित: मृदित, अस्, आ, अम्, pressed, squeezed; crushed, bruised, pounded, ground, trampled upon, trampled down, laid waste; rubbed; (अम्), n. a particular disease of the membrum virile.
मृदिनी: मृदिनी, f. good earth or soil.
मृदु: मृदु, उस्, उस् or वी, उ (compar. म्रदीयस्, su-perl. म्रदिष्ठ, q. q. v. v.; cf. rt. म्रद्, from which in Uṇādi-s. 1. 29. मृदु is said to be de-rived), ‘easily pressed or squeezed,’ soft, tender, sup-ple, flexible, pliant; mild, gentle; weak, moderate; blunt; slow; (उस्), m. the planet Saturn [cf. मन्द]; N. of a king; (वी), f. a vine with red grapes [cf. मृ-द्वीका]; (उ), n. softness, mildness, gentleness; [cf. Gr. βραδύς (fr. μραδύς like βροτό-ς fr. μροτό-ς); Lat. bardus, mollis (fr. molvis for modvis or morvis), mollities, mollīre, blandus; Old Germ. milti; Mod. Germ., Angl. Sax., and Eng. mild; Russ. molodyĭ, ‘young;’ Hib. meirbh, ‘slow, tedious, weak.’] —मृदु-कृष्णायस, अम्, n. ‘soft-iron,’ lead. —मृदु-कोष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, having relaxed bowels, relaxed, easily affected by medicine. —मृदु-क्रिया, f. the act of softening, mollify-ing. —मृदु-गण, अस्, m. = मृदु-वर्ग below. —मृदु-गन्धिक, अस्, m. a species of plant. —मृदु-गमन, अस्, आ, अम्, going softly, having a soft or gentle gait; (आ), f. a goose or female swan. —मृदु-गामिन्, ई, इनी, इ, going softly, having a soft or gentle gait. —मृदु-चर्मिन्, ई, m. a species of birch tree (= चर्मिन्). —मृदु-चाप, अस्, m., N. of a Dānava. —मृदु-च्छद, अस्, m. a species of birch tree; a kind of mountain Pīlu tree. —मृदु-जातीय, अस्, आ, अम्, somewhat soft, slightly weak. —मृदु-ता, f. or मृदु-त्व, अम्, n. softness, gentleness, tenderness, mildness, weakness; मृदु-तां गम् or व्रज्, to become mild or weak, be appeased. —मृदु-ताल, अस्, m. a species of tree (= श्री-ताल). —मृदु-तीक्ष्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, soft and violent, gentle and harsh, (used as an epithet of the two Nakṣatras Kṛttikā and Vi-śākhā.) —मृदु-त्वच्, क्, or मृदु-त्वच, अस्, m. ‘having a soft bark,’ a species of birch tree. —मृदु-पत्त्र, अस्, m. ‘soft-leafed,’ a rush, reed. —मृदु-परुष-गुण, औ, m. du. ‘the qualities of mild and harsh,’ mildness and harshness. —मृदु-पर्वक, अस्, m. or मृदु-पर्वन्, अ, n. ‘soft-jointed,’ a reed, cane. —मृदु-पाणि, इस्, इस्, इ, ‘soft-handed,’ having a delicate hand. —मृदु-पीठक, अस्, m. a kind of sheat-fish, silurus. —मृदु-पुष्प, अस्, m. ‘having soft flowers,’ Acacia Sirissa (= शिरीष). —मृदु-पूर्व, अस्, आ, अम्, commencing softly, friendly at first, gentle, tender; (अम्), ind. mildly or friendly at first, gently, tenderly, blandly, softly, coaxingly. —मृदु-प्रयत्न, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. (to be pro-nounced) with a gentle effort. —मृदु-प्रिय, अस्, m., N. of a Dānava. —मृदु-प्रौढ, अस्, आ, अम्, full of gentleness; mild and haughty. —मृदु-फल, अस्, m. ‘having soft fruit,’ N. of various plants (= विकङ्कत, विकण्टक, मधु-नालिके-रक). —मृदु-भाषिन्, ई, इणी, इ, speaking sweetly. —मृदु-मृत्स्न, अस्, आ, अम्, consisting of soft or fine particles or atoms. —मृदु-रोम-वत्, आन्, or मृदु-लोमक, अस्, m. ‘having soft hair,’ a hare. —मृदु-वर्ग, अस्, m. the group of Nakṣatras called मृदु (viz. Anu-rādhā, Citrā, Revatī, and Mṛga-śiras). —मृदु-वाच्, क्, क्, क्, ‘soft-voiced,’ mild in speech. —मृदु-वात, अस्, m. a gentle breeze, zephyr. —मृदु-विद्, त्, m., N. of a son of Śvaphalka. —मृदु-स्पर्श, अस्, आ, अम्, soft to the touch, soft. —मृदु-हृदय, अस्, आ, अम्, tender-hearted, kind. —मृदूत्पल (°दु-उत्°), अम्, n. the blue lotus, Nymphæa Cyanea. —मृद्व्-अङ्ग, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, ‘tender-limbed,’ delicately formed; (ई), f. a delicate woman; (अम्), n. tin. —मृद्व्-अवग्रह, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. easily indicating the division of the members of a compound.
मृदुक: मृदुक, अस्, आ, अम्, soft, tender, gentle; (अम्), ind. softly, gently, tenderly.
मृदुर: मृदुर, अस्, m., N. of a son of Śvaphalka, (also read मुदर।) —मृदुर-स्वन, see under भि-दुर-स्वन।
मृदुल: मृदुल, अस्, आ, अम्, soft, tender, mild, gentle; (अम्), n. water; Amyris Agallocha (= अ-गुरु).
मृदूअस्: मृदू-अस्, cl. 2. P. मृद्व्-अस्ति, &c., to be or become soft.
मृदूभाव: मृदू-भाव, अस्, m. the becoming soft.
मृदूभू: मृदू-भू, cl. 1. P. -भवति, &c., to become soft.
मृद्यमन: मृद्यमन, अस्, आ, अम्, being crushed or bruised.
मृद्वीका: मृद्वीका, f. a vine; a bunch of grapes.
मृदङ्कुरु: मृदङ्कुरु मृदङ्कुरु, उस्, or मृदङ्कुर, अस्, m. the green pigeon, Columba Hariala.
मृदङ्ग: मृदङ्ग मृदङ्ग, अस्, m. (according to Uṇādi-s. 1. 120. fr. rt. 1. मृद्), a kind of drum, tabour; noise, din; a bamboo cane; (ई), f. a species of plant (= घोषातकी). —मृदङ्ग-फल, अस्, m. the jack or bread-fruit tree. —मृदङ्ग-फ-लिनी, f. = मृदङ्गी।
मृदङ्गक: मृदङ्गक, अम्, n. a kind of metre, four times ¯ ¯ ˘ ¯ ˘ ˘ ˘ ¯ ˘ ˘ ¯ ˘ ¯ ˘ ¯.
मृदर: मृदर मृदर, अस्, आ, अम् (perhaps fr. rt. 1. मृद्, said to be fr. rt. मृ), sporting, sportive; passing quickly away, transient.
मृध्: मृध् 1. मृध्, cl. 1. P. A. मर्धति, -ते, मर्धितुम्, (Ved.) to kill, injure, hurt; to contemn, neglect, forget, disregard, be disgusted with (with acc.); to be moist; to moisten; [cf. pro-bably Gr. μαλθακός; Goth. maurthr; Angl. Sax. mordher, mordhor; Old Germ. multjan.]
2. मृध्, त्, f., Ved. (according to Sāy.) combat, fight, battle; one who contemns or injures; an ad-versary, foe, enemy.
मृध: मृध, अम्, n. combat, fight, war, battle; (said to be also अस्, m.)
मृधस्: मृधस्, अस्, n., Ved. war, battle; contempt, indif-ference; मृधस्-कृ, to disdain, contemn, injure.
मृध्र: मृध्र, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. one who injures, an enemy; (आणि), n. pl. disdain, contempt, abuse, insult, contumely. —मृध्र-वाच्, क्, क्, क्, Ved. speaking injuriously or contumeliously, insulting.
मृन्मय: मृन्मय मृन्-मय, मृल्-लोष्ट, &c. See under 2. मृद्।
मृळ्: मृळ् मृऌ, Ved. See under rt. मृड्।
मृश्: मृश् 1. मृश् (often confounded with rt. 1. मृष्), cl. 6. P. मृशति (some-times also A. मृशते), ममर्श, मर्क्ष्यति or म्रक्ष्यति, अमृक्षत् or अमार्क्षीत् or अम्रा-क्षीत्, मर्ष्टुम् or म्रष्टुम्, to touch, stroke, handle; to rub, rub off; to touch (mentally), con-sider, reflect, deliberate; [cf. Lat. mulc-e-o, (pro-bably also) mulc-o: perhaps Hib. mear, ‘a finger, toe;’ mearacht, ‘fingering or touching a musical instrument.’]
2. मृश्, क्, क्, क्, (at the end of comps.) one who strokes or touches, a stroker, (see Gram. 181.)
मृशय: मृशय मृशय for मृचय, q. v.
मृष्: मृष् 1. मृष् (often confounded with rt. 1. मृश्), cl. 4. P. A. मृष्यति, -ते (rarely cl. 1. P. A. मर्षति, -ते), ममर्ष, म-मृषे, मर्षिष्यति, -ते, अमर्षीत् (ep. अमृ-षत्), अमर्षिष्ट, मर्षितुम्, to bear, endure, suffer; to permit, let, allow; to bear patiently, (मु-हूर्तम् मृष्यताम्, have patience for a moment); to forget, let slip (from the mind), neglect; to par-don, forgive, excuse; cl. 10. P. A. or Caus. मर्ष-यति, -ते (according to Vopa-deva also मृषयति, -ते), -यितुम्, Aor. अमीमृषत् or अममर्षत्, अमीमृषत or अममर्षत, to bear, suffer; endure, tolerate, allow, put up with; to forgive, excuse, pardon; [cf. Goth. marzjan; Old Germ. marrjan; Angl. Sax. myrran.]
2. मृष्, ट्, ट्, ट्, (at the end of comps.) one who bears or endures, bearing, (see Gram. 181.)
मृष् 3. मृष् (connected with rt. 2. मिष्), cl. 1. P. मर्षति, ममर्ष, मर्षितुम्, to sprinkle, pour out.
मृषा: मृषा, ind. (probably an old inst. fr. a form मृष, and perhaps meaning originally ‘with for-getfulness’), in vain, to no purpose, uselessly; wrongly, incorrectly, falsely, untruly, untruthfully, lyingly, feignedly, (sometimes used like a substantive, e. g. वर्जनीयम् मृषा बुधैः, untruthfulness is to be avoided by the wise); मृषा कृ, to act falsely, feign; Mṛṣā, as ‘Untruth,’ is personfied as the wife of A-dharma. —मृषा-ज्ञान, अम्, n. false or spu-rious knowledge, ignorance, folly. —मृषा-त्व, अम्, n. incorrectness, falsity. —मृषा-दान, अम्, n. ‘false gift,’ feigned or insincere promise of a gift. —मृषा-दृष्टि, इस्, इस्, इ, having a false view or opinion. —मृषाध्यायिन् (°षा-अध्°), ई, m. a species of crane, Ardea Nivea, (compared to a reli-gious hypocrite, hence its names तापस, दाम्भिक, तीर्थ-सेविन्।) —मृषानुशासिन् (°षा-अन्°), ई, इनी, इ, punishing unjustly. —मृषा-भाषिन्, ई, इणी, इ, speaking falsely or untruthfully, a liar. —मृषार्-थक (°षा-अर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having a false sense or meaning, untrue, absurd; (अम्), n. an impossibility, absurdity (as a rabbit's horn, &c.). —मृषा-वाच्, क्, f. an untrue or satirical speech, sarcasm, irony. —मृषा-वाद, अस्, m. an untrue speech, lie; sarcasm, irony; (अस्, आ, अम्), speaking falsely or untruthfully, a liar. —मृषा-वादिन्, ई, इनी, इ, speaking falsely or untruthfully, a liar; (ई), m. one who brings forward an unjust or unfounded charge, a false accuser. —मृषोद्य (°षा-उद्°), अस्, आ, अम्, speaking untruthfully, lying, a liar; (अम्), n. untruthfulness, lying.
मृषाय: मृषाय (fr. मृषा), Nom. A. मृषायते, &c., to err, be mistaken, hold a wrong notion or opinion.
मृषालक: मृषालक मृषालक, अस्, m. the mango tree.
मॄ: मॄ मॄ (connected with rts. मृ and मृण्), cl. 9. P. मृणाति, ममार, मरिष्-यति, अमारीत्, मर्तुम्, Ved. to bruise, smash, crush, break; kill, hurt, injure.
मे: मे मे, cl. 1. A. मयते, ममे, मास्यते, अमास्त, मातुम्, to change, exchange, barter: Caus. मापयति, -यितुम्, to cross over, (perhaps fr. rt. 3. मा): Desid. मित्सते: Intens. मेमीयते, मामेति, मामाति; [cf. Gr. ἀ-μείβ-ω, ἀμείβ-ο-μαι, ἀ-μεύ-σα-οθαι, παρ-αμείβ-εινμ ἀμοιβή, μοῖ-το-ς: Lat. me-a-re, mov-e-o, mô-tu-s, mô-tio, mô-men-tu-m, mu-ta-re, mû-tuu-s, communis, munus: Goth. maithms, maidjan, ga-mains: Angl. Sax. madhm, mane, man, ge-mœne: Slav. me-na, ‘change:’ Lith. mai-na-s, ‘exchange;’ mainý-ti, ‘to change, exchange.’]
मापयान: मापयान, अस्, आ, अम्, (fr. the Caus.), crossing over (fr. rt. 3. मा ?).
मेक: मेक मेक, अस्, m. (probably onomato-poetic), a goat.
मेकल: मेकल मेकल, अस्, m., N. of a mountain; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people, (also wrongly read मेलक); (आ), f., N. of a river (= मेकल-कन्-यका). —मेकल-कन्यका or मेकल-कन्या, f. ‘daughter of Mekala,’ an epithet of the Narmadā river. —मेकलकन्यका-तट, N. of a district. —मेकलाद्रि (°ल-अद्°), इस्, m. the Mekala moun-tain. —मेकलाद्रि-जा, f. ‘sprung from the Mekala mountain,’ an epithet of the Narmadā river.
मेक्षण: मेक्षण मेक्षण, अम्, n. (fr. मिक्ष्), Ved. a wooden stick or spoon for stirring up the Caru or taking small portions from it.
मेखला: मेखला मेखला, f. a girdle, belt, waist-belt, (in one or two instances अस् or अम्, m. or n.); the zone of a woman; the triple zone worn by the first three classes, (according to Manu II. 42. that of a Brāhman ought to be of मुञ्ज, that of a Kṣatriya of मूर्वा, that of the Vaiśya of शण or hemp); the girth of a horse; a band or fillet; anything girding or surrounding [cf. सागर-म्°]; a sword-belt, baldric; a sword-knot or string fastened to the hilt; the place of the girdle, the hips; the cords or lines drawn round an altar, or on the four sides of the hole in which sacrificial fire is offered; the edge or slope of a mountain [cf. नि-तम्ब]; Hemionitis Cordifolia; N. of a place; of a woman; of the Narmadā river, [cf. मेकला।] —मेखल-कन्-यका = मेकल-कन्यका, q. v. —मेखला-पद, अम्, n. the place of the girdle, the hips. —मेखला-बन्ध, अस्, m. investiture with the girdle; the rites connected with such investiture. —मेखला-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. having a girdle or belt, wearing a fillet. —मेखला-विन्, ई, इनी, इ, Ved. wearing a girdle. —मेखली-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, -कर्तुम्, to put on a girdle, to put on the sacrificial string.
मेखलाल: मेखलाल, अस्, m. ‘having a girdle,’ epithet of Śiva; (according to a Scholiast = मेखलयालङ्-कृत।)
मेखलिक: मेखलिक, अस्, आ, अम्, wearing a girdle.
मेखलिन्: मेखलिन्, ई, इनी, इ, wearing a girdle; (ई), m. an epithet of Śiva; a Brāhmanical student or youth who, previous to his marriage, wears a girdle suited to his caste, Brahma-cārin.
मेघ: मेघ, अस्, m. a cloud, (काल-म्°, a black cloud); cloudy weather; a mass, multitude; a fragrant grass, Cyperus Rotundus; N. of one of the six Rāgas or musical scales; of a Rākṣasa; of the father of the fifth Arhat of the present Ava-sarpiṇī; of a poet, (also read मेच); of a mountain; (अम्), n. talc; [cf. Gr. ὀ-μίχ-λη; Goth. milh-ma, ‘a cloud;’ Lith. mig-la, ‘a mist.’] —मेघ-कफ, अस्, m. ‘cloud-phlegm,’ hail. —मेघ-कर्णा, f., N. of one of the Mātṛs attending on Skanda. —मेघ-काल, m. ‘cloud-time,’ the rainy season. —मेघ-कूटा-भिगर्जितेश्वर (°ट-अभ्°, °त-ईश्°), अस्, m., N. of a Bodhi-sattva. —मेघ-गम्भीर, अस्, आ, अम्, deep as (the rumbling of) a cloud. —मेघ-गर्-जन, अम्, n. ‘cloud-rumbling,’ thundering, thunder. —मेघ-गिरि, इस्, m., N. of a mountain. —मे-घङ्-कर, अस्, ई, अम्, ‘cloud-making,’ producing clouds. —मेघ-चिन्तक, अस्, m. ‘anxious for clouds,’ the Cātaka bird (supposed to drink only rain-water, and therefore naturally eager for rainy weather). —मेघ-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘cloud-born,’ coming from the clouds; (अस्), m. a large pearl. —मेघ-जाल, अम्, n. ‘cloud-collection,’ a mass of clouds, thick clouds; talc. —मेघ-जीवक or मेघ-जीवन, अस्, m. ‘living on clouds,’ the Cātaka bird. —मेघ-ज्योतिस्, इस्, n. (according to the Amara-koṣa, इस्, m.), ‘cloud-light,’ a flash of lightning, the fire produced from lighting. —मेघ-डम्बर, अस्, m. thunder; [cf. मेघाडम्बर।] —मेघ-तरु, उस्, m., Ved. ‘cloud-tree,’ a parti-cular form of cloud. —मेघ-तिमिर, अम्, n. ‘cloud-darkness,’ darkness resulting from a clouded sky, cloudy or rainy weather. —मेघ-त्व, अम्, n. the being a cloud, the state of a cloud, cloudiness; मे-घत्वम् उप-गम्, to become a cloud. —मेघ-दीप, अस्, m. ‘cloud-light,’ lightning. —मेघ-दुन्-दुभि, इस्, m., N. of an Asura. —मेघ-दुन्दुभि-स्वर-राज, अस्, m., N. of a Buddha. —मेघ-दूत, अस्, m. ‘cloud-messenger,’ N. of a celebrated poem by Kālidāsa. —मेघदूत-पाद-समस्या, f., N. of a work. —मेघदूताभिध (°त-अभ्°), अस्, आ, अम्, entitled ‘cloud-messenger.’ —मेघ-द्वार, अम्, n. ‘cloud-gate,’ heaven, the sky, ether. —मेघ-नाद, अस्, m. ‘cloud-noise,’ sound of rain, thunder; (अस्, आ, अम्), sounding or rumbling like thunder, making a noise like thunder; (अस्), m. an epithet of Varuṇa; N. of one of the attendants of Skanda; of a Dānava; of a son of Rāvaṇa, afterwards called Indra-jit, as having conquered Indra (see Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara-kāṇḍa XXXIV); of a frog; Amaranthus Po-lygonoides; the Palāśa tree, Butea Frondosa. —मे-घनाद-जित्, त्, m. ‘conqueror of Megha-nāda or Indra-jit, son of Rāvaṇa,’ an epithet of Lakṣamaṇa, the favourite brother of Rāma (the account of his fighting and killing Indra-jit is in Rāmāyaṇa, Yuddha-kāṇḍa LXVII-LXX). —मेघनाद-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a sacred bathing-place on the Narmadā river. —मेघनादानुलासिन् (°द-अन्°), ई, m. ‘re-joicing in the rumbling of thunder-clouds,’ a peacock. —मेघ-नादिन्, ई, इनी, इ, sounding or making a noise like thunder; crying with joy at the appear-ance of clouds; (ई), m., N. of a Dānava. —मेघ-नामन्, आ, m. ‘cloud-named,’ a fragrant grass, Cy-perus Rotundus. —मेघ-निर्घोष, अस्, m. the rumbling of clouds, thunder; (अस्, आ, अम्), sounding or making a noise like thunder. —मेघ-पङ्क्ति, इस्, f. a line or succession of clouds. —मेघ-पर्-वत, अस्, m., N. of a mountain. —मेघ-पाली, f. a proper N. —मेघ-पुष्प, अम्, n. ‘cloud-blossom,’ water; मेघय: मेघय, Nom. P. मेघयति, -यितुम्, to make cloudy, cause cloudy weather.
मेघयत्: मेघयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, Ved. making cloudy; (अन्ती), f., N. of one of the seven Kṛttikās.
मेघाय: मेघाय, Nom. A. मेघायते, -यितुम्, Ved. to form clouds, become cloudy.
मेघ्य: मेघ्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. being in the clouds; according to Pāṇ. मेघ्य at the end of a comp. = मेघम् अर्हति or मेघ इव।
मैघ: मैघ, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging to the clouds, cloudy; descended from clouds (Ved.).
मेङ्गनाथ: मेङ्गनाथ मेङ्ग-नाथ, अस्, m., N. of a race (?). —मेङ्गनाथ-भट्ट, अस्, m. a proper N.
मेच: मेच मेच, अस्, m., N. of a poet; [cf. मेघ।]
मेचक: मेचक मेचक, अस्, आ, अम् (said to be fr. rt. मच्), dark-blue, dark-coloured, black; (अस्), m. dark-blue colour, black; blackness; an eye of a peacock's tail; a teat, nipple; smoke; a cloud; Mo-ringa Pterygosperma; a kind of gem; (अम्), n. darkness; sulphuret of antimony. —मेचकापगा (°क-अप्°), f. ‘dark-blue river,’ an epithet of the Yamunā. —मेचकाभिधा (°क-अभ्°), f. a species of creeper (= पाताल-गरुडी).
मेचकचातनी: मेचकचातनी मेचकचातनी, f. a various reading for मचकचातनी, q. v.

मेट्: मेट् मेट् (= rt. म्रेट्), cl. 1. P. मेटति, मेटितुम्, to be mad.
मेटुला: मेटुला मेटुला, f. the myrobalan tree (= आमलकी).
मेठ: मेठ मेठ, अस्, m. an elephant keeper [cf. मेण्ड]; an elephant driver (= यन्तृ); a ram [cf. मेढर].

मेड्: मेड् मेड्, cl. 1. P. मेडति, &c., = rt. मेट् above.
मेडि: मेडि मेडि or मेऌइ, इस्, m., Ved. crackling, emitting sparks, rustling (said of wind, fire, &c.); any jingling or murmuring sound; (a reading मेडवस् is given for the pl. मेडयस्।)
मेढी: मेढी मेढी, f. See मेथि below.

(fr. rt. 1. मिह् + त्र; according to native lexicographers also अस्, m.), mem-brum virile, the penis; (अस्), m. a ram; [cf. मी-ढ्वस्, मेण्ढ, मेष।] —मेढ्र-चर्मन्, अ, n. or मेढ्र-त्वच्, क्, f. the fore-skin, prepuce. —मेढ्र-ज, अस्, m. an epithet of Śiva. —मेढ्र-रोग, अस्, m. venereal disease. —मेढ्र-शृङ्गी, f. मेढ्रक: मेढ्रक, अस्, m. the penis; a ram.
मेण्ढ: मेण्ढ, अस्, m. (formed fr. मेढ्र above), a ram.
मेण्ढक: मेण्ढक, अस्, m. a ram; a proper N.
मेण्ढ्र: मेण्ढ्र, अस्, m. = मेण्ढ above; membrum virile.
मेण्ठ: मेण्ठ मेण्ठ, अस्, m. an elephant keeper or feeder (= मेठ); N. of a poet (= भर्तृ-मेण्-ठ).
मेण्ड: मेण्ड, अस्, m. an elephant keeper.
मेतार्य: मेतार्य मेतार्य, अस्, m. (with Jainas) N. of one of the eleven Gaṇādhipas.

मेथ्: मेथ् मेथ् (connected with rt. मिथ्, q. v.), cl. 1. P. A. मेथति, -ते, मेथि-तुम्, to meet; (A.) to meet one another, associate; to reproach, revile; to strike, hurt, kill; to know, understand.
मेथि: मेथि, इस्, m. (perhaps connected with rt. 1. मि), a pillar, post; a pillar in the middle of a threshing-floor to which oxen are bound, any central body, (also written मेधि, मेधी, मेढी, मेठि, मेठी, f.; मेढी-भूत or मेधी-भूत, forming a solid pillar or centre); a post to which cattle are tied; a prop for supporting the shafts of a carriage; (ई), f. = मेथिका. —मेथि-ष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. standing at the post to which cattle are bound.
मेथिका: मेथिका or मेथिनी, f. a sort of grass, Trigondella Fœnum Græcum.
मेद्: मेद् मेद् = rt. 1. मिद्, q. v.
मेद: मेद मेद, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 2. मिद्), fat (= मेदस् below); a species of plant (= अलम्बुषा); a particular mixed caste (the son of a Vaideha by a Kārāvara female); N. of a serpent-demon; (आ), f. a root resembling ginger (said to be one of the eight principal medicines, used especially in cases of fever and consumption); (ई), f., see Gaṇa Gaurādi to Pāṇ. मेदक: मेदक, अस्, m. spirituous liquor used for dis-tillation.
मेदन: मेदन, अम्, n., Ved. the act of fattening.
मेदस्: मेदस्, अस्, n. fat, marrow, lymph (as one of the seven Dhātus or constituent elements of the body, and supposed to be a serous or adipose secretion that spreads amongst the muscular or fleshy fibres, per-forming the same functions to the flesh that the marrow of the bones performs to them; in Hindū physiology its proper seat is said to be the abdomen); vigour, energy (Ved.); corpulence; excessive fatness, morbid or unnatural corpulence (= मेद-दोष); a mystical term for the letter व्; [cf. perhaps Gr. μῡε-λό-ς for μεδυλό-ς; Lat. medulla for medusla or medurla.] —मेदः-पुच्छ or मेदः-पुच्छक, अस्, m. the fat-tailed sheep. —मेदः-सार, अस्, आ, अम्, one in whom the Dhātu fat predominates; (आ), f. = मेदा. —मेदस्-कृत्, त्, n. ‘fat-producing,’ the body, flesh. —मेदस्-तेजस्, अस्, n. ‘strength of the Medas,’ bone. —मेदस्-पिण्ड, अस्, m. a lump of fat. —मेदस्-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. possessed of fat, fat. —मेदस्-विन्, ई, इनी, इ, ‘having Medas,’ corpu-lent, fat; robust, stout, strong. —मेदो-गण्ड, अस्, m., Ved. a kind of fatty excrescence. —मेदो-ग्रन्थि, इस्, m. a lump or knot of fat, a fatty tumor. —मेदो-ज, अम्, n. ‘produced by Medas,’ bone. —मेदो-धरा, f. a membrane in the abdomen containing the fat, the omentum. —मेदो-ऽर्बुद, अम्, n. a fatty tumor unattended with pain. —मेदो-वती, f. = मेदा। —मेदो-वह, अम्, n. (in anatomy) a vessel con-veying fat, a lymphatic. —मेदो-वृद्धि, इस्, f. increase of fat, corpulence; enlargement of the scrotum.

मेदुर: मेदुर, अस्, आ, अम्, fat; smooth, soft, bland, unc-tuous; thick, dense; (with inst. or at the end of a comp.) thick with, as thick as, full of, covered with.
मेदुरित: मेदुरित, अस्, आ, अम्, thick, thickened, made dense; unctuous.
मेद्य: मेद्य, अस्, आ, अम्, fat; thick, consistent, (opposed to द्रव।)
मेदिनी: मेदिनी मेदिनी, f. See under मेदिन् above.
मेध्: मेध् मेध् (= rts. मिध्, मिथ्), cl. 1. P. A. मेधति, -ते, &c., to meet, associate, accompany; to hurt, kill, immolate; to revile; to understand: Caus. मेधयति, -यितुम्, to cause to understand.
मेध: मेध, अस्, आ, अम्, one who kills or immolates; (अस्), m. (also अम्, n. in Ved.), the juice of meat, broth, nourishing or strengthening drink (Ved.); marrow (especially of the sacrificial victim), sap, pith, essence (Ved.); a sacrificial animal, victim; an animal sacrifice; an offering, oblation, sacrifice in general; N. of the reputed author of Vājasaneyi-saṃhitā, 33, 92; N. of a son of Priya-vrata; see Gaṇa Pacādi to Pāṇ. III. 1, 134; (आ), f. vitality, strength, vigour, power, ability (Ved.); mental vigour or power, un-derstanding, intelligence, intellect, prudence, wisdom; retentiveness, memory; Intelligence personified as the wife of Dharma and daughter of Dakṣa; a form of Dākṣāyaṇī in Kaśmīra; a form of Saras-vatī; a symbolical expression for the letter ध्; (according to native authorities also) a sacrifice; (according to Naigh. II. 10) = धन; (आस्), f. pl. the products of the understanding, ideas, perceptions, thoughts, opinions. —मेध-ज, अस्, m. ‘sacrifice-born,’ an epithet of Viṣṇu. —मेध-पति, इस्, m., Ved. ‘lord of sacrifice,’ Rudra. —मेध-साति, इस्, f., Ved. (perhaps) expression of devotion, service or worship of the gods; (according to Sāy.) the receiv-ing or giving of the oblation. —मेधा-कार, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. inspiring mental power, causing intelli-gence, bestowing wisdom. —मेधा-कृत्, त्, त्, त्, causing mental power or intelligence; (त्), m. a species of culinary plant (= सितावर). —मेधा-चक्र, अस्, m., N. of a king. —मेधा-जनन, अस्, ई, अम्, productive of wisdom; (Ved.) N. of a rite (and of its appropriate sacred text) for producing mental and bodily strength in a new-born child or in a youth. —मेधा-जित्, त्, m. an epithet of Kātyā-yana. —मेधातिथि (°धा-अत्°), इस्, m., N. of a Kāṇva (author of the hymns Ṛg-veda 1. 12 — 23, VIII. 1, &c.; cf. मेध्यातिथि); of the father of Kaṇva; of a son of Manu Svāyambhuva; of one of the seven sages under Manu Sāvarṇa; of a son of Priya-vrata; of a lawyer or commentator on the Mānava-dharma-śāstra; of a river; a parrot [cf. मेधा-विन्]. —मेधा-रुद्र, अस्, m. an epithet of Kālidāsa. —मेधा-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, possessing wis-dom, intelligent, wise; (अती), f. a species of plant (= महा-ज्योतिष्मती); a proper N. —मेधा-वर, अस्, m. a proper N. —मेधावि-ता, f. cleverness, prudence, judiciousness. —मेधा-विन्, ई, इनी, इ, pos-sessed of mental power, intelligent, intellectual, wise, judicious, endowed with sound judgment, having a good memory; (ई), m. a learned man, sage, teacher, Pandit; a parrot [cf. मेधातिथि]; an intoxicating beverage, (in this sense perhaps an error for मा-धवी); N. of a Brāhman; of a king (son of Su-naya and father of Nṛpañ-jaya); of a son of Bhavya and of a Varṣa named after him; an epithet of Vyāḍi; (इनी), f. epithet of the wife of Brahmā. —मेधा-सूक्त, अम्, n. epithet of a particular Vedic hymn.
मेधयु: मेधयु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. full of sap or marrow, strong, powerful; (Sāy.) = सङ्ग्रामेच्छु, eager for war, or = यज्ञ-क्रमणेच्छु।
मेधस्: मेधस्, अस्, n. = मेध, a sacrifice (Ved.); (आस्), m., N. of a son of Manu Svāyambhuva; of a son of Priya-vrata; (आस्, आस्, अस्), at the end of an adj. comp. = मेधा, intelligence, knowledge, understand-ing (e. g. आत्म-मेधस्, knowing or understanding the Supreme Spirit); [cf. अल्प-म्°, दुर्-म्°।]
मेधस: मेधस, अस्, m. a proper N.
मेधिर: मेधिर, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. मेधा), Ved. wise, in-telligent, clever.
मेधिष्ठ: मेधिष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम् (superl. of मेधा-विन्), wisest, most intelligent.
मेधीयस्: मेधीयस्, आन्, असी, अस् (compar. of मेधा-विन्), wiser, more intelligent.
मेध्य: मेध्य, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. मेध), full of sap, vigorous, mighty (Ved.); fresh, uninjured (Ved.); belonging to a sacrifice; fit for a sacrifice or oblation, free from blemish (as a victim); clean, purified, pure (not defiling by contact or by being eaten); = मे-धिर, wise, intelligent, (in this sense fr. मेधा; according to Pāṇ. = मेधायाम् भवः; = मेधाम् अर्हति।) —मेध्य-तम, अस्, आ, अम्, most pure, purest. —मेध्य-तर, अस्, आ, अम्, more pure, purer. —मेध्य-ता, f. or मेध्य-त्व, अम्, n. purity, (especially) ceremonial purity. —मेध्य-मन्दिर, अस्, m., N. of an author. —मेध्य-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, consisting of pure matter. —मे-ध्यातिथि (°य-अत्°), इस्, m., N. of a Ṛṣi (a Kāṇva and author of Ṛg-veda VIII. 1, 3-29, IX. 41-43).
मेधि: मेधि मेधि, मेधी। See मेथि, p. 794, col. 3.
मेना: मेना मेना, f. a woman (Ved.); the female of any animal (Ved.); speech, = वाच् (Ved.); (ac-cording to Mādhava) the sound of thunder; (accord-ing to Sāy.) N. of the daughter of Vṛṣaṇ-aśva (the latter being sometimes called Mena); N. of an Apsaras (wife of Hima-vat and mother of Pārvatī); of a river. —मेना-जा, f. ‘daughter of Menā,’ Pār-vatī. —मेना-धव, अस्, m. ‘husband of Menā,’ Hima-vat.
मेनका: मेनका, f., N. of the daughter of Vṛṣaṇ-aśva; of an Apsaras (wife of Hima-vat). —मेनकात्मजा (°का-आत्°), f. ‘daughter of Menakā,’ Pārvatī. —मे-नका-प्राणेश, अस्, m. ‘husband of Menakā,’ Hima-vat. —मेनका-हित, अम्, n., N. of a Rāsaka or kind of drama.
मेनि: मेनि, इस्, f., Ved. a missile weapon, a thunder-bolt; a various reading for मेना, speech (Naighaṇ-ṭuka 1. 11).
मेनिला: मेनिला, f., N. of a princess.
मेनुल: मेनुल, अस्, m. a proper N.
मेनाद: मेनाद मे-नाद, अस्, आ, अम्, making the sound मे; (अस्), m. a goat; a cat; a peacock.
मेन्धिका: मेन्धिका मेन्धिका or मेन्धी, f. a plant, Lawsonia Alba (a reddish dye is extracted from its leaves, used for staining the palms of the hands, the tips and nails of the fingers, and the soles of the feet).
मेप्: मेप् मेप्, cl. 1. P. मेपति, मेपितुम्, to go, move; to worship (?).
मेब्: मेब् मेब् (= rt. मेव्), cl. 1. A. मेबते, मेबितुम्, to worship, serve.
मेम: मेम मेम, (with Buddhists) a particular high number.
मेमिष: मेमिष मेमिष, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. Intens. of rt. 1. मिष्), Ved. in अति-म्°, opening the eyes wide, staring.
मेय: मेय मेय, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. 3. मा), to be measured, measurable, to be spanned [cf. मुष्टि-म्°]; capable of being estimated, discernible.
मेरक: मेरक मेरक, अस्, m., N. of an enemy of Viṣṇu; a seat covered with bark.
मेरु: मेरु मेरु, उस्, m. (in Uṇādi-s. IV. 101, said to be fr. rt. 1. मि), N. of a fabulous mountain regarded as the Olympus of Hindū mythology, (it is said to form the central point of Jambu-dvīpa, all the planets revolving round it, and is compared to the cup or seed-vessel of a lotus, the leaves of which are formed by the different Dvīpas; its height is said to be 84, 000 Yojanas, 16, 000 of which are below the surface of the earth; its shape is variously described, as square, conical, spherical, or spiral, and its four faces are variously coloured, being white towards the east, yellow to the south, black to the west, and red to the north; the river Ganges falls from heaven on its summit, and flows thence to the surrounding worlds in four streams; the regents of the four points of the compass occupy the corres-ponding faces of the mountain, the whole of which consists of gold and gems; its summit is the resi-dence of Brahmā, and a place of meeting for the gods, Ṛṣis, Gandharvas, &c.; when not regarded as a fabulous mountain, it appears to mean the highland of Tartary north of the Himālaya); the central or most prominent bead in a rosary, large middle gem of a necklace; the most prominent finger-joint in certain positions of the fingers; N. of a Cakra-vartin; of a person mentioned in Rāja-taraṅgiṇī VIII. 1418; epithet of a particular kind of temple; N. of the palace of Gāndhārī, one of the wives of Kṛṣṇa; (उस्), f., N. of the wife of Nābhi and mother of Ṛṣabha. —मेरु-कल्प, अस्, m., N. of a Buddha. —मेरु-कूट, अस्, अम्, m. n. the summit of Meru; (अस्), m., N. of a Buddha. —मेरु-तन्त्र, अम्, n., N. of a Tantra. —मेरु-तुङ्ग, अस्, m., N. of a Jaina. —मेरु-दुहितृ, ता, f. the daughter of Meru. —मेरु-दृश्वन्, आ, आ or अरी, अ, one who has seen or visited Meru. —मेरु-देवी, f., N. of a daughter of Meru (wife of Nābhi and mother of Ṛṣabha, who was an incarnation of Viṣṇu). —मेरु-धामन्, आ, m. ‘having Meru for a habitation,’ an epithet of Śiva. —मेरु-ध्वज, अस्, m., N. of a king. —मेरु-नन्द, अस्, m., N. of a son of Sva-rocis. —मेरु-पर्वत, अस्, m. the mountain Meru. —मेरु-पुत्री, f. a daughter of Meru. —मेरु-पृष्ठ, अम्, n. the summit of Meru; मेरुक: मेरुक, अस्, m. fragrant resin, incense; N. of a district in the north-east of Madhya-deśa.
मेरुटू: मेरुटू मेरुटू, (with Buddhists) a parti-cular high number.
मेरुदु: मेरुदु, (with Buddhists) a particular high number.
मेरुण्डा: मेरुण्डा मेरुण्डा, f. a particular goddess, (probably incorrect for भेरुण्डा।)
मेल: मेल मेल, अस्, आ, m. f. (fr. rt. मिल्), meeting, coming together, union, intercourse; an assembly, company, society; (in modern dialects) a large con-course of people collected at stated periods for reli-gious or commercial purposes; a fair; (आ), f. a musical scale; (with Buddhists) a particular high number; any black substance used for writing, ink-powder, ink, (in this and the following senses pro-bably connected with Gr. μέλας); antimony, eye-salve; the indigo plant. —मेला-नन्द, अस्, आ, m. f. an ink-bottle; [cf. मेला-मन्दा below.] —मेला-नन्दाय, Nom. (? m.) or मेलान्धुक (°ला-अन्°), अस्, m. an ink-bottle. —मे-ला-मन्दा, f. an ink-bottle. —मेलाम्बु, उस्, m. an ink-bottle; (probably for मेलान्धु।)
मेलक: मेलक, अस्, m. meeting, union, coming together, intercourse; a congress, assembly, a company [cf. नटक-म्°]; मेलकं कृ, to assemble together; ग्रह-मेलक, a conjunction of the planets. —मे-लक-लवण, अम्, n. a kind of salt (= मृत्तिका-लवण; cf. क्षार-मेलक, क्षार-मृत्तिका).
मेलन: मेलन, अम्, n. the act of meeting, union, coming together, junction, assembling, associating with; an encounter; mixing with, mixture; adding to.
मेलयत्: मेलयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत् (fr. the Caus.), causing to be mixed or added to, mixing, adding.
मेलापक: मेलापक, अस्, m. (fr. the Caus.), uniting, bring-ing together; conjunction (of planets).
मेलायन: मेलायन, अम्, n. mixing together, combination.
मेलु: मेलु and मेलुद, (with Buddhists) a particular high number.
मेव्: मेव् मेव् (= rts. म्लेव्, मेब्), cl. 1. A. मेवते, मेवितुम्, to worship, serve.
मेवाड: मेवाड मेवाड, अस्, m., N. of a man.
मेवार्य: मेवार्य मेवार्य for मेतार्य, q. v.
मेशिका: मेशिका मेशिका in काल-म्°, q. v.
मेशी: मेशी मेशी, f., Ved. epithet of water in a particular formula, (also read मेषी।)
मेष: मेष मेष, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 2. मिष्; accord-ing to some fr. rt. 1. मिष्), a ram, wether, sheep, (in Ved. applied also to a fleece or anything woollen); the sign of the zodiac Aries, or the first arc of 30° in a circle; a kind of drug; a species of plant [cf. मेष-कुसुम, मेष-पुष्पा]; N. of a demon said to possess children; (आ), f. a kind of carda-moms; (ई), f. an ewe; Nardostachys Jatamansi; Dalbergia Ougeinensis; [cf. काल-म्°।] —मेष-कम्बल, अस्, m. a sheep's fleece or woollen dress serving for an outer garment, a woollen rug or blanket. —मेष-कुसुम, अस्, m. Cassia Tora; [cf. मेषाक्षि-कुसुम।] —मेष-पाल or मेष-पा-लक, अस्, m. a shepherd. —मेष-पुष्पा, f. a species of plant. —मेष-मांस, अम्, n. the flesh of sheep, mutton. —मेष-यूथ, अम्, n. a flock of sheep. —मेष-लोचन, अस्, m. Cassia Tora. —मेष-वल्ली, f. Odina Pinnata. —मेष-वाहिन्, ई, इनी, इ, riding on a ram; (इनी), f., N. of one of the Mātṛs attending on Skanda, (also read मेघ-वाहिनी।) —मेष-विषाणिका, f. = मेष-शृङ्गी, q. v. —मेष-शृङ्ग, अस्, m. a species of tree (enumerated among the द्रुमाणां राजानः); a species of poisonous plant; (ई), f. Cassia Tora.
मेषक: मेषक, अस्, m. a species of vegetable, = जीव-शाक; (इका), f. an ewe; [cf. काल-मेषिका।]
मेषाय: मेषाय, Nom. A. मेषायते, &c., to act like a goat.
मेषायित: मेषायित, अस्, आ, अम्, acting like a ram or goat.

मेह: मेह मेह, अस्, m. (according to some also) अम्, n. (fr. rt. 1. मिह्), making water; urine, (मे-हं कृ, to make water; अ-मेह, retention of urine); urinary disease, excessive flow of urine, dia-betes; a ram (= मेष); a goat; [cf. Gr. μοιχός.] —मेह-घ्नी, f. ‘curing diabetes,’ Indian saffron. —मेह-हाट, N. of a place; [cf. मेद-पाट।]
मेहत्: मेहत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, urining, passing urine.

मेहिन्: मेहिन्, ई, इनी, इ, (at the end of comps.) making water; suffering from a particular urinary disease.

मैत्राबार्हस्पत्य: मैत्राबार्हस्पत्य, Ved. belonging or pertain-ing to Mitra and Bṛhas-pati.
मैत्रायण: मैत्रायण, अम्, n. (fr. मैत्र + अयन), be-nevolence; (अस्), m. a patronymic, see Gaṇa Naḍādi to Pāṇ. IV. 1. 89, (in this sense fr. 1. मित्र); N. of the author of a Gṛhya-sūtra; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a school (named after Maitri); (ई), f., N. of the mother of Pūrṇa; of a female teacher. —मैत्रा-यण-गृह्य-पद्धति, इस्, f., N. of a work by Prathama-puruṣa on the sixteen Saṃskāras.
मैत्रायणक: मैत्रायणक, see Gaṇa Arīhaṇāid to Pāṇ. IV. 2, 80.
मैत्रायणि: मैत्रायणि or मैत्रायणी, N. of an Upaniṣad.
मैत्रायणीय: मैत्रायणीय, आस्, m. pl., N. of a school. —मै-त्रायणीय-परिशिष्ट, अम्, n., N. of a work.
मैत्रावरुण: मैत्रावरुण, अस्, ई, अम्, Ved. descended or derived from Mitra and Varuṇa, of or belonging to them; (अस्), m. a patronymic (see Ṛg-veda VII. 33, 11); of Agastya; of Vālmīki; epithet of one of the officiating priests (the first assistant of the Hotṛ, who was also called Pra-śāstṛ; cf. कोकिल-म्°). —मैत्रावरुण-श्रुति, इस्, f., N. of a work.
मैत्रावरुणि: मैत्रावरुणि, इस्, m. the son of Mitra and Varuṇa, a patronymic of Mānya or Agastya; of Vasiṣṭha; of Vālmīki.
मैत्रावरुणीय: मैत्रावरुणीय, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. relating to the Maitrāvaruṇa Ṛtvij; (अम्), n. the office of the preceding.
मैत्रि: मैत्रि, इस्, m., Ved., N. of a teacher (from whom the Maitry-upaniṣad derives its title).
मैत्रिक: मैत्रिक, अम्, n. (fr. 1. मित्र or मैत्र), a friendly office, (used at the end of an adj. comp.)
मैत्रिन्: मैत्रिन्, ई, इणी, इ (fr. मैत्र), friendly, benevo-lent, a friend.
मैत्रेय: मैत्रेय, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मैत्री), friendly, re-lating to a friend, benevolent; (अस्), m. (fr. मि-त्रयु), a patronymic of Kauṣārava; of Glāva, (according to a Scholiast a metronymic fr. मित्रा); N. of a Bodhi-sattva and future Buddha; of the Vidūṣaka in the Mṛc-chakaṭikā; of a grammarian (= मैत्रेय-रक्षित); a particular mixed caste, = मैत्रेयक; (ई), f., N. of an Upaniṣad (pro-bably as composed by Maitri); of the wife of Yājña-valkya; of certain other women. —मैत्रेय-रक्-षित, अस्, m., N. of a grammarian. —मैत्रेय-वन, अम्, n., N. of a forest. —मैत्रेय-सूत्र, अम्, n., N. of a Sūtra work.
मैत्रेयक: मैत्रेयक, अस्, m., N. of a particular mixed caste or degraded tribe (the offspring of a Vaideha father by an Ayogavī, whose business is to praise great men and announce the dawn by ringing a bell, Manu X. 33); (इका), f. descent from Mitrayu; a contest between friends or allies (= मित्र-युद्-ध).
मैथिल: मैथिल मैथिल, अस्, ई, अम्, relating or be-longing to Mithilā; (अस्), m. a king of Mithilā; (आस्), m. pl. the people of Mithilā; (ई), f. an epithet of Sītā (daughter of Janaka, king of Mithilā). —मै-थिल-वाचस्-पति, इस्, m. a proper N.
मैथिलिक: मैथिलिक, आस्, m. pl. the inhabitants of Mithilā.
मैथिलेय: मैथिलेय, अस्, m. a metronymic from Maithilī.
मैथुन: मैथुन मैथुन, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मिथुन), paired, coupled, forming a pair or one of each sex; united by marriage; relating or belonging to copu-lation, (मैथुनं वासस्, a garment worn during sexual intercourse); entered into (as a marriage) for the sake of cohabitation; (अम्), n. copulation, coitus, sexual intercourse or connection; union, con-nection; marriage, matrimony, (at the end of an adj. comp. मैथुन forms its fem. in आ।) —मै-थुन-गत, अस्, आ, अम्, engaged in copulation. —मैथुन-ज्वर, अस्, m. the excitement of sexual passion. —मैथुन-धर्मिन्, ई, इणी, इ, cohabiting, copulating. —मैथुन-वैराग्य, अम्, n. abstinence from sexual indulgence. —मैथुनी-भाव, अस्, m. (fr. मैथुनी-भू), copulation, sexual union.
मैथुनिक: मैथुनिक (at the end of a comp.) = मैथु-निन्।
मैथुनिन्: मैथुनिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having sexual intercourse, sexually united; (ई), m. one who has had sexual connection with a woman; Ardea Sibirica, [cf. कामिन्।]
मैथुन्य: मैथुन्य, अस्, आ or -नी (?), अम्, proceeding from sexual passion, caused by the desire for sexual union; relating to copulation.
मैधातिथ: मैधातिथ मैधातिथ, अस्, ई, अम्, Ved. re-lating to Medhātithi; (अम्), n., N. of a Sāman.
मैधाव: मैधाव, अस्, m. (fr. मेधा-विन्), the son of a wise man.
मैधावक: मैधावक, अम्, n. (fr. मेधा-विन्), intelli-gence, prudence, wisdom.
मैध्यातिथ: मैध्यातिथ, अम्, n. (fr. मेध्यातिथि), N. of a Sāman.
मैनाक: मैनाक मैनाक, अस्, m. (fr. मेना), N. of a mountain (son of Hima-vat by Menā or Menakā, and said to have alone retained his wings when Indra clipped those of the other mountains; according to some this mountain was situated between the southern point of the Indian peninsula and Laṅkā); N. of a Daitya. —मैनाक-स्वसृ, सा, f. ‘sister of Maināka,’ an epithet of Pārvatī.
मैनाल: मैनाल मैनाल or मैनिक, अस्, m. (fr. मीन), a fisher, fisherman.
मैनेय: मैनेय मैनेय, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people.
मैन्द: मैन्द मैन्द, अस्, m., N. of an ape or monkey-demon killed by Kṛṣṇa. —मैन्द-मर्-दन, अस्, or मैन्द-हन्, हा, m. ‘killer of Mainda,’ an epithet of Viṣṇu or Kṛṣṇa.
मैमत: मैमत मैमत and मैमतायन, अस्, and मैमतायनि, इस्, m. (fr. मिमत), patronymics.
मैरव: मैरव मैरव, अस्, ई, अम्, relating or be-longing to mount Meru.
मैरावण: मैरावण मैरावण, अस्, m., N. of an Asura.
मैरेय: मैरेय मैरेय, अस्, अम्, m. n. (according to the lexicographers only अम्, n.), a kind of intoxi-cating drink (extracted from the blossoms of the Lythrum Fructicosum, with sugar, &c.).
मैरेयक: मैरेयक, अस्, अम्, m. n. = मैरेय above; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a mixed caste.
मैलिन्द: मैलिन्द मैलिन्द, अस्, m. a bee.
मैश्रधान्य: मैश्रधान्य मैश्रधान्य, अम्, n. (fr. मिश्र-धान्य), a dish prepared by mixing various kinds of grain.
मैहिक: मैहिक मैहिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मेह), relat-ing to urinary disease.
मो: मो मो (मा + उ), Ved. and not, nor, not indeed (see under 1. मा).
मोक: मोक मोक, अम्, n. (fr. rt. 2. मुच्), the cast-off skin of an animal [cf. निर्-म्°]; (ई), f., Ved. night.
मोक्तुकाम: मोक्तु-काम, अस्, आ, अम्, wishing to let go, de-siring to shoot or cast.
मोक्तृ: मोक्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ, a releaser, liberator, deliverer, rescuer, saviour; one who pays or discharges (a debt), a payer.
मोक्ष्: मोक्ष् मोक्ष्, cl. 1. P. A. मोक्षति, -ते (more properly to be regarded as an anomalous Desid. fr. rt. 2. मुच्), to set free, liberate; to free one's self from or wish to do so (A.); cl. 10. P. (ep. also A.) मोक्षयति (-यते), -यितुम् (perhaps to be regarded as a Nom. fr. मोक्ष below), to free, set free, set at liberty, liberate, emancipate; to set free from (with abl.); to detach, extract; to loose, untie, undo; to wrest away, wrest from (with abl.); to shed, cause to flow; to cast, hurl, fling.
मोक्ष: मोक्ष, अस्, m. emancipation, deliverance, free-dom, liberation, escape, release; release from worldly existence, final emancipation, eternal bliss resulting from the soul's final liberation and its exemption from further transmigration; death; epithet of particular sacred hymns conducive to final emancipation; de-livery, discharge; the act of loosing, loosening, untying, unbinding, undoing, solving, (प्रश्न-म्°, the settling of a question); acquittance of an obli-gation; (in astronomy) the liberation of an obscured planet, end of an eclipse, the last contact or separa-tion of the eclipsed and eclipsing bodies; shedding, causing to flow; the act of discharging, casting, flinging, shooting; strewing, scattering; separating, falling off, falling down; a species of tree (= मुष्कक). —मोक्ष-काङ्क्षिन्, ई, इणी, इ, de-sirous of liberation or final emancipation. —मोक्ष-क्रिया-समाचार, अस्, आ, अम्, affording a method for effecting liberation. —मोक्ष-ज्ञान, अम्, n. knowledge of the beatitude attained through final emancipation. —मोक्ष-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha. —मोक्ष-दा, f., N. of a female ascetic. —मोक्ष-देव, अस्, m. an epithet applied to Hiouen-thsang. —मोक्ष-द्वार, अम्, n. ‘gate of emancipation,’ an epithet of the sun. —मोक्ष-धर्म, अस्, m. law or rule of emancipation. —मोक्षधर्म-पर्वन्, अ, n. ‘section relating to the law or rules of emancipation,’ N. of a section of the twelfth book of the Mahā-bhārata, from Adhyāya 174 to the end. —मोक्षधर्मार्थ-दीपिका (°म-अर्°), f., N. of a commentary on the preceding section of the Mahā-bhārata. —मोक्ष-पुरी, f. ‘city of emancipation,’ an epithet of the city of Kāñcī. —मोक्ष-भाज्, क्, क्, क्, receiving final emancipation. —मोक्ष-महा-परिषद्, त्, f. ‘great emancipation-assembly,’ the great Buddhist general council. —मोक्ष-मार्ग, अस्, m. ‘path of emancipation,’ N. of a Jaina work. —मोक्ष-लक्ष्मी-विलास, अस्, m., N. of a temple. —मोक्ष-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having final emancipation, con-nected with eternal bliss. —मोक्ष-विंशक, अम्, n. ‘twenty verses on emancipation,’ epithet of the verses Hari-vaṃśa 14348 sqq. —मोक्ष-शास्त्र, अम्, n. the doctrine of final emancipation. —मोक्ष-सा-धन, अम्, n. means of emancipation. —मोक्षान्-तरङ्-ग (°ष-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, nearest or next to final emancipation. —मोक्षोपाय (°ष-उप्°), अस्, m. means of emancipation; a sage, saint, de-votee (?).
मोक्षक: मोक्षक, अस्, इका, अम्, (at the end of a comp.) setting at liberty, freeing, delivering, emancipating; (अस्), m. a species of tree; one who looses or unties or sets free, a deliverer, liberator.
मोक्षण: मोक्षण, अस्, ई, अम्, liberating, emancipating; (अम्), n. the act of loosing, loosening; emancipa-tion, releasing, rescuing, setting at liberty, liberation; letting go, giving up, resigning, abandoning, desert-ing; squandering; shedding, causing to flow; [cf. रक्त-म्°।]
मोक्षणीय: मोक्षणीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be let go or liberated, to be given up or resigned, to be disregarded or neglected, (अ-मोक्षणीय, inevitable.)
मोक्षमाण: मोक्षमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, setting free, liberating.
मोक्षयत्: मोक्षयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, setting free, liberating.
मोक्षयितृ: मोक्षयितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who frees or libe-rates, a liberator, emancipator.
मोक्षाय: मोक्षाय, Nom. A. मोक्षायते, -यितुम्, to become emancipated, tend to emancipation.
मोक्षित: मोक्षित, अस्, आ, अम्, set free, let go, liberated, allowed to be at large.
मोक्षिन्: मोक्षिन्, ई, इणी, इ, striving after emancipation; emancipated, redeemed.
मोक्ष्य: मोक्ष्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be set free or liberated; to be saved.
मोग: मोग मोग, अस्, m. the chicken-pox or some similar disease.
मोघ: मोघ मोघ, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. 1. मुह्), vain, useless, aimless, fruitless, unprofitable, (अमो-घातिथि, a guest who does not come causelessly or uselessly); left, abandoned; idle; (अस्), m. an en-closure, hedge, fence; (आ), f. the trumpet flower, Bignonia Suaveolens; a species of plant, the seeds of which are used as a vermifuge, = विडङ्ग; (अम्), ind. in vain, uselessly. —मोघ-कर्मन्, आ, आ, अ, one whose actions are fruitless or unavailing, observing useless ceremonies. —मोघ-ज्ञान, अस्, आ, अम्, one whose knowledge is useless or unavailing, cultivating any but religious wisdom. —मोघ-ता, f. vainness, uselessness, aimlessness, erringness, (अ-मोघतया युतम् अस्त्रम्, a weapon endowed with unerring-ness, Kirātārj. VI. 40); idleness. —मोघ-पुष्पा, f. a barren woman. —मोघ-हासिन्, ई, इनी, इ, laugh-ing without any cause or occasion. —मोघाश (°घ-आश्°), अस्, आ, अम्, one whose hopes are vain. —मोघी-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, -कर्तुम्, to make vain, render useless, foil, frustrate, baffle, disappoint. —मोघी-भू, cl. 1. P. -भवति, -भवितुम्, to become useless or aimless, be foiled. —मोघी-भूत, अस्, आ, अम्, become useless, rendered vain, foiled.
मोघोलि: मोघोलि, इस्, m. an enclosure, hedge, fence; [cf. मोघ above.]
मोच: मोच मोच, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 2. मुच्), Mo-ringa Pterygosperma; (probably) the plantain tree, Musa Sapientum; (आ), f. Musa Sapientum (= क-दली, रम्भा); the cotton shrub; the indigo plant; (ई), f. Hingtscha Repens [cf. हिल-मोची]; (अम्), n. a plantain, banana (the fruit). —मोच-निर्यास or मो-च-रस or मोच-सार or मोच-स्राव, अस्, or मोच-स्रुत्, त्, m. the resin of Gossampinus Ramphii.
मोचक: मोचक, अस्, इका, अम् (fr. Caus. of rt. 2. मुच्), liberating, emancipating; (अस्), m. a liberator, one who has abandoned all worldly passion and desire, an ascetic, devotee; Moringa Pterygosperma; the plantain tree, Musa Sapientum; (इका), f. Musa Sapientum.
मोचन: मोचन, अस्, ई, अम्, releasing, freeing from; casting, darting; (ई), f. a species of plant, = कण्ट-कारी; (अम्), n. the act of releasing, liberating, liberation, emancipation, setting free, loosing, (ऋण-मोचन, the releasing from a debt, paying a debt for any one); the act of unyoking, unharnessing; letting loose, discharging, emitting. —मोचन-पट्-टक, ‘clearing-cloth,’ a filter.
मोचनीय: मोचनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be released or set free, to be let loose; to be resigned or given up.
मोचयितव्य: मोचयितव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be set free or re-leased, (sometimes with inst. of the thing from which there is release); capable of being set at liberty.
मोचयितृ: मोचयितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, freeing, setting free, re-leasing.
मोचयित्वा: मोचयित्वा, ind. having freed or loosed, having unharnessed.
मोचाट: मोचाट, अस्, m. the pith or heart of the banana tree; the fruit of the banana; a kind of pungent seed, Nigella Indica; sandal-wood.
मोचित: मोचित, अस्, आ, अम्, caused to be released, set at liberty, emancipated.
मोचिन्: मोचिन्, ई, इनी, इ, setting free, liberating.
मोच्य: मोच्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be set free or released; to be given up or restored.
मोचिक: मोचिक मोचिक, अस्, m. a leather manu-facturer, shoe-maker, &c.; [cf. Hindī موچي]
मोटक: मोटक मोटक, अस्, अम्, m. n. (fr. rt. मुट्), a globule, pill; मोटकं नेत्र-रोगाणाम्, a pill to be used as a remedy against ophthalmia; (अस्), m., N. of an author; (ई), f., N. of a Rāgiṇī; (अम्), n. a broken or crushed leaf.
मोटन: मोटन, अस्, ई, अम्, crushing, pressing, rubbing, grinding, tearing, destroying [cf. गज-म्°]; (अस्), m. wind, air; (अम्), n. the act of crushing, breaking, grinding, strangling, (गल-मोटन, wringing the neck); [cf. अङ्गुलि-म्°।]
मोटनक: मोटनक, अम्, n. crushing, entire destruction; a kind of metre, four times ¯¯˘˘¯˘˘¯˘˘¯.
मोटि: मोटि मोटि in कर्ण-म्°, q. v.
मोट्टायित: मोट्टायित मोट्टायित, अम्, n. showing affec-tion in the absence of a loved object by various ways of recalling him to mind, the silent expression of returned affection, (one of the ten Bhāvas or proper-ties of women.)
मोढ: मोढ मोढ, अस्, m., N. of a family.
मोढक: मोढक, अस्, m. a proper N.
मोण: मोण मोण, अस्, m. dried fruit; a kind of fly (= नक्र-मक्षिका); a basket in which snakes are carried.
मोणक: मोणक, a word used to explain डिम्बिका।
मोतीराम: मोतीराम मोतीराम, अस्, m., N. of a son of Kānada.
मोद: मोद मोद, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 2. मुद्), pleasure, delight, gladness, joyousness, joyfulness; fragrance, perfume [cf. आ-मोद]; N. of a Muni; (आ), f. = अज-मोदा, q. v. —मोद-कर, अस्, m., N. of a Muni. —मोद-मोदिनी, f. ‘delighting by fragrance,’ Eugenia Jambolana (= जम्बु). —मोदाख्य (°द-आख्°), अस्, m. the mango tree. —मोदा-गिरि, इस्, m., N. of a country. —मोदाढ्या (°द-आढ्°), f. = अज-मोदा, q. v. —मोदा-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a city.
मोदक: मोदक, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, delighting, rejoicing, pleasing, gladdening, exhilarating, causing happiness or delight; glad, cheerful; (अस्, अम्), m. n. a small round sweetmeat or a sweetmeat in general; (in medicine) a sort of pill; (अस्), m. a particular mixed caste (the son of a Kṣatriya by a Śūdra mother); (अम्), n. a kind of metre, four times ¯˘˘¯˘˘¯ ˘˘¯˘˘¯; (ई), f., N. of a particular mythical club or weapon. —मोदक-कार, अस्, m. a sweetmeat-maker, confectioner. —मोदक-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, composed of sweetmeats. —मोदक-शराव, अस्, अम्, m. n. a dish of sweetmeats.
मोदकिका: मोदकिका, f. (at the end of a comp. after nu-merals), a sweetmeat.
मोदन: मोदन, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. the Caus.), giving joy, gratifying, gladdening, delighting, (generally at the end of a comp., e. g. क्रव्याद-गण-मोदन, giving joy to numbers of beasts of prey, Mahā-bh. Droṇa-p. 1576); (अम्), n. the act of pleasing or affording pleasure; joy, pleasure; = उच्छिष्ट-मो-दन, wax.
मोदनीय: मोदनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be rejoiced at, to be delighted in, delightful.
मोदमान: मोदमान, अस्, आ, अम्, rejoicing, being glad.
मोदयत्: मोदयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, rejoicing, delighting; (अन्ती), f. a sort of wild lovage, Ptychotis Ajowan; Arabian jasmine.
मोदाकिन्: मोदाकिन्, ई, m. (probably) N. of a hill (Mahā-bh. Bhīṣma-p. 427).
मोदायनि: मोदायनि, इस्, m. a patronymic from Moda.
मोदित: मोदित, अस्, आ, अम्, pleased, gratified, delighted; (अम्), n. pleasure, delight.
मोदिन्: मोदिन्, ई, इनी, इ, rejoicing, glad, pleased, cheerful, merry, happy; making glad, gladdening, gratifying, delighting, (often at the end of comps., cf. गीत-म्°); (इनी), f., N. of various plants (= अज-मोदा, मल्-लिका, यूथिका, वृत्त-मल्लिका); musk; an intoxi-cating beverage.
मोदोष: मोदोष, अस्, m., N. of a preceptor.
मोमुघ: मोमुघ मोमुघ, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. Intens. of rt. 1. मुह्), very much perplexed, greatly embar-rassed; mad, insane.
मोरट: मोरट मोरट, अस्, m. a species of plant with sweet juice (= क्षीर-मोरट); the milk of a cow recently calved, biestings, (according to lexico-graphers, अम्, n.); (आ), f. = मूर्वा, hemp used for bow-strings, Sanseviera Roxburghiana; (अम्), n. the root of the sugar-cane; the flower of Alangium Hexapetalum; the root of this plant.

(fr. rt. 2. मुष्), a robber, thief, plunderer; robbery, theft, stealing; plundering, sacking, (नगर-मोष, plundering a city); anything robbed or stolen, stolen property. —मोष-कृत्, त्, त्, त्, one who practises theft, a thief. —मोषाभिदर्शन (°ष-अभ्°), अम्, n. seeing or witnessing a robbery.

मोह: मोह मोह, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 1. मुह्), uncon-sciousness, loss of consciousness, fainting, a swoon; delusion, bewilderment, perplexity, distraction, phrenzy; weakness of intellect, ignorance, folly, foolishness, infatuation; error, mistake, going astray; pain, affliction; wonder, amazement, astonishment; Infatuation (personified as the offspring of Brahmā); (in phil.) darkness or delusion of mind preventing the discernment of truth (leading men to believe in the reality of worldly objects and to addict themselves to mundane or sensual enjoyment); a magical art employed to bewilder an enemy (= मोहन); मो-हात्, ind. through ignorance, from folly or infatuation. —मोह-कलिल, अम्, n. a thicket or snare of illu-sion. —मोह-चूडोत्तर (°ड-उत्°), अम्, n., N. of a work. —मोह-जाल, अम्, n. the net of delusion, the snare or fetters of illusory objects, the fascination of the world. —मोह-निद्रा, f. ‘sleep of infatua-tion,’ thoughtless assurance, overweening confidence. —मोह-पाश, अस्, m. the snare of (wordly) illu-sion. —मोह-मन्त्र, अस्, m. an infatuating spell, deluding charm. —मोह-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, consist-ing of infatuation, leading to delusion, perplexing. —मोह-मुद्गर, अस्, m. ‘hammer of ignorance or infatuation,’ N. of a metrical exposition of the Vedānta philosophy; of another work. —मोह-रात्रि, इस्, f. ‘night of bewilderment,’ the night when the world is to be destroyed. —मोह-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, possessed of infatuation, infatuated, foolish, igno-rant. —मोह-शास्त्र, अम्, n. erroneous or false teaching, false doctrine. —मोह-शूलोत्तर (°ल-उत्°), अम्, n., N. of a work. —मोहोपमा (°ह-उप्°), f. ‘error-comparison,’ a rhetorical figure in which there is a confusion of the subject and object of a comparison (e. g. ‘regarding thy face, O dear one, as the moon, I run after the moon as if it were thy face’).
मोहक: मोहक, अस्, इका, अम्, bewildering, confusing, infatuating, causing ignorance or folly.
मोहन: मोहन, अस्, ई, अम्, stupefying, depriving of con-sciousness or sensation, bewildering, perplexing, puzzling, confusing, deceiving, deluding, leading astray, infatuating, fascinating; (अस्), m. the thorn-apple; epithet of Śiva; N. of one of the five arrows of Kāma-deva, the god of love; (आ), f. the flower of a sort of jasmine; a sort of grass, Trigonella Cor-niculata; (ई), f. मोहनीय: मोहनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, relating to delusion, de-pending on illusion or error, resulting from infatua-tion, producing delusion; perplexing, puzzling, con-fusing.
मोहयत्: मोहयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत् (fr. the Caus.) stupefying, bewildering, depriving of sense.
मोहयितृ: मोहयितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who perplexes or deludes, a perplexer, infatuator.
मोहित: मोहित, अस्, आ, अम्, stupefied, perplexed, bewil-dered, infatuated, deluded, beguiled, fascinated, (often in comps., e. g. काम-मोहित, infatuated by love.)
मोहिन्: मोहिन्, ई, इनी, इ, stupefying, confusing, puzzling, perplexing, illusive, fallacious, beguiling, alluring, fascinating; (इनी), f. a fascinating woman; N. of an Apsaras; the flower of a species of jasmine.
मोहुक: मोहुक, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. being deluded, falling into error or confusion, going astray.

मौकुन्द: मौकुन्द मौकुन्द, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to Mukunda, i. e. Viṣṇu.

मौघ्य: मौघ्य मौघ्य, अम्, n. (fr. मोघ), vain-ness, uselessness.

मौञ्ज: मौञ्ज मौञ्ज, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मुञ्ज), made of Muñja grass or its fibres; resembling Muñja grass; (अस्), m. a blade of Muñja grass; (ई), f., scil. मे-खला, a Brāhman's girdle or cord made of a triple string of Muñja grass; any girdle. —मौञ्जी-तृणा-ख्य (°ण-आख्°), अस्, m. मौदकिक: मौदकिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मोदक), consisting or composed of sweetmeats; (अस्), m. a seller of sweetmeats, confectioner.

मौदनेयक: मौदनेयक, see Gaṇa Kattryādi to Pāṇ. IV. 2, 95.

मौदाकिन्: मौदाकिन्, a various reading for मोदाकिन्।

मौलि: मौलि, इस्, m. (probably fr. मूल), the head, the top of anything; the plant Jonesia Asoka; a patro-nymic; (अयस्), m. pl., N. of a tribe; (इस्), m. f. a diadem [cf. मुकुट], crown, crest; a tuft or lock of hair left on the crown of the head after tonsure, a top-knot (= चूडा); hair ornamented and braided round the head, = धम्मिल; (इस्), f. the earth, (in this sense according to some मौली, f.) —मौलि-मणि, इस्, m. f. a crest gem, jewel worn in a diadem. —मौलि-मण्डन, अम्, n. an ornament for the head. —मौलि-माला or मौलि-मालिका, f. a wreath or crown worn on the head. —मौलि-मालिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having a wreath or crown on the top of the head; उदयाचल-मौलिमालिन्, having the eastern moun-tain for its crest (said of the sun). —मौलि-मुकुट, अम्, n. a diadem for the head, tiara; [cf. मुकुट।] —मौलि-रत्न, अम्, n. a crest jewel, crown jewel, head jewel. —मौल्य्-आभरण, अम्, n. a head ornament.
मौलिक: मौलिक, अस्, ई, अम्, producing roots, &c.; coming from or belonging to the root, radical, original [cf. मूलिक]; chief, principal, being of low origin, (op-posed to कुलीन); inferior; (अस्), m. a digger of roots, a dealer in roots; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people.
मौलिक्य: मौलिक्य, अम्, n. an abstract noun from मूलिक, see Gaṇa Purohitādi to Pāṇ. V. 1, 128.
मौलिन्: मौलिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having a diadem or crown, diademed, crested; having at the top, (sometimes at the end of a comp., e. g. चक्र-मौली शकटः, a cart having the wheels uppermost.)
मौलेय: मौलेय, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people.
मौल्य: मौल्य, अस्, -ली, अम्, being at the root; (अम्), n. price, (for मूल्य।)
मौशल: मौशल मौशल, मौषल, &c., incorrectly for मौसल below.
मौषिकि: मौषिकि मौषिकि, इस्, m. a metronymic from Mūṣikā.
मौषिकीपुत्र: मौषिकी-पुत्र, अस्, m., N. of a preceptor.
मौष्टा: मौष्टा मौष्टा, f. (fr. मुष्टि), a combat with fists, boxing match, sparring, playing at fisticuffs.
मौष्टिक: मौष्टिक, अस्, m. a cheat, impostor, rogue, sharper.
मौसल: मौसल मौसल, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मुसल), club-shaped, club-formed; relating to the battle with clubs, (मौसलम् पर्व = मौसल-पर्वन् be-low); fought with clubs (as a battle); an epithet of a Madhu-parka (composed of ghee and spirituous liquor); (आस्), m. pl. of मौसल्य below. —मौ-सल-पर्वन्, अ, n. ‘Musala-section,’ N. of the six-teenth book of the Mahā-bhārata (in which is de-scribed the death of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma and the self-destruction of Kṛṣṇa's family through the curse of some Brāhmans; it is narrated that in consequence of this curse, the Andhakas and Yādavas indulged in intoxicating liquors which led to a general quarrel in which the infuriated relatives, having no weapons, plucked the rushes [एरका], and with these, turned to clubs by the working of the curse, slaughtered each other).
मौसल्य: मौसल्य, अस्, m. a patronymic from Musala.
मौसुल: मौसुल मौसुल, अस्, m. a Moslim, Mussul-mān, Muhammedan.
मौहूर्त: मौहूर्त मौहूर्त, अस्, m. (fr. मुहूर्त), an astrologer.
मौहूर्तिक: मौहूर्तिक, अस्, ई, अम्, lasting for a moment or instant, momentary; relating to a particular time; (अस्), m. an astrologer; N. of a class of celestial beings (children of Muhūrtā).
म्न: म्न म्न in चर्म-म्न, q. v.
म्ना: म्ना म्ना (connected with rt. मन्, with which म्ना was originally identical), cl. 1. P. मनति, मम्नौ, म्नास्यति, अम्नासीत्, म्ना-यात् or म्नेयात्, म्नातुम्, to bind or fix in the mind, repeat over in the mind, fix in the memory by frequent repetition, repeat; to study or learn diligently; to remember; to celebrate, praise (Ved.): Pass. म्नायते: Caus. म्नापयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अमिम्नपत्: Desid. मिम्नासति: Intens. माम्ना-यते, माम्नाति, माम्नेति; [for comparisons see under rt. मन्।]
म्नात: म्नात, अस्, आ, अम्, fixed in the mind, repeated, learnt, remembered; [cf. आ-म्°, समा-म्°।]
म्यक्ष्: म्यक्ष् म्यक्ष् (a Vedic verb, of which the following forms are found, म्यक्षति, मिम्यक्ष, मिमिक्षतुस्, मिमिक्षुस्, मिमिक्षिरे, अम्यक्, मिमिक्षत्), to be fixed in or on; to be in any place or state; to be near, to be present, to be at hand; to go to, reach; to be associated or united; (Sāy. = प्राप्नोति, सङ्गच्छते, संहतो भ-वति।)
म्रक्ष्: म्रक्ष् म्रक्ष् or मृक्ष् (connected with rts. 1. मृज्, मक्ष्), cl. 1. P. म्रक्-षति, मृक्षति, &c., to accumulate, collect, as-semble; to rub; cl. 10. P. म्रक्षयति, मृक्ष-यति, &c., to accumulate, collect; to combine, mix; to rub, smear, anoint; to speak indistinctly or incor-rectly; (according to some) to divide, cut.
म्रक्ष: म्रक्ष, अस्, आ, अम्, rubbing, destroying, (in तुवि-म्°, q. v.); (अस्), m. concealment of one's vices or failings, hypocrisy, slyness. —म्रक्ष-कृत्वन्, आ, अरी, अ, Ved. rubbing to pieces, destroying (said of Indra; Sāy. = वध-कर्तृ).
म्रक्षण: म्रक्षण, अम्, n. the act of rubbing in or on, anointing, smearing the body with unguents; any-thing to be rubbed on, ointment, oil.
म्रद्: म्रद् म्रद् (another form of rt. 1. मृद्, q. v.), cl. 1. A. म्रदते, मम्रदे, म्र-दितुम्, to rub; to grind, pound, reduce to powder; to tread or trample on: Caus. म्रदयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अमम्रदत्: Desid. मिम्रदिषते: Intens. माम्रद्यते, माम्रत्ति।
म्रद: म्रद, म्रदस्, in ऊर्ण-म्रद, ऊर्ण-म्र-दस्, q. q. v. v.
म्रदय: म्रदय म्रदय (fr. मृदु), Nom. P. म्र-दयति, -यितुम्, Ved. to make soft or smooth; to polish.
म्रदिमन्: म्रदिमन्, आ, m. softness, tenderness, mildness, gentleness. —म्रदिमान्वित (°म-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, endowed with softness, soft, mild, kind.
म्रदिष्ठ: म्रदिष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम् (superl. of मृदु), very soft, exceedingly mild, softest.
म्रदीयस्: म्रदीयस्, आन्, असी, अस् (compar. of मृदु), softer, milder.
म्रातन: म्रातन म्रातन, अम्, n. Cyperus Rotundus.
म्रित्: म्रित् म्रित् [cf. rt. मृ], cl. 4. P. म्रित्यति, Ved. to decay, moulder away, be dissolved.
म्रुच्: म्रुच् म्रुच् [cf. rts. म्रुञ्च्, म्लुच्], cl. 1. P. म्रोचति, Aor. अम्रुचत् or अम्रोचीत्, &c., to go, move: Desid. मुम्रुचिषति, मुम्रो-चिषति।
म्रोक: म्रोक, अस्, m., N. of a destructive Agni (men-tioned in Atharva-veda V. 31, 9); of a flame.
म्रुञ्च्: म्रुञ्च् म्रुञ्च्, cl. 1. P. म्रुञ्चति, &c., = rt. म्रुच् above.
म्रेट्: म्रेट् म्रेट् or म्रेड् (= rts. मेट्, म्लेट्), cl. 1. P. म्रेटति, म्रेडति, to be mad.
म्लक्त: म्लक्त म्लक्त (?), अस्, आ, अम्, stolen.
म्लक्ष्: म्लक्ष् म्लक्ष्, cl. 10. P. म्लक्षयति, to cut, divide.
म्लात: म्लात म्लात, म्लान, म्लायिन्, म्लास्नु। See col. 3.
म्लात, अस्, आ, अम्, faded, withered; made white by tanning (said of leather).
म्लिलष्ट: म्लिलष्ट म्लिष्ट, &c. See under rt. म्लेछ् below.
म्लुच्: म्लुच् म्लुच् [cf. rt. म्रुच्], cl. 1. P. म्लोचति, Aor. अम्लुचत् or अम्लोचीत्, &c., to go; to go down: Desid. मुम्लुचिषति, मुम्लोचिषति।
म्लुक्त: म्लुक्त in अप-म्लुक्त, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. retired, withdrawn, concealed, hidden.
म्लुञ्च्: म्लुञ्च् म्लुञ्च्, cl. 1. P. म्लुञ्चति, &c., = rt. म्लुच् above.
म्लुप्: म्लुप् म्लुप्, another form of rt. म्लुच् above.
म्लुप्त: म्लुप्त in उप-म्लुप्त, अस्, आ, अम्, retired, with-drawn, concealed, hidden.
म्लेच्छ्: म्लेछ् म्लेछ्, cl. 1. P. म्लेच्छति, मिम्लेच्-छ, म्लेच्छितुम्, cl. 10. P. म्लेच्छ-यति, -यितुम्, to speak confusedly or barbarously; to talk an unintelligible or foreign language, to speak a provincial or barbarous dialect.
म्लेछ्: म्लेछ् म्लेछ्, cl. 1. P. म्लेच्छति, मिम्लेच्-छ, म्लेच्छितुम्, cl. 10. P. म्लेच्छ-यति, -यितुम्, to speak confusedly or barbarously; to talk an unintelligible or foreign language, to speak a provincial or barbarous dialect.
म्लिष्ट: म्लिष्ट, अस्, आ, अम् [cf. Pāṇ. VII. 2, 18], spoken barbarously or indistinctly, indistinct (as speech), foreign, barbarous; = म्लान, withered, faded, faint; (अम्), n. indistinct speech, a foreign language. —म्लिष्टोक्ति (°ट-उक्°), इस्, f. indistinct or bar-barous speech.
म्लेच्छ: म्लेच्छ, अस्, m. a foreigner, barbarian, non-Arian, man of an outcast race, (a generic term for a person speaking any language but Sanskrit and not conform-ing to the usual Hindū institutions); a wicked or bad man, sinner; foreign or barbarous speech, igno-rance of the language of the country; (अम्), n. copper. —म्लेच्छ-कन्द, अस्, m. ‘foreign-root,’ Allium Ascalonicum, garlic. —म्लेच्छ-जाति, इस्, m. a man belonging to one of the Mleccha or barbarian races, a barbarian, savage, mountaineer (as a Kirāta, Śa-vara, Pulinda). —म्लेच्छ-देश, अस्, m. a foreign or barbarous country, any country inhabited by people of a language and institutions different from the Hindūs. —म्लेच्छ-निवह, अस्, m. a host or swarm of barbarians. —म्लेच्छ-भाषा, f. a foreign or barbarous language. —म्लेच्छ-भोजन, अस्, m. ‘food of foreigners or barbarians,’ wheat; (अम्), n. = यावक, half-ripe barley. —म्लेच्छ-मण्डल, अम्, n. the country of the Mlecchas or barbarians. —म्लेच्छ-मुख, अम्, n. ‘foreign countenance,’ copper (see म्लेच्छास्य). —म्लेच्छ-वाच्, क्, क्, क्, speaking a barbarous or foreign language, speaking the language of the Mlecchas, (opposed to आर्य-वाच्, speaking the language of the Āryas, Manu X. 45.) —म्लेच्छाख्य (°छ-आख्°), अम्, n. ‘called Mlec-cha,’ copper. —म्लेच्छाश (°छ-आश°), अस्, m. ‘food of barbarians,’ wheat; [cf. म्लेच्छ-भोजन।] —म्लेच्छास्य (°छ-आस्°), अम्, n. ‘barbarian-face,’ copper, (so named because the complexion of the Greek and Muhammedan invaders of India was sup-posed to be copper-coloured; cf. म्लेच्छाख्य।)
म्लेच्छन: म्लेच्छन, अम्, n. the act of speaking unintel-ligibly or confusedly; speaking in a foreign or bar-barous tongue.
म्लेच्छित: म्लेच्छित, अस्, आ, अम्, spoken barbarously or un-intelligibly, foreign, barbarian; (अम्), n. a foreign tongue, ungrammatical speech.
म्लेच्छितक: म्लेच्छितक, अम्, n. the speaking in a language unintelligible to others, foreign speech.
म्लेट्: म्लेट् म्लेट् or म्लेड् (= rt. म्रेट्), cl. 1. P. म्लेटति, म्लेडति, &c., to be mad.
म्लेव्: म्लेव् म्लेव् [cf. rt. मेव्], cl. 1. A. म्ले-वते, &c., to serve, worship, gratify by service.
म्लै: म्लै म्लै, cl. 1. P. म्लायति (ep. also A. म्लायते, and cl. 2. P. म्लाति, म्लान्ति), मम्लौ (मम्ले), म्लास्यति, अम्लासीत्, म्लायात् or म्लेयात्, म्लातुम्, to wither, fade, decay; to be faint or languid, grow weary, languish; to become weak or feeble; to become thin or emaciated; to be dispirited or downcast; to be sad: Caus. म्लाप-यति, -यितुम्, to cause to wither or fade; to enfeeble, make languid or dispirited, emaciate; [cf. Gr. βλάπτω = Caus. म्लापयति, μῶλυς, μωλυρύς.]
म्लान: म्लान, अस्, आ, अम्, withered, faded; wearied, weary, wan; languid, languishing; enfeebled, ema-ciated, faint, feeble, weak; dispirited, dejected, sad, downcast, melancholy; foul, dirty [cf. मल]; black, dark-coloured; (अम्), n. a withered or faded state, withering, fading; absence of brightness or lustre. —म्लान-क्षीण, अस्, आ, अम्, withered and lan-guishing. —म्लान-ता, f. witheredness, the state of being faded; the being out of spirits; lassitude, languor. —म्लान-मनस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, depressed in mind, dispirited. —म्लान-वक्त्र, अस्, आ, अम्, hav-ing a downcast countenance. —म्लान-स्रज्, क्, क्, क्, having a withered or faded garland. —म्लानाङ्ग (°न-अङ्°), अस्, ई, अम्, having enfeebled limbs, weak-bodied; (ई), f. a woman during the menses. —म्ला-नेन्द्रिय (°न-इन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having enfeebled senses.
म्लानि: म्लानि, इस्, f. withering, fading, decay; languor, faintness, lassitude, weariness, emaciation; growing thin; dejection, sadness; foulness, filth.
म्लायत्: म्लायत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, fading, withering; lan-guishing. —म्लायद्-वक्त्र, अस्, आ, अम्, having a haggard or sorrowful face, having an emaciated appearance.
म्लायमान: म्लायमान, अस्, आ, अम्, fading, withering, lan-guishing.
म्लायिन्: म्लायिन्, ई, इनी, इ, becoming faded or withered; growing thin or emaciated.
म्लास्नु: म्लास्नु, उस्, उस्, उ, becoming faded or withered; growing thin or emaciated.
महल्लिका: महल्लिका, f. a female attendant in the women's apartments.
महाक्षौहिणी: महाक्षौहिणी (°हा-अक्°), f. a thousand million billions.
मिताक्षरासिद्धान्तसङ्ग्रह: मिताक्षरा-सिद्धान्त-सङ्ग्रह; transfer ‘(अस्, आ, अम्), speaking with caution &c.,’ to मितार्थ-भाषिन्।
